causal_chain.bug_semantics: During ZIP extraction, a local attacker who can mutate the extraction directory can replace an already-validated parent directory with a symlink before the destination pathname is opened. The path-based write then follows the rebound parent and creates or truncates a file outside the extraction root with the OpenClaw process's privileges.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The first shared ZIP extractor performed only a lexical path.resolve/string-prefix boundary check, then separately awaited mkdir and ZIP decoding before calling fs.writeFile(outPath, data). It never bound validation to the identity of the parent directory or opened output file, creating the parent-symlink TOCTOU window at the extractor's inception.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The Zalo webhook router matched a registered route using the normalized URL pathname, but unauthenticated failure accounting used the raw req.url, including its query string, as part of the key in a process-global Map with no maximum size or expiry. An attacker could repeatedly POST to the same reachable valid webhook path with an invalid or missing secret while varying ?nonce=..., causing every 401 to create and retain a distinct webhookStatusCounters entry and eventually exert memory pressure or trigger OOM. The similarly raw-URL-keyed rate-limit map was also unbounded, although that path ran only after successful target authentication; the unauthenticated advisory path is the 401 status-counter insertion.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit a23e0d5140e5126f5055a46824cae4ba0a097ba3 added Zalo webhook ingress hardening, including anomaly accounting and rate limiting. In extensions/zalo/src/monitor.ts it introduced webhookStatusCounters as an unbounded Map, recordWebhookStatus() as an unconditional insertion for security error statuses, and calls that passed req.url for pre-authentication 401 responses. This composed a normalized route match with attacker-controlled raw-URL keying and unbounded retention; later commit 453664f09d0911cc1829d22c63f664f0ad2c8c10 only moved the already-vulnerable logic into monitor.webhook.ts.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The Git node accepted an attacker-selected local repository and ran push/pushTags while Git's file transport remained permitted. An authenticated workflow author could stage repository metadata whose configured local target was a crafted repository containing receive hooks; the local git-receive-pack path then executed those hooks as the n8n process. The later default core.hooksPath=/dev/null mitigation covered hooks for the invoking repository but did not make a write to an attacker-controlled local target safe. The fix validates configured remotes and, when hooks are disabled, removes file from GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL specifically for push and pushTags.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The first Git node implementation trusted repository-controlled local configuration and destination selection: it constructed simple-git with a workflow-supplied baseDirectory and exposed git.push() without restricting local remote targets or the file transport. This crossed a trust boundary from an authenticated workflow into Git's executable receive-hook behavior.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: When the normal Whirlpool import fails, openssl_encrypt searches sysconfig, user, and Flatpak site-packages with broad whirlpool*.so, pywhirlpool*.so, whirlpool-py311*.so, whirlpool*.pyd, and pywhirlpool*.pyd globs; it then chooses a matching candidate, creates an import-name symlink (or copies it on Windows), and imports the native extension. The vulnerable implementation authenticated neither the candidate's identity nor its integrity, ownership, or permissions, so an attacker able to place a matching native module in a searched location (or make a matching symlink there) could have attacker-controlled native code loaded during Whirlpool setup/use.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: cb07e5f88a98f4459a5f828142e740c024810692 first added openssl_encrypt/modules/setup_whirlpool.py with the broad native-module discovery, first-match/fallback selection, symlink-or-copy, and subsequent import chain, and wired setup_whirlpool() into openssl_encrypt/modules/crypt_core.py and post-install handling. Later formatting and Flatpak-path commits preserved that mechanism; the later hash-registry implementation was an additional carrier, not the origin of the already-live flaw.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Repo.clone() and Repo.clone_from() converted caller-supplied separate_git_dir/separate-git-dir input into git clone --separate-git-dir=<path> and executed it while allow_unsafe_options remained false. Because --separate-git-dir redirects the complete Git metadata directory, an attacker whose input is forwarded as a clone option can make Git create repository metadata outside the intended clone destination; the clone safety denylist omitted this option and therefore raised no UnsafeOptionError.

The contemporaneous command wrapper rendered separate_git_dir as --separate-git-dir=<value>, so this was the first affected public clone API and the first commit whose default clone path could honor an attacker-controlled external metadata directory. Later commit b425301ad16f265157abdaf47f7af1c1ea879068 added clone_from() on the same _clone path, and later safety-denylist commits e6108c7997f5c8f7361b982959518e982b973230 and 5c59e0d63da6180db8a0b349f0ad36fef42aceed preserved the original flaw by omitting --separate-git-dir.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: PluginImportGuard.restore_hidden_modules() restored saved entries, cleared self.hidden_modules, and only then evaluated len(self.hidden_modules), so every restoration audit message reported zero regardless of the number restored. In setup, hide_dangerous_modules() deleted blocked modules from the process-global sys.modules before sys.meta_path.insert(0, import_guard) installed the blocking finder; a thread scheduled between those two operations could re-import a deleted blocked module and retain access to it, bypassing the intended sandbox in a multi-threaded process.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: IndexFile.from_tree accepted one to three caller-controlled treeish values, appended them after GitPython's own --index-output=<temporary-index> argument, and passed the resulting argv to git read-tree without rejecting option-shaped treeish values or inserting --. causal_chain.bug_semantics: When a plugin lacked READ_FILES, PluginSandbox attempted to confine filesystem access by replacing only builtins.open with restricted_open. pathlib.Path.open/read_text/read_bytes/write_text/write_bytes and io.open retained independent file-opening paths, and pathlib/io were available to plugin code, so an untrusted plugin could read or modify paths outside the sandbox's allowed directories without passing _is_safe_path.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef created the plugin sandbox and first implemented _restrict_file_operations as a single-name monkey patch: it assigned builtins.open = restricted_open but did not interpose io.open or pathlib.Path methods. The same commit advertised a zero-trust security sandbox, made this incomplete hook the READ_FILES enforcement boundary, and therefore originated the bypass rather than merely moving or refactoring existing vulnerable code.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A malicious repository can put traversal components in a .gitmodules section name. GitPython parses that attacker-controlled section name without validation, assigns it to Submodule._name, and during Submodule.update(init=True) uses it to form <parent git dir>/modules/<name>. The resulting escaped path is passed to directory and clone operations, so initialization creates an attacker-controlled Git repository outside the intended clone directory.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc introduced _module_abspath() with os.path.join(parent_repo.git_dir, 'modules', name) and changed the initialization branch of Submodule.update() from the tree-backed submodule path to this unchecked name-derived path before Repo.clone_from(). That is the first causal connection between an untrusted .gitmodules name and the filesystem repository-creation sink; the pre-existing unchecked sm_name() parser alone did not create this attack path.

evidence: The first-party advisory https://github.com/gitpython-developers/GitPython/security/advisories/GHSA-hmq2-w58f-27jc states that <=3.1.57 is affected and >=3.1.58 is patched. It identifies the flow sm_name(section) -> Submodule.iter_items() assigning sm._name -> _module_abspath() joining parent_repo.git_dir/modules/name -> clone/filesystem operations, and documents a released-3.1.57 PoC that creates /tmp/gitpython_poc_escaped_root/modules_dir while core Git rejects the suspicious name.

At 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc, git/objects/submodule/util.py sm_name() returns section[11:-1] unchecked; git/objects/submodule/base.py iter_items() reads n = sm_name(sms) and assigns sm._name = n. The same commit adds _module_abspath() at then-lines 204-210, whose Git-file branch returns os.path.join(parent_repo.git_dir, 'modules', name).

The 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc diff changes the Submodule.update() initialization branch from module_path = join_path_native(self.repo.working_tree_dir, self.path) to module_path = self._module_abspath(self.repo, self.path, self.name), after which Repo.clone_from(self.url, module_path, n=True) creates the repository. The path value in the parent was constrained by the required pc.tree[path] lookup; the newly used section name was not validated.

Immediate-parent tree verification: git rev-parse 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc^ returns a9a5414300a245b6e93ea4f39fbca792c3ec753f. git grep on that exact parent tree finds neither _module_abspath nor a git_dir/modules/name join. Direct inspection of the parent update branch shows only join_path_native(self.repo.working_tree_dir, self.path) feeding Repo.clone_from(). The BIC tree contains _module_abspath at base.py:204, the unchecked join at :206, and update's call at :422.

git log -L over _module_abspath traces the function through formatting/type-only edits to its zero-line addition in 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc. The next commit 67680a0877f01177dc827beb49c83a9174cdb736 extracts the same behavior into _clone_repo() and is therefore a refactor, not the BIC; the vulnerable update-to-clone path already exists in 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc.

Release boundary: git for-each-ref --contains identifies 0.3.6 as the earliest release tag containing the BIC. Peeled tag commits are 0.3.5=a2d39529eea4d0ecfcd65a2d245284174cd2e0aa (does not contain the BIC) and 0.3.6=4df4159413a4bf30a891f21cd69202e8746c8fea (does contain it). causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated n8n member could preserve attacker-controlled responseText containing script while making the Form node's expression-evaluated respondWith resolve to redirect. renderFormCompletion loaded responseText regardless of the selected response mode, omitted the sandbox Content-Security-Policy whenever respondWith was redirect, and passed both values to a Handlebars completion template that preferred responseText and emitted it with triple braces. A visitor submitting the public form therefore received the attacker's raw HTML without the sandbox and the script executed from the n8n origin with the visitor's session context.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The mechanism was assembled in two steps. Commit 7ea920dbe742c0ca7c79c9df749aa7d7c898c571 intentionally stopped sanitizing responseText but simultaneously installed an unconditional sandbox CSP, so it did not yet create the advisory's same-origin execution path. Commit 7f651ca5a3162ba0f13242dc934047e32998b33c then made that CSP conditional on respondWith not being redirect while leaving responseText loaded and rendered independently of respondWith. That guard removal is the smallest commit that completed the vulnerable combination.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The unified FastAPI server enabled both JWT-protected modules by default while supplying public, hardcoded 39-character HS256 signing secrets for each module. Startup validation checked only that each secret was at least 32 characters and that the two values differed, so both defaults passed. Because TokenAuth.verify_token() trusted any correctly signed token with the module issuer and the route dependencies returned the attacker-controlled sub claim without requiring that client_id to exist, anyone knowing the source could forge a bearer token for an arbitrary client_id and reach authenticated keyserver upload/revocation and telemetry event APIs.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The authenticated workflow-controlled Edit Image Draw Text operation word-wraps its text parameter and passes the resulting string to gm.drawText(). gm 1.23.1 constructs a quoted GraphicsMagick MVG -draw argument and escapes double quotes, but it does not escape backslashes already supplied by the caller. An attacker can place a backslash immediately before a quote so gm's added backslash is itself escaped, closing the intended MVG text primitive and allowing a following attacker-selected MVG primitive to make a blind outbound request or open a local file.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The vulnerable data flow is already present in the repository's parentless public root snapshot 9cb9804eeec1576d935817ecda6bd345480b97fa: packages/nodes-base/nodes/EditImage.node.ts reads the text node parameter, builds renderText with lines.join('\n'), and sends it directly to gmInstance.drawText(), while packages/nodes-base/package.json declares gm ^1.23.1. That root is a 257-file, 42,436-line initial import rather than the smallest source commit, and no pre-root public commit/member history exists from which to identify the commit that actually authored the flawed mechanism.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: search_files checked the literal user-supplied glob for a slash-delimited '..' segment before calling fast-glob, but did not validate the paths produced by glob expansion. A pattern such as '{a,..}/SECRET.txt' contains no literal '..' segment, passes the check, and can expand to '../SECRET.txt'; the tool then joined that result to the resolved working directory and either returned the outside filename or read matching lines from the outside file, disclosing files readable by the n8n OS user.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: PR #30670 replaced the parent implementation's bounded readdir-based collectFiles traversal with fastGlob(name, { cwd: resolvedDir }) and added only assertPatternStaysInside(name). The new pre-expansion lexical check rejected explicit absolute paths and literal '..' segments, but the result path was consumed by path.join(resolvedDir, fp) without post-expansion canonicalization or containment checking. That change first created the advisory's path-confinement bypass.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: CredentialsPermissionChecker builds the set of credential IDs to authorize by filtering node.credentials against credential-type names inferred statically from unresolved node parameters. For an HTTP Request node, an attacker with edit access to a shared workflow can put another user's known credential ID under its real credential type while setting genericAuthType to an expression. The pre-execution checker sees the expression source string rather than the runtime-resolved type, so the real credential key is omitted from the authorization query; execution later resolves the expression and loads/uses that credential, enabling unauthorized use or exfiltration.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The smallest causal change is PR member commit 7d6023fe3478df86d88f3602f1ea5b53819a050b. It changed mapCredIdsToNodes from checking every referenced credential to skipping any credential whose key is not in getActiveCredentialTypes, and its new static inference handled nodeCredentialType but not dynamically selected generic credential types. Squash landing 608e3bf214328e679c03da3e4a6e9c22ceaac9ca carried that flaw. Later bundle 2d9a2ec76e180b54e8091e31b1e0638c909abd99 added genericAuthType to the static set, fixing literal generic types but preserving the advisory's expression form because it inserted the unresolved expression literal rather than the resolved credential type.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A user who can configure a Budibase automation can supply an arbitrary HTTP(S) URL to the outgoing-webhook (and later Zapier, n8n, Slack, Discord, and Make.com) step. The server dereferenced that URL with axios/node-fetch without destination validation, so it could reach loopback, RFC1918, link-local/cloud-metadata, and other internal services (CWE-918). The REST datasource's separate guard was also fail-open by default because an unset BLACKLIST_IPS produced an empty list and isBlacklisted returned false; it neither protected automation fetches nor supplied secure defaults.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 3ae82b95a31bcb6b3803d3ad8d8c5accb7606ef3 first created and registered the executable OUTGOING_WEBHOOK automation. Its run function accepted inputs.url, normalized it only by adding http://, and called axios(request) with no allowlist/denylist or resolved-address check. Commit 3d77163773d0ab37342e9e2be5d6b8797758e4eb later changed axios to node-fetch, and a3bb2e0d770fe0c66f0382aebef86faa2bbcc696 renamed/migrated the same step to TypeScript; those are implementation changes preserving the pre-existing SSRF, not introducers. Commit 564c724be11895fa6bc1766aef3a149fae3223e3 later added an opt-in REST-only blacklist whose empty-default behavior left that separate path unprotected when BLACKLIST_IPS was unset.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A post-authenticated user with Create and Modify permission can write attacker-controlled bytes outside the user's scope when an in-scope symlink points to a not-yet-existing out-of-scope file. EvalSymlinks on the link returns fs.ErrNotExist; the guard then walks the lexical path up to the link's in-scope containing directory and approves that ancestor. The subsequent OpenFile call uses O_CREATE|O_TRUNC, so the OS follows the dangling symlink and creates the target outside the scope.

Commit 7c2c0a11b31b2bb214d741005a0b02b1764208b3 later moved the same flawed fallback into ScopedFs.within and centralized OpenFile behind that guard; the refactor preserved rather than originated the flaw.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: TemplateContext.Reset() made a context appear safe to reuse but left its CachedTemplates dictionary intact. After one render cached a request-dependent include, a later render on the reset context found the same path in CachedTemplates and returned the old compiled Template without invoking ITemplateLoader.Load(), so content authorized for an earlier request, user, or tenant could cross the reuse boundary.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 2e95889099c3ee5e7a4c0147b7355ecd309200af introduced the public Reset() API and explicitly promised safe same-thread reuse, but reset only output, global, culture, and source-file stacks. Scriban's include cache and loader-on-cache-miss path already existed in the immediate parent; omitting CachedTemplates from the newly defined reset boundary is therefore the smallest change that created the advisory's vulnerable lifecycle.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: TemplateContext caches an IObjectAccessor solely under the target's System.Type. For ordinary .NET objects, the cached TypedObjectAccessor eagerly computes its member dictionary using the context's then-current MemberFilter (and MemberRenamer). If the same TemplateContext is later reused after MemberFilter is tightened, GetMemberAccessor returns the permissive accessor already cached for that Type, so reads or writes of members now denied by policy remain available.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: ace7a0ebafa6d01500f83c35975cde38d559fa3d first added TemplateContext.MemberFilter and, in the same commit, passed that mutable per-context policy into TypedObjectAccessor while leaving the pre-existing Type-only _memberAccessors cache unchanged and without invalidation. The later 2e95889099c3ee5e7a4c0147b7355ecd309200af added TemplateContext.Reset with an explicit safe-reuse contract but likewise retained the accessor cache, making the stale-policy flaw directly reachable during pooled/cross-request reuse; that later commit amplified but did not originate the flawed filter/cache composition.

audit_record.reasoning: The attack requires a context to first encounter a model Type under a permissive filter, causing TypedObjectAccessor to snapshot that Type's allowed members, and then to reuse the context under a stricter filter. Because lookup consults only the Type key, later member-expression access receives the old accessor and bypasses the new sandbox policy. Historical decomposition separates three stages: the Type cache existed from the initial repository history; ace7a0e was the smallest normal commit that made it security-sensitive to MemberFilter by adding the policy and feeding it into the cached accessor; 2e95889 later formalized safe TemplateContext reuse without flushing that cache. The immediate parent lacks MemberFilter and the filter-bearing constructor entirely, while ace7a0e's own diff writes both causal additions, establishing parent absence and the BIC. The direct fix clears the stale accessors during Reset and is released exactly at the declared 7.0.0 patched boundary after 6.6.0. Finally, attribution is restricted to the BIC commit object: it is a one-parent human-authored commit with no AI marker. The correct closed verdict is therefore NOT_AI regardless of any signals on later lifecycle commits.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Rendering a ScriptObject recursively stringifies each member value without cycle detection. A ScriptObject whose member points back to itself therefore repeatedly re-enters the object-to-string path; with ObjectRecursionLimit left at its default value of 0, the guard is disabled and recursion continues until an uncatchable StackOverflowException terminates the host process.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e made ScriptObject rendering traverse the real stored member values and recursively call ScriptValueConverter.ToString on each one. Its parent exposed the InternalValue wrapper instead and had no dedicated recursive ScriptObject rendering block, so the advisory's self-referential ScriptObject path begins in this commit. Commit a9affb64614358838aba16f28acb198f914e586d later added an opt-in ObjectRecursionLimit guard but initialized it to 0 (unlimited), preserving the flaw by default rather than introducing the recursive attack path.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: POST /api/provider-nodes/validate accepts caller-controlled baseUrl and apiKey, makes server-side requests to baseUrl-derived provider endpoints, and forwards the supplied secret in Authorization headers. The later assertPublicUrl mitigation checks only the URL hostname string: it neither resolves DNS nor revalidates redirect destinations, and its IPv4-mapped IPv6 regex expects a dotted quad even though WHATWG URL canonicalization has already converted that quad to hextets. A mapped loopback or link-local literal, a domain resolving to a private address, or a redirect can therefore reach internal services. The custom-embedding path reflects the first 200 bytes of a non-2xx response other than 401/403; the other paths expose status, timing, and error differences for blind port scanning.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 0a28f9f924d2dc53027a910679ee3cff3e63a59c created the validation route and, in the same minimal change, read baseUrl/apiKey from the request, interpolated baseUrl into /models, fetched it without any destination policy, and forwarded apiKey as a Bearer token. That is the first complete attacker-controlled outbound-request mechanism. Commit 0b8bed5793c7a7c9beb7a5db7368720907f61ebc later added the custom-embedding branch and 200-byte error-body disclosure; 090886ced9a3481837f5687ec66da7d9f33eea08 later connected a hostname-only guard; and 8ac631d6158c0f04976a0d0f7ca9ec2b981efeb5 later added an ineffective mapped-IPv6 check. Those later changes altered impact or attempted mitigation but did not originate the SSRF sink, which was already exploitable in their parents.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A browser page can retain the attacker-controlled origin name while DNS rebinding moves its TCP connection to Paperclip on loopback. Paperclip accepted the attacker hostname because the API had no Host-header gate, assigned requests without a valid bearer credential the trusted board actor, allowed that actor to create/configure an agent, and exposed a heartbeat invocation path whose process adapter passed the stored command and arguments to node:child_process spawn. Thus visiting an attacker page could turn an unauthenticated cross-origin web request into command execution as the Paperclip OS user.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: abadd469bc85e9fa5137ff5ffce433f1c2db2c0b is the smallest commit that completed the RCE mechanism. In one non-merge commit it added server/src/middleware/auth.ts with a board actor as the default for requests lacking a recognized bearer key, mounted company and expanded agent routes in server/src/app.ts without any Host validation, added agent creation and POST /agents/:id/heartbeat/invoke, and created server/src/services/heartbeat.ts where non-HTTP adapter configuration supplies command, args, cwd, and env to spawn(). Its immediate parent had the basic API shell but neither heartbeat.ts nor this process-execution path, so it could not execute an API-configured local command through the disclosed chain.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The runner registration-token API exposed token creation through GET routes. The existing token-scope middleware derives Read versus Write solely from the HTTP method, so a read-scoped user, organization, repository, or admin token could pass the GET route even though shared.GetRegistrationToken calls actions_model.NewRunnerToken when no usable token exists. The caller receives that credential and can register an Actions runner, which can then execute workflow jobs with access to repository source and secrets.

The scope middleware already treated all GET requests as Read in that member's immediate parent. A later member, bba250f3e99bef12bbd9a1d9d790ab8155c999d5, added the user and repository variants, extending rather than originating the same flawed mechanism.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated non-site-admin with the perm_template permission can GET the event-template add page (or edit a template writable by that user's organisation). EventTemplatesController::__setBuilderConfig() queried every enabled Galaxy row without Galaxy visibility conditions, grouped the results by type, retained each type and description, and embedded that data in window.ET_BUILDER_CONFIG.multipickerSources. Consequently, the builder response disclosed metadata for enabled private distribution-0 galaxies owned by other organisations.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 47bf71cc78d13c06e1eaa4d9842e6f94ddce4bea introduced the galaxy-type picker and, in the same atomic feature commit, first added the server-side Galaxy->find('all') with only 'Galaxy.enabled' => true. It did not call Galaxy::buildConditions() or otherwise restrict by the requesting user's organisation/distribution before exposing Galaxy.type and Galaxy.description to the browser.

The vulnerable mechanism is therefore absent from the direct parent.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The scoped-token rollout guarded the mutating PUT /user route with the read-only profile:read capability. RequireScopes therefore admitted an access token carrying only profile:read, while UpdateUser trusted the token's associated admin identity and allowed its password to be replaced. The token holder could then log in with the replacement password and receive a session JWT; session JWTs deliberately bypass scope checks, turning a read-only token into unrestricted administrator access.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An administrator or authenticated caller with connect-write authority can persist an attacker-chosen ConnectURL. The public GET /api/connects/info path, and later the authenticated connection-health path, cause the server to append /api/connect and issue an unrestricted outbound HTTP request to that stored URL. Because the request primitive performs no URL, resolved-address, redirect, loopback, private-network, or link-local/cloud-metadata validation, the caller can make the Ech0 server reach internal services and metadata endpoints and return or infer their responses.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: fabee479ccf98c081bb065926c726b461a42fdf3 first moved peer-detail retrieval from the browser into the server: it added publicRoutes.GET("/connects/info", controllers.GetConnectsInfo), GetConnectsInfo's iteration over stored ConnectURL values, and pkg.SendRequest implemented with an unconstrained http.Client.Do. The same commit therefore created both the server-side attacker-controlled request and the missing trust-boundary validation; later copies, retries, health checks, rewrites, and the fetchPeerConnectInfo extraction preserved rather than originated that mechanism.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An admin-issued access JWT carrying only a minimal capability such as echo:read was accepted by JWTAuthMiddleware and reached all nine /api/panel/comments/* routes because those AuthRouterGroup registrations had no RequireScopes middleware. The comment service's requireAdmin checked only the viewer's database user role, not the token's scopes, so the limited token could list/get comments, change status or hot state, delete or batch-moderate comments, read/write comment settings, and send a test email.

It did not add enforcement to the already-existing comment panel routes. Its immediate parent could issue only the old unrestricted token and therefore did not contain the scoped-token authorization contract that could be bypassed. Later member b47fa1c75d890cd080e3f6699bbfca8cd8d4b939 added RequireScopes to other route families but still left comment.go untouched, preserving the flaw when the member chain landed as squash 3f8fb150158723aca31df2ae937a1aa7b31ac254.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: PUT /api/global/users/tenant/owner performed a top-privilege identity mutation without an internal-or-admin authorization check. Its cloudRestricted middleware validated an internal API key only when neither SELF_HOSTED nor DISABLE_ACCOUNT_PORTAL was set; in those self-hosted/account-portal-disabled modes it simply called next(). causal_chain.bug_semantics: Ech0 treated access-token scopes as an opt-in route property rather than an invariant of authenticated access. A deliberately low-scope token for an administrator (for example, echo:read) was accepted by the shared JWT middleware on privileged routes that omitted RequireScopes; downstream services commonly checked only the account's IsAdmin bit. The public backup export path was worse: it reparsed a query token and rebuilt viewer state from only claims.Userid, dropping token type, scopes, audience, and JTI, so the same low-scope token could export the database ZIP.

Its immediate parent 387667192911c86db1e1bcb3f544ce12d340ffdb minted only unscoped access tokens, so the scoped least-privilege contract that could be bypassed did not yet exist. causal_chain.bug_semantics: Ech0 globally ran its i18n middleware before every route and accepted an unauthenticated request's raw Accept-Language value with only TrimSpace. The value reached golang.org/x/text/language.ParseAcceptLanguage both directly through ResolveLocale and indirectly through go-i18n's NewLocalizer. x/text's CVE-2022-32149 guard counted '-' but not '_', although its scanner later treats '_' as '-', so a near-1 MiB header composed of malformed underscore-separated tags bypassed the guard and repeatedly exercised the quadratic gobble/memmove path, consuming seconds of CPU per request and enabling denial of service.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit b55edabd228d3de41e781bd3100f2e1ee0835516 introduced the entire backend i18n path: internal/i18n/i18n.go added ResolveLocale, the unsanitized goi18n.NewLocalizer wrapper, and Middleware reading Accept-Language, while internal/router/middleware.go installed that middleware globally. Thus the application's exposure originated when attacker-controlled header input was first connected to the vulnerable parser without a size or shape bound; the parser defect itself pre-existed in x/text.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated non-administrator can select a directory whose root path is allowed even though a descendant is denied by a path rule. Copy, rename, and delete then recurse over the filesystem subtree without authorizing each source descendant and, for copy/rename, the corresponding destination descendant. The user can therefore expose or relocate denied content at an allowed destination, or destroy it by deleting its allowed parent.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit b4067cc423b1a0a9d24441bd52e2a53207a49fe9 first added resource.go with recursive directory mutation endpoints: resourceDeleteHandler called FileSystem.RemoveAll on the request root and resourcePatchHandler called FileSystem.Rename on the source root, with no path-rule check for descendants. Commit 05896697fa2730e59b8bcf6f1253da0f6fb8b5a9 later added only one c.User.Allowed(r.URL.Path) gate before dispatch, creating the root-authorized/descendants-unchecked form; commit 149465ab5278c135030466632c7fa79905c4646b added the copy variant. The v2 rewrite and later root checks preserved the same missing descendant authorization until the 2026 fix.

In the validated clone, `git show b4067cc... -- resource.go` shows resource.go created from /dev/null and introduces resourceDeleteHandler -> c.us.FileSystem.RemoveAll(..., r.URL.Path) and resourcePatchHandler -> c.us.FileSystem.Rename(..., src, dst), without a descendant walk or rule checker. `git cat-file -e f6aeb27c...:resource.go` fails because the immediate parent has no resource.go, while the BIC tree has it, directly proving the vulnerable implementation absent from the parent. `git log -L` shows 05896697... later adding a single root c.User.Allowed(r.URL.Path) gate while leaving recursive Rename/RemoveAll unchanged, and 149465ab... later adding recursive copy; thus those are lifecycle refinements, not the first writer. At v2.63.21, http/resource.go checks only NewFileInfo/Checker on the delete root and d.Check(src)/d.Check(dst) on patch roots, then calls RemoveAll, fileutils.Copy, or fileutils.MoveFile without descendant-rule checks. `git grep checkDescendants v2.63.21 -- http/resource.go` has no match; v2.63.22 has calls before delete and patch plus an afero.Walk implementation that checks every source and mapped destination path with CheckRules. `git merge-base --is-ancestor 72faf6dd... v2.63.22` succeeds and the same check against v2.63.21 fails; tag tips are f6fb8f6bf52d714b2215534033a3c96316069efc (v2.63.21) and afeb478ee1b9d6800d438891d7d56e69204b81f4 (v2.63.22). `git tag --contains b4067cc...` begins at v1.0.0 and includes the vulnerable v2 line through v2.63.21, so the BIC predates the reported affected releases and the fix lands at the patched boundary.

Commit 05896697fa2730e59b8bcf6f1253da0f6fb8b5a9 later added only one c.User.Allowed(r.URL.Path) gate before dispatch, creating the root-authorized/descendants-unchecked form; commit 149465ab5278c135030466632c7fa79905c4646b added the copy variant. The v2 rewrite and later root checks preserved the same missing descendant authorization until the 2026 fix.
audit_record.reasoning: The advisory and fix define the invariant: authorization must cover every path a recursive mutation reads, moves, writes, or removes, not merely the requested root. Starting from the fix, history tracing followed RemoveAll, Rename/MoveFile, and Copy rather than blaming the 2026 patch or a later refactor. The earliest surviving commit that wrote this unsafe recursive mutation design is b4067cc423b1a0a9d24441bd52e2a53207a49fe9: it created resource.go and added directory-wide RemoveAll and Rename calls without descendant authorization. Its immediate parent lacks that file, so the implementation is directly absent there. The later 05896697 root rule gate narrowed the pre-existing omission into the exact allowed-parent/denied-child bypass, 149465ab added copy, the 12b2c215 v2 aggregate carried the design forward, and later root-only checks did not cure it. The direct fix 72faf6dd adds a pre-mutation tree walk and denies the operation if any source or mapped destination path violates a rule. Finally, only the BIC commit object was used for attribution: its human author/committer and trailer set contain no AI marker, so the causal result is NOT_AI.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Access rules treated the request path as a case-sensitive, slash-separated string and performed literal/prefix matching before the same path was resolved by the host filesystem. On case-insensitive filesystems, a case variant of a denied path therefore missed the rule but named the denied file; on Windows, backslashes and traversal components likewise missed the rule but were normalized by the filesystem. An authenticated user could consequently disclose or mutate an administrator-denied file within the user's filesystem scope.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 9c36dea485ddd16a90f0a615e20baddaee6b9cde first added the access-rule model and its vulnerable enforcement in one change: filemanager.go's User.Allowed compared the uncanonicalized URL with strings.HasPrefix(url, rule.Path), while newly added http.go passed raw request-derived paths to Allowed and then performed filesystem operations. Its immediate parent 780f1bc16e4e5270fed2a6b7da442a47084d8c4b contains none of Rule, User.Allowed, or that comparison. Later commits only moved, extracted, or broadened this mechanism, and the v2 rewrite aggregate preserved it.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated BASIC app user can POST /api/attachments/:datasourceId/url. The route's TABLE/WRITE authorization is satisfied by the built-in BASIC role, and getSignedUploadURL loads the named S3 datasource, then uses its stored IAM credentials to presign a PutObject for the request body's bucket and key. Thus a non-builder can obtain an upload capability; where the datasource has no configured bucket constraint, the caller can select any bucket writable by those IAM credentials.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The exploitable authorization regression begins in 23d75319026aec328a707e40e9437cb3bd6d9912, which replaced authorized(BUILDER) with authorized(PermissionType.TABLE, PermissionLevel.READ) on the signed-upload route. Its immediate follow-up test proves a BASIC user receives HTTP 200 and a signed URL. Commit 3e881e13186eb9da19c37deb2f55b3ab46e560b8 tightened READ to WRITE before release, but BASIC is the built-in WRITE role, so it retained the same unauthorized access. The controller's caller-controlled bucket sink pre-existed; 23d7531 is the smallest commit that exposed that sink to BASIC users.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated user with Create permission could create a TUS upload with a small finite Upload-Length, then send a PATCH body larger than Upload-Length minus Upload-Offset. tusPatchHandler streamed the entire body to the file with io.Copy before comparing the resulting offset with the cached declared length; reaching or exceeding that length merely completed the upload. The excess bytes therefore remained on disk, and repeated oversized PATCH uploads could exhaust the filesystem.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: PR #5270 member 6337c4452529dfc018885a7d05cc4f1e217316c5 first made FileBrowser accept and retain the client's finite Upload-Length: it added registerUpload/getActiveUploadLength, retrieved that value in tusPatchHandler, and used it only after the pre-existing unbounded io.Copy to unregister a completed upload. Its direct parent advertised Upload-Length: -1 and neither parsed nor tracked a declared length, so the advisory-specific promise-and-bypass mechanism did not yet exist. GitHub later squash-merged the PR as 0f27c91eca581482ce4f82f6429f5dac12f8b64e.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: On a fresh instance with no password configured, check_auth() deliberately admitted every request. POST /api/settings nevertheless accepted the ownership-establishing _set_password pseudo-setting: save_settings() hashed the attacker-chosen value into settings.json as password_hash, turning authentication on. A remote unauthenticated first caller could therefore choose the initial credential, authenticate (and, after the later session-continuity change, receive a session immediately), and lock out the intended operator. The missing invariant was that the unauthenticated disabled-auth state must not permit a non-local client to perform the transition that establishes the first trust root.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The optional-password feature commit introduced both halves of the flaw together: api/auth.py made check_auth() return true whenever no password existed, while api/config.py made the already-generic /api/settings save path interpret untrusted _set_password as authority to persist the first password. It added no locality, bootstrap token, or existing-owner check around that transition. A later commit only added automatic cookie issuance; it did not originate the takeover because an attacker could already log in with the password they selected.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The now-rejected report alleged that an attacker could alter the authentication strategy in an OTP-stage sign-in request and complete an OAuth sign-in without the correct code because the server did not revalidate the prepared verification stage. The public report supplies no concrete request, strategy pair, reproducible proof, or vulnerable server behavior, and the canonical CVE record now states that further investigation found this was not a security issue.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: If the reported behavior had been real, the security decision would have been in Clerk's Frontend API server: the server would have failed to bind an attempted factor strategy and credential to the sign-in's prepared challenge. packages/clerk-js/src/core/resources/SignIn.ts is only a typed transport wrapper that posts caller-supplied factor parameters to attempt_first_factor/attempt_second_factor; client-side typing or request construction cannot enforce authorization against a network attacker. The canonical CNA rejection means no actual flaw origin is established in this repository or elsewhere.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A logged-in user could submit a saved graph configuration whose config_json was checked only for syntactically valid JSON. The server stored and returned the object without a property allowlist; an administrator's list included every user's saved configurations. Loading one parsed the stored JSON and applyConfig spread every property of attacker-controlled stixStyles or mispStyles entries into GRAPH_CONFIG. Those style maps were then passed to Pivotick as nodeStyleMap/defaultNodeStyle, and Pivotick interpreted a supplied svgIcon as HTML, so viewing/loading the saved configuration could execute attacker script in another user's browser.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit a0a9834b21b40ab570db54e1c6e6c2cf100b5f9a introduced the complete unsafe saved-configuration path in one focused feature commit: the graph_config model and save/list routes, unrestricted JSON persistence, the saved-config loader, and applyConfig's unrestricted style-object spreads. Its immediate parent had none of the graph-config persistence, loading, or patch-application mechanism, making this ordinary one-parent feature commit the smallest reconstructable BIC rather than the later branch merge or a release commit.

git show 9b317587fa4ec11b6f72c2d1d8b98a686537b4fb is the direct one-parent fix: website/web/conversions/conversions.py validates clean JSON before saving and sanitizes stored config_json on list; conversions_core.py permits only known keys and only shape/color/size in style entries; conversionGraph.js calls sanitizeConfigPatch before merging; graphSafety.js independently filters the client patch and excludes svgIcon/iconClass. git tag --contains the fix returned only v1.5, and v1.5 tree grep confirms validate_graph_config, sanitize_stored_graph_config, and sanitizeConfigPatch while v1.4 still has the vulnerable path. audit_record.reasoning: The vulnerability begins when a0a9834b21b40ab570db54e1c6e6c2cf100b5f9a adds persistent graph configurations and accepts arbitrary JSON structure. A malicious authenticated user can place svgIcon inside a style entry, store it, and rely on an administrator's all-config listing to make that row available. The saved-config loader parses the row, applyConfig copies the unrecognized property into the live style map, and the renderer hands the map to Pivotick's HTML-interpreting svgIcon path. causal_chain.bug_semantics: The authenticated ticket routes trusted a user-controlled numeric ticket id without constraining the selected Ticket to Auth::user()->company_id. GET /ticket/update/{id} returned another tenant's ticket data and, after attachment support was added, enumerated that ticket's attachment directory; POST /ticket/save accepted an id, loaded that arbitrary Ticket, overwrote its fields and company_id, and thereby let the caller hijack it; GET /ticket/delete/{id} loaded and deleted an arbitrary Ticket while using generic Request, so neither tenant ownership nor TicketDeleteRequest permission authorization was enforced.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The core cross-tenant read and write/hijack mechanism originated in the initial ticket CRUD commit 2feef9f35593dba39525f6a8a07b4cd3f74f19bd: TicketUpdateController called Ticket::find($id), and TicketSaveController called Ticket::find($request->id) before assigning the authenticated user's company_id, with no ownership predicate. Commit 946a0c5e43a1178534e5b013ea2608d565686220 later extended the same trust error to deletion, commit 626b0228c248637086ce91bb17b2ec1b1c21961b later extended the read impact to attachments, and repository/refactor changes preserved rather than originated the core flaw.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The authenticated GET /get_history_details endpoint loads a retained history row by caller-controlled history_id, then loads its parent conversion. The repository lookup deliberately returns None for a soft-deleted conversion. The vulnerable guard authorized only when the parent existed (`if conversion_obj and ...`), so a missing/deleted parent skipped the denial and the endpoint returned conversion_history.to_json(), including retained input_text, old_output_text, and new_output_text, to any logged-in user who could request that history ID.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 37d7ba64638ad78f4604725f81bafac497ca235a introduced the exact fail-open mechanism in one ordinary commit: it added @login_required and a parent-visibility check to get_history_details, but made that check conditional on a truthy parent, while simultaneously changing get_convert() to exclude inactive soft-deleted conversions by default and return None. Thus deletion made the authorization subject disappear and the new conditional treated that state as authorized. Later renames/repository extraction and 9a8a78d1df3ca96f8d26884b8a08e03a7260c925's access.can_see refactor preserved the outer `conversion_obj and` condition rather than originating the flaw.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The POST routes /fetch_misp_event and /misp_search_events accepted a caller-controlled HTTPS MISP base URL, passed it through _validate_misp_url, and then made a server-side request whose response was returned to the caller. A caller could therefore supply a domain resolving to an internal address and use the server to reach and read an internal MISP endpoint. Both routes were also callable anonymously, increasing exposure, although the unresolved-domain allow decision is the SSRF root cause.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The authenticated POST /contact/save path trusted the request's numeric contact id and loaded Contact::find(...) without company_id scoping before overwriting the record, so a user could blindly modify another tenant's contact. The authenticated GET /contact/export-vcard/{id} path likewise used Contact::findOrFail($id) without company_id scoping and returned the selected record's vCard, allowing cross-tenant PII disclosure by id enumeration.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The write primitive originated in 266c2bec31a4ef56431f0ee9ed4dfadfa12661b9, which added the authenticated /contact/save route and a new ContactSaveController whose update branch selected a Contact solely by attacker-controlled id; contacts were already owned through company-scoped leads, so the missing ownership check was exploitable at introduction. Commit 9fda3ee70b7b6035f729a154f7bf50bfabbd3b7f later added an explicit contact.company_id on creation while retaining the unscoped update. Commit 65f6b9f961efe533b4d3f20f1eddad132fe8ef1d merely moved the same vulnerable save logic into ContactRepository and is not the BIC. The independent vCard disclosure surface was added from scratch by a0306e77f95aaf57afec25ef74e4aa2da275c830.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The Markdown and PDF evaluation-export endpoints enforced only conversion-level visibility, then build_evaluation_report() queried every non-deleted evaluation Comment for that conversion without applying the existing per-comment privacy rule. The report serialized both c.content and the author's first name, so a viewer allowed to see the conversion could export private evaluation comments that were reserved for the conversion owner, comment author, or an administrator.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Remote-data DOM XSS in the MISP event browser: the server accepts an operator-selected remote MISP instance, copies that instance's event fields into JSON, and the browser interpolates those values into template strings assigned to innerHTML. A malicious or compromised remote MISP can therefore inject markup or script-capable content through event IDs, information, organization/date/count/threat fields, tag names and colors, TLP/distribution labels, or flash/error text; unvalidated tag colors also enter inline CSS.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48 added the remote-MISP connection/browser feature and, in the same atomic commit, passed remote response fields through website/web/convert/convert.py and rendered them with div.innerHTML, overlay.innerHTML, and tr.innerHTML in website/web/templates/convert/misp_to_stix.html. The core mistake was treating remote-derived strings and colors as trusted HTML/CSS instead of creating DOM nodes and assigning textContent plus validating colors. Commit 26ecb7e6a608b5be73fa552928e00bef7cac4f22 later expanded selection/distribution behavior and added further instances of the same mechanism, but b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48 is the earliest and smallest real BIC for the vulnerable event-browser mechanism.

Under the protocol, that makes the closed verdict NOT_AI regardless of AI signals on unrelated commits.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: rConfig deliberately disabled Laravel self-registration with Auth::routes(['register' => false]), but a later bare Auth::routes() call registered the framework's default registration endpoints again. An unauthenticated POST /register therefore reached RegisterController, whose create() method omitted role; the users.role database column defaulted to Admin, and the RegistersUsers flow authenticated the newly created account. The attacker consequently obtained a logged-in Administrator account without invitation, approval, or prior credentials.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The smallest first-writer is 5ae01b3781de867baad1a8aa8aebfc3448812f68. In the multiple-SSO feature commit, routes/web.php gained the single causally decisive line Auth::routes(); between the new SAML logout and provider redirect routes. The already-present disabled-registration call, framework registration controller, and Admin column default made that new route dangerous, but they did not expose registration while the only auth route declaration had register=false. The candidate's immediate parent 6202a5d9e061fce98de25ec8b62a4973c0dffd35 has no bare call.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated GET /download-export request supplied filename directly to download_export(), which concatenated export_path() with the raw $_GET['filename'] value and, after only file_exists(), passed the resulting path to response()->download(). A filename containing ../ could therefore escape the exports directory and disclose any file readable by the web-server account.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: In authenticated HTTP mode, an attacker-controlled Bearer token was treated as a session-file basename without restricting its alphabet or confining the resulting path. The token was joined as SESSION_DIR / f"{token}.session" and opened as a Telethon session. After the project added an exact-name denylist for the legacy session name `telegram`, a token such as `../fast-mcp-telegram/telegram` still resolved to the same default telegram.session file, passed the literal reserved-name comparison, and authenticated the remote client as that Telegram account.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 763b3e781d8fb0067fbedd85ea0f25d53a951a2e introduced multi-user HTTP Bearer authentication and the causal coupling between the raw header token and a filesystem path. Its src/server.py accepted any nonempty string after `Bearer ` and placed it in request context, while src/client/connection.py:38-55 created a client from SESSION_DIR / f"{token}.session" with no token-shape or path-containment check. Commit 1be7e62feb6160ecbe32d15f0ab940769f094968 later added exact reserved-name rejection but left that pre-existing path primitive unchanged, so it narrowed the direct `telegram` bypass without closing traversal aliases.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: When the experimental Extension backend handles another node's added or removed lease, it JSON-unmarshals attacker-controlled flannel.alpha.coreos.com/backend-data and writes that string to stdin of runCmd while launching the configured SubnetAddCommand or SubnetRemoveCommand through sh -c. A user able to set Kubernetes Node annotations can therefore feed untrusted content into a root-privileged shell-command path on every flannel node using this backend, enabling cross-node command injection; non-Extension backends do not execute this path.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The trust-boundary error was present in the original Extension backend implementation: its first commit simultaneously introduced the BackendData annotation flow, the stdin pipe, and sh -c execution for subnet add/remove hooks. Later empty-data handling, package moves, logging changes, and context refactors preserved rather than originated that mechanism.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An MCP caller can invoke smart_user with operation=get-user-info, useCache=false, and an attacker-controlled username. SmartUser.run dispatches that request through getUserInfo(options) to getUserDetails(options.username), which on Unix interpolates username into `getent passwd "${username}" || grep "^${username}:" /etc/passwd` and passes the resulting string to promisified child_process.exec. POSIX command substitution remains active inside double quotes, so a username containing `$(...)` or backticks executes arbitrary commands with the MCP server process's privileges.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The vulnerable smart-user.ts implementation did not originate in an independently authored commit visible in this repository. Commit fc3582544f6df4a14dcd3015edc835780f746aff added the entire file while importing the complete pre-existing hypercontext tools package; PR #6 explicitly labels fc35825 as the initial integration of 367 hypercontext tool files. Because an import/move is not a BIC under the audit protocol, the smallest commit that originally wrote the vulnerable shell interpolation lies in the unavailable hypercontext source history.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The awx CLI import command parses attacker-supplied YAML from client.stdin with awxkit.yaml_file.Loader. Loader registers !include and !import, and extractFile joins the directive value to the input stream's directory (which is empty for <stdin>), expands the result with glob.glob, converts matches to absolute paths, and opens and recursively parses them without rejecting absolute paths, '..' traversal, or symlink escapes. A user who imports a malicious YAML document can therefore disclose arbitrary locally readable YAML-formatted files.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The advisory combines two x-proxy-path trust failures. In admin.ts, an attacker-controlled request header was inserted verbatim into served HTML, JavaScript, and CSS; because those header-dependent responses also lacked Vary and private/no-store cache controls, the reflection enabled direct or shared-cache-poisoning XSS on the admin origin. Separately, specialpages.ts passed a sanitizer that allowed leading slashes and then concatenated its result into a 302 Location. An x-proxy-path value of //evil.example therefore produced //evil.example/p/<encoded-pad>, which a browser follows as a protocol-relative cross-origin redirect.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: There are two independently introduced mechanisms. The open-redirect mechanism first appeared when PR #7710 member f784c8c47c16e184b3ef3bdbf84485d4e5c42eb2 changed a safe relative redirect into an absolute redirect prefixed by sanitizeProxyPath(req), whose then-current character filter preserved a leading //. That member was later represented on the main branch by squash commit 451bd9c3ebb0dded99dd0ff21811ee00e0940c29. causal_chain.bug_semantics: On Linux/Unix, LocalFolderExtractor first constructs and canonicalizes new File(destination, archiveEntryName) while backslashes in the untrusted RAR name are still literal filename characters. A name such as '..\..\tmp\evil' therefore passes the destination-prefix check. If the file does not exist, makeFile then splits that same name on backslashes and rejoins the components with File.separator, turning the previously literal '..' components into real '/' traversal. extract subsequently opens FileOutputStream on that reconstructed path and writes attacker-controlled archive content outside the extraction directory.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The causal flaw is the two-stage, inconsistent interpretation of an archive pathname: validation and use do not operate on the same normalized representation. The backslash-splitting/reconstruction and write path first appear in the repository's root initial-import commit 6f32323c983015d96c64084418793853f514b519 in testutil/src/main/java/de/innosystec/unrar/testutil/ExtractArchive.java. That implementation was later promoted and moved through production paths without changing the mechanism; e60b915f8932c08b9b6874a97f00676decba069a added canonical-path validation but left it before the separator reinterpretation, creating the advisory's explicit validation bypass rather than originating the underlying arbitrary-write mechanism.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Etherpad generated import/export working-file names in the shared process temporary directory from Math.random(), then used ordinary write, rename, and converter operations that follow existing symbolic links. A local low-privilege user who can predict a token and pre-create the corresponding /tmp path as a symlink can redirect Etherpad's file operation to a target writable by the Etherpad process, causing disclosure or overwrite; import output can contain attacker-influenced converted document content.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The earliest causal origin is eeddf1348f351c92355d010ced56c3b511ca8f46: the initial document-export implementation created node/ExportHandler.js with Math.floor(Math.random()*new Date().getTime()), a hard-coded /tmp/eplite_export_ path, fs.writeFile(), and converter output at a sibling predictable path. b13fbbfd73ab18f69d45de382ffb1fc51fe96f1f added the same design to import two days later. Commits 4fc4a3538148bc995fff989794e91779ed4c847f and b0976a292f70c2c6d344bafd2793aed09027f74b later changed the token formula to Math.random()*0xFFFFFFFF, reducing it to the advisory's exact 32-bit form, but they did not originate the insecure shared-temp predictable-name mechanism.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated environment-key holder can supply a run-metadata operation whose unconstrained key is a JSONHero path such as $.__proto__.polluted. applyMetadataOperations passes that key to JSONHeroPath.set on a normal cloned object without rejecting __proto__, constructor, or prototype segments, so the write reaches Object.prototype in the shared webapp process; inherited attacker properties then corrupt unrelated Prisma and metrics objects across tenants and can crash the process.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: PR #1563 added the metadata-operations API and, in its member commit cf80a02d23d99b0f4eebe4ac5eb42059f34b2b3d, created packages/core/src/v3/runMetadata/operations.ts with JSONHeroPath(operation.key).set(...) while simultaneously defining every keyed operation schema with key: z.string(). The endpoint's API-key-authenticated request body was therefore connected directly to a prototype-walking setter with no dangerous-segment validation from the feature's first implementation.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The Admin Console gadget bootstrap accepts the request-controlled gadget parameter as a URL/path, parses the referenced XML into a GadgetModule, and emits the module text with escaping disabled inside JSFTemplating. That template path evaluates EL in the attacker-controlled XML/content (the source itself warns that JSFT content is evaluated twice), so expressions such as #{7*7} execute server-side and richer EL access to constructors, static methods/fields, getClass(), or class can reach arbitrary code execution.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The causal origin is the 2009 gadget endpoint commit ece6ab82e495d2cf87cbf4ec78170727adf2c7f1: it first added gadget.jsf and wired #{param.gadget} into gf.getGadgetModule while rendering pageSession.gadget.text through escape=false. The immediately preceding infrastructure commit 16e12748c3def5754a21f3019a1794b899862017 supplied the URL-capable XML loader, but had no request-reachable gadget.jsf endpoint; ece6ab82 is therefore the smallest commit that completed the vulnerable untrusted-input-to-EL-evaluation path.

HTML output escaping does not neutralize server-side EL evaluation.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated bot author can store a rich-text link whose URL uses the javascript: scheme. The @typebot.io/js viewer rendered that author-controlled link into the DOM without validating its scheme—initially by assigning serialized content.html to SolidJS innerHTML and, after a 2023 refactor, by assigning the rich-text element URL directly to an anchor href. When a visitor clicks the link, the browser executes the payload in the embedding host page's origin, allowing theft of host-origin cookies, session tokens, and other accessible data; victim authentication is not required.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The smallest reconstructable BIC is PR #194's sole member commit 3487850b9f4808617d347ddde4d9701f56662894. It created packages/js/src/features/blocks/bubbles/textBubble/components/TextBubble.tsx and introduced the unsafe sink innerHTML={props.content.html} for author-controlled serialized rich text, while the pre-existing builder toolbar already exposed LinkToolbarButton without a protocol allowlist. GitHub landed the same parent and identical tree as mainline carrier 1a3869ae6d9fa92fc71ef9d981bfffb8e4ee4ecc. Commit e0a9824913237cb5340d262770e9e8290fbc4002 later replaced the stored-HTML sink with a recursive Plate renderer containing <a href={props.element.url as string}>, preserving rather than originating the missing-scheme-validation flaw; 765c4b2f8c1fd4ec610bc81b2547efbda65452ae was another refactor of that same unsafe href.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The privileged /admin/gateways/test flow performed a security decision on DNS answers obtained while validating the submitted hostname, then gave an httpx-based ResilientHttpClient a URL containing that same hostname. The client therefore performed an independent connection-time resolution. An attacker controlling DNS could return a public address for validation and then rebind the hostname to a private, loopback, link-local, or cloud-metadata address for the actual request, bypassing the SSRF network checks.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: PR #3115 member d34f611030166bbdd4ea2d93d909098c9dc8d934 first inserted SecurityValidator.validate_url(str(request.base_url), ...) into admin_test_gateway while retaining construction of full_url from the validated hostname string and passing that URL to ResilientHttpClient. causal_chain.bug_semantics: The unauthenticated static-download route passes request.getParameter("version") into BaseUtils.replaceFileNameAndExtension without validating it. For a request to the route base (/file/static/noauth in the renamed endpoint, formerly /downloadFile/static/noauth), the path-derived fileName is "noauth", whose full-path component is empty, so the helper replaces it entirely with attacker-controlled version. A value such as ../../etc/passwd is then handed to FileUtils.readFile(APP_DOWNLOAD_FOLDER_PATH, fileName, ...), which constructs new File(APP_DOWNLOAD_FOLDER_PATH, fileName) and can escape the intended download directory, exposing arbitrary readable files without authentication.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit b34987f7b37b5fd6a03b9dd9092bd18efc936d46 added version as a cache/content-identity filename override during a resources/web-client refactor. The normal producer generated an ID for version, but DownloadFileRequestHandler treated the HTTP parameter as if it were trusted and reused it as a filesystem child path. The already-existing security rule exempted /downloadFile/static/noauth/** from authentication, making this new trust-boundary error remotely reachable immediately.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: ZPan initialized its process-wide HS512 JWT helper with the public constant "123". A remote attacker who knows that repository-visible secret can sign a z-token whose subject and roles claim an administrator identity; LoginAuthWithRoles accepts the signature and then authorizes protected API routes from the attacker-controlled roles, bypassing password authentication.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 4fae6e2bdcab183ef59dd9f4055e2633ec2523f5 added the new user/token authentication subsystem. Its newly created internal/app/service/token.go made NewToken call jwtutil.Init("123") and used that same global helper to issue and verify RoleClaims; the same commit added the cookie-to-roles authentication middleware and protected-route role checks. The hard-coded signing key, rather than a per-installation secret, is therefore part of the original implementation of this authentication mechanism, not a later move or refactor of pre-existing vulnerable lines.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A remote ActivityPub Create/Note can supply an Emoji tag whose icon.url and name are attacker-controlled. NodeBB converted a matching shortcode into an img element by interpolating those values into quoted HTML attributes after the original note content had already been sanitized, then stored the generated HTML. Remote-post rendering could bypass markdown/sanitize-html, so an attribute breakout in the generated markup became persistent same-origin JavaScript for viewers.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 09b1e11940bebab92bbb48c8a1e1714fc9e95ea6 introduced incoming ActivityPub emoji expansion in src/posts/create.js before database storage and first wrote the causal unescaped sink, interpolating tag.icon.url directly into img src. Commit 3968c822a2291d32d79a86ba625858a90e8496f9 added the unescaped title attribute from tag.name one day later. Commit 9608cce693d43579b54ef2500133f0630f7a96c3 later moved/generalized the existing mechanism as Helpers.renderEmoji; it is a refactor, not the BIC.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated Project Manager or Owner can store a repository git_url beginning with Git's --upload-pack= option. The server-side schedule commit-hash poller passes that value directly after `git ls-remote` without an end-of-options delimiter; Git parses it as an option and invokes the attacker-selected upload-pack command through a shell, yielding command execution in the Semaphore server process.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit a30df1527e15c4c0060979bc2b7b120a8234111f changed GetLastRemoteCommitHash from running `git ls-remote origin <branch>` in the already-cloned repository to running `git ls-remote <Repository.GetGitURL()> <branch>` in the temporary directory. That single-line data-flow change first placed the stored, attacker-controlled GitURL in Git's option-parsing position; the existing makeCmd helper appended the arguments to exec.Command("git") without `--`.

The assigned GHSA-93jq-5gw9-rx3q is an unreviewed alias of that issue; NVD now marks assigned CVE-2026-73682 rejected in favor of CVE-2026-73294.

`git log -L ':GetLastRemoteCommitHash:lib/GitRepository.go' 40e018aaa19cdcd33e8e8882095b19926fb1db2e^` traces the vulnerable call to a30df1527e15c4c0060979bc2b7b120a8234111f. Thus the advisory's vulnerable URL-to-ls-remote flow is absent in the immediate parent and present in the BIC.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A client can issue XKB SetMap requests with XkbSetMapResizeTypes so that CheckKeyTypes() computes nMaps from the client-controlled sum firstType + nTypes but checks only a lower bound. After growing num_types to 255, a request with firstType=255 and nTypes=10 passes the firstType > num_types test because equality is allowed, computes nMaps=265, and writes mapWidthRtrn[i + firstType] for indices 255 through 264. The caller supplies the fixed 256-byte stack array mapWidths[XkbMaxLegalKeyCode + 1], so indices 256 through 264 overwrite nine bytes beyond it into adjacent stack state, permitting denial of service and potentially privilege escalation when the X server runs privileged.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The repository's initial X.Org R6.6 baseline commit ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1 added xkb/xkb.c with the complete vulnerable composition: a fixed XkbMaxLegalKeyCode+1 mapWidths stack buffer, client-controlled nMaps = firstType + nTypes with no upper bound, and the mapWidthRtrn[i + req->firstType] write. Whitespace/style changes and the 2010 zero-initialization of the same fixed-size array did not originate the mechanism.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A remote caller could supply an arbitrary HTTP(S) target in GET /api's url query parameter. PullMD passed that value to its server-side web extractor and returned the fetched content without rejecting loopback, private, link-local, CGNAT, or cloud-metadata destinations or revalidating redirect targets, so a request such as /api?url=http://100.100.100.200/latest/user-data could disclose cloud instance metadata and reach other internal services.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The root release commit wired req.query.url directly from server.js into extractWebFn(url), while lib/web.js wrapped globalThis.fetch only with a timeout and then called fetchFn(url, { headers }). It added no URL-scheme, hostname, DNS-result, IP-range, or redirect-hop policy between attacker input and the outbound request; that unsafe fetch design, rather than a later refactor or move, is the causal origin.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: When AUTH_ENABLED=true, an external request from outside INTERNAL_SERVICE_IPS that omits X-Internal-Service receives None from request.headers.get(), while an unset INTERNAL_SERVICE_SECRET also yields None from os.getenv(). is_internal_request() compared those values directly, so None == None returned true; verify_api_key() then created an unauthenticated internal principal with scopes ["all"], satisfying require_scope("admin") and exposing admin key creation, listing, and revocation. The bypass does not by itself pass the generate-master-key handler's additional is_master_key check.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An unauthenticated proxy client can put an arbitrary HTTP(S) origin in x-headroom-base-url. Headroom uses that origin as the upstream without establishing that its resolved addresses are public, forwards the incoming request headers and body to it, and returns the upstream response. A caller can therefore reach loopback, link-local/cloud-metadata, RFC 1918, and other internal services through the proxy and read their responses; the incoming Authorization header also follows the caller-selected destination. The reference compose deployment amplified reachability by publishing the proxy on 0.0.0.0 without requiring HEADROOM_PROXY_TOKEN.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 729cc035a474b4ff04c6c16c62d3a5f4e515c56f introduced the trust-boundary violation in headroom/proxy/server.py: the catch-all route read x-headroom-base-url and immediately passed custom_base.rstrip('/') to the pre-existing handle_passthrough method. That method copied all request headers except Host into the outbound request and relayed the response content/status/headers. The commit added no scheme, hostname, address-class, DNS, or operator-allowlist validation. Later commits moved the same catch-all mechanism and expanded it to dedicated OpenAI handlers; they did not originate the already exploitable SSRF.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: On a glamor-backed X server, glamor_font_get() sized a CPU-side font-atlas heap buffer and each glyph slot from the font's declared maxbounds, but copied each bitmap using that glyph's unchecked GLYPHWIDTHBYTES and GLYPHHEIGHTPIXELS metrics. libXfont2's PCF parser did not recompute maxbounds from the per-glyph records, so an authenticated X client could supply a PCF whose individual metrics exceeded (or were negative relative to) maxbounds; drawing text then made the row memcpy write attacker-controlled bytes beyond the allocated atlas, with negative values also permitting unsigned/size_t wrap.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 732e3b9c08532f40656010eac9d128601cc88c3f changed glamor_font_get() from issuing one glTexSubImage2D call per glyph to building one CPU heap staging atlas. It introduced bits = malloc(overall_width * overall_height), where overall_width/height came from maxbounds, together with a loop bounded by GLYPHHEIGHTPIXELS(glyph) and memcpy(dst, src, GLYPHWIDTHBYTES(glyph)) without checking those per-glyph dimensions against the maxbounds-derived slot. That new mismatch is the exact heap-buffer-overflow mechanism.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: When the optional webhook server is enabled, it listens on all interfaces and accepts POST requests containing an attacker-controlled exec string. Authentication is fail-open: WebhookServer.authenticate returns true whenever the configured token is empty, a state the configuration comments explicitly describe as 'empty = no auth'. The handler then dispatches req.Exec to a shell with -c/-Command. Thus an attacker who supplies a nonempty, reconstructable session_key (and a project when multiple projects are configured) can execute an arbitrary shell program as the cc-connect process without a credential. The shell interpretation of exec is an intentional feature; the security failure is exposing that full shell capability across a network endpoint while treating an omitted token as authorization.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The complete vulnerable mechanism originated in the single-parent feature commit 6ae088a658077a2f11a83ded6ac53c0dbddefd38: it created core/webhook.go, added the network listener and /hook handler, defined the JSON exec field, made an empty token authenticate successfully, passed exec to sh -c, wired the server into main, and documented an empty token as disabling authentication. This is the smallest repository-visible BIC, not the later shell-helper refactor.

The handler then dispatches req.Exec to a shell with -c/-Command. evidence: First-party report https://github.com/chenhg5/cc-connect/issues/1488 identifies core/webhook.go's empty-token authentication bypass, exec dispatch, all-interface listener, and shell sink; maintainer @chenhg5 replied on 2026-07-03 that the report was confirmed valid and described the same two-part chain. Source review adds an important reachability qualification: handleHook requires a nonempty session_key, resolveEngine must succeed, and executeShell must reconstruct the named platform context. Consequently, the issue's displayed curl body, which omits session_key, would be rejected at the required-field check, but adding a valid/reconstructable session key reaches the confirmed unauthenticated shell path.

`git show 6ae088a658077a2f11a83ded6ac53c0dbddefd38 -- core/webhook.go config/config.go config.example.toml cmd/cc-connect/main.go` shows one cohesive +503-line webhook feature. In core/webhook.go it creates WebhookRequest.Exec, starts http.Server at fmt.Sprintf(":%d", ws.port), routes POST /hook through authenticate, returns true for ws.token == "", dispatches req.Exec, and runs exec.CommandContext(ctx, "sh", "-c", req.Exec). config/config.go and config.example.toml state that an empty token means no authentication, while main.go starts the listener whenever webhook.enabled is true.

The BIC's newly added core/webhook_test.go makes the insecure policy explicit: TestWebhookServer_NoTokenRequired creates a server with an empty token and asserts authenticate succeeds. The same test file validates that exec is accepted as one of the two request action types, corroborating that no-token access and network-triggered exec were deliberately shipped together rather than accidentally joined by later history.

History searches `git log --all -S 'if ws.token == ""' -- core/webhook.go` and `git log --all -S 'req.Exec' -- core/webhook.go` each identify 6ae088a658077a2f11a83ded6ac53c0dbddefd38 as the first writer. The complete path log contains only the introducer, a later broad error-handling commit b9af7ea7ba641eb9278d45c9a19f361692acef44, and shell-configuration refactor 6feaf90f2f8cccec2203169b4d0edc3edd538837. The latter only replaces direct sh -c construction with shellExecCommand while continuing to pass req.Exec, so it preserves rather than introduces the vulnerable trust boundary.

Immediate-parent verification is direct: `git ls-tree -r --name-only 805045501b12fd3cf3834d19b0b882b32803e8c2 -- core/webhook.go` returns no path, and `git diff-tree --name-status 805045501b12fd3cf3834d19b0b882b32803e8c2 6ae088a658077a2f11a83ded6ac53c0dbddefd38 -- core/webhook.go` reports `A core/webhook.go`. Therefore the parent tree lacks the endpoint, empty-token bypass, request exec field, and webhook shell sink. The BIC is a one-parent public-DAG feature commit; no smaller reachable member commits exist to decompose.

Release-boundary check: v1.2.2-beta.1 resolves to ecea1ef36d86bb70dd633fb342f655d108ea52cb (2026-03-12) and lacks core/webhook.go, while the 2026-03-14 BIC is contained by v1.2.2-beta.2, which resolves to 9223201696e3f91b2f9fb456bba7dcef0a76bcd3 (2026-03-16). `git tag --contains 6ae088a...` starts at v1.2.2-beta.2 and includes v1.4.1.
