evidence: The assigned GHSA/CVE advisory describes the authorization failure for org.apache.artemis:artemis-stomp-protocol and identifies Apache PR https://github.com/apache/artemis/pull/6395 plus commit 53173375c4d5e4b57890e89d37ed8b666c974474; its published boundary is vulnerable through 2.53.0 and first patched in 2.54.0.

At fix parent 845339b1b66ecd7eac3dc07351cda850ee476d56, artemis-protocols/artemis-stomp-protocol/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/artemis/core/protocol/stomp/StompConnection.java:191-198 detects an existing address missing effectiveAddressRoutingType, adds the type to an EnumSet, and calls manager.getServer().updateAddressInfo directly. VersionedStompFrameHandler.java:190-198 invokes this path before STOMP SEND, while StompConnection.java:545-556 invokes it before SUBSCRIBE.

git show 53173375c4d5e4b57890e89d37ed8b666c974474 removes autoCreateDestinationIfPossible and routes both SEND and SUBSCRIBE through StompConnection.checkAutoCreate, which calls getSession().getCoreSession().checkAutoCreate. At that commit ServerSessionImpl.checkAutoCreate updates a missing routing type through createAddress, and ServerSessionImpl.java:1005-1012 performs securityCheck(..., CheckType.CREATE_ADDRESS, this) before addOrUpdateAddressInfo. The added StompWithSecurityTest cases require ERROR AMQ229032 for send-only and consume-only users requesting MULTICAST on an ANYCAST address and assert that MULTICAST remains absent.

git log -S'updateAddressInfo(simpleQueue, routingTypes)' identifies d773e8f66b5db2b0fcaa646384c24690d38aaa69 as the 2018-04-10 origin and ede2051960ddd6bf5657076fe5889f18a5699c6c as a later 2020 refactor; git log -L over the vulnerable method likewise traces the existing-address augmentation branch to d773e8f66b5db2b0fcaa646384c24690d38aaa69. In that BIC, StompConnection.java:296-297 contains routingTypes.add(effectiveAddressRoutingType) followed by updateAddressInfo.

Direct parent-tree verification: d773e8f66b5db2b0fcaa646384c24690d38aaa69 has the single parent e937c9903f9fa429c23fe50a3fd49e99ad2de0b9, and git grep at that exact parent finds neither updateAddressInfo nor routingTypes.add(effectiveAddressRoutingType) in StompConnection.java. The BIC diff shows the parent only handled addressInfo == null; unsupported types on existing addresses therefore reached checkRoutingSemantics and were rejected.

Version boundary verification: git grep finds no updateAddressInfo sink in StompConnection.java at tag 2.5.0, finds it at 2.6.0:297 and 2.53.0:197, finds it absent at 2.54.0, and finds the authenticated getCoreSession().checkAutoCreate call at 2.54.0:514. git tag --contains places d773e8f66b5db2b0fcaa646384c24690d38aaa69 first in 2.6.0 and places fix 53173375c4d5e4b57890e89d37ed8b666c974474 first in 2.54.0. ASF JIRA ARTEMIS-1794 also records the BIC feature's fix version as 2.6.0.

The GHSA's broad lower range begins at 2.0.0, but direct source inspection at tag 2.0.0 shows autoCreateDestinationIfPossible only creates through ServerSession when the address is absent and checkRoutingSemantics rejects a requested type missing from an existing address; the direct server update branch does not appear until 2.6.0. This is a documented advisory-range overbreadth, not evidence for an earlier BIC of this exact flaw.

audit_record.flaw_origin: Commit d773e8f66b5db2b0fcaa646384c24690d38aaa69 added the first existing-address/missing-routing-type branch to StompConnection.autoCreateDestinationIfPossible. audit_record.reasoning: The vulnerability is the authorization bypass in the existing-address routing-type augmentation, not generic STOMP auto-creation. Before the BIC, STOMP could auto-create a missing address through ServerSession (and its security boundary), but it did not mutate an existing address to satisfy a mismatched routing type; checkRoutingSemantics rejected that request. ARTEMIS-1794 commit d773e8f66b5db2b0fcaa646384c24690d38aaa69 deliberately enabled two STOMP routing types on the same address and introduced the smallest causal branch: it directly changed the broker's AddressInfo outside ServerSession authorization. The exact sink is absent from its immediate parent and is present beginning with release 2.6.0. Later refactors retain the same mechanism, so they are not introducers. causal_chain.bug_semantics: Bastillion's authentication filter was mapped only to /manage/* and /admin/*, while the lmvc controller dispatcher accepted any raw request URI containing an annotated controller path plus .ktrl. A request such as /anything/manage/viewUsers.ktrl therefore missed the prefix-scoped AuthFilter but was still substring-dispatched to the privileged /manage/viewUsers controller; unauthenticated attackers could read administrative data, create a MANAGER account, and register systems.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The flawed routing primitive was first written in the lmvc framework's 2018 initial source commit: BaseKontroller.execute() used request.getRequestURI().contains(c.path() + DispatcherServlet.CTR_EXT). Bastillion first integrated that framework in 65475902748be6b86a95d17b8409518697fe1e77 while retaining prefix-only AuthFilter mappings, making the mismatch exploitable in the application. Later package renames, artifact releases, and the 2026 source import merely carried the same line forward.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: When the image proxy is enabled, an authenticated poster can place an attacker-chosen non-HTTPS URL in a BBCode [img] tag. SMF's BBCode renderer converts that URL into a local proxy.php URL and generates the required secret-derived hash itself. A subsequent request to that local URL makes the forum server fetch the remote URL. Before the fixes, the fetch path did not resolve and reject private, loopback, link-local, or other reserved destination addresses on the initial request and every redirect, so an attacker-controlled hostname or redirect could make SMF request internal services, including link-local metadata endpoints.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The proxy fetch endpoint was already present in the immediate parent and required a secret-derived hash, but was not yet an attacker-usable signing oracle. Commit a892a53ba45330d69b8ad8b1ede82aebaa29537b completed the vulnerable mechanism by adding BBCode-renderer code that accepts the untrusted image URL and automatically emits /proxy.php?request=<url>&hash=md5(<url>.<secret>) without any destination-address validation. This is the smallest commit that made the pre-existing unvalidated server-side fetch reachable with a valid signature from attacker-controlled BBCode.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: ApproveAttach obtains the boards on which the authenticated user has approve_posts permission, but its per-attachment predicate uses assignment instead of comparison: $allowed_boards = array(0) || in_array(...) (later [0] and \in_array). Because || binds more tightly than =, the non-empty array(0)/[0] left operand is truthy, short-circuits the membership test, and assigns boolean true to $allowed_boards; every queried pending attachment therefore passes the authorization gate. A low-privileged authenticated caller can consequently approve, reject, or delete pending attachments outside boards they may moderate.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The vulnerable predicate predates the repository's accessible Git history. The sole Git root, a18e888838460a816fdbc2703e7e05ce7f626c91 (2012-01-24, message '10610'), is a 1,045-file whole-project snapshot and already contains the flawed line at Sources/ManageAttachments.php:1500. Later commits only preserve or move the same mechanism: 51ad4a4b2c1f7e292501f583d6defed62d56b535 renames ManageAttachments.php, 958840edad356bf237fd19790c36797d163cd383 extracts ApproveAttach into Sources/Actions/AttachmentApprove.php, a86ccb86190d867bd144a76a4c8d777e6c74a7b2 modernizes array(0) to [0], and 74e835324fbdbc594b2e67b068e548e541a163da qualifies in_array. causal_chain.bug_semantics: The reported mechanism is that POST /api/v1/invitation-code/redeem has no DeveloperDep or API-key dependency and treats an eight-character invitation code as the sole credential; a valid, unexpired, unredeemed code is looked up and exchanged for an SDK-scoped access JWT, a refresh token, and the bound user_id. Thus anyone who obtains a still-valid code can redeem it first. This is not actually missing authentication: the code was deliberately designed as a single-use bearer credential for standalone/mobile onboarding, and the CNA ultimately rejected CVE-2026-78154 as a false positive.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: PR #455 intentionally created the public bearer-code onboarding flow. Its first member commit 8d4ae726e100f72b6687f5a5678f624631c80e8a added backend/app/api/routes/v1/user_invitation_code.py with the public redeem handler and backend/app/services/user_invitation_code_service.py with the code lookup and SDK access/refresh-token issuance. The later squash landing d602dc9f01963e7e7bb9533122dc63368f4d69fd, revocation hardening, async-to-sync refactor, schema move, and documentation clarification did not originate the reported mechanism. The alleged flaw is therefore the original, explicit product design rather than a later accidental authentication regression.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: On an installation whose active cluster credential was the compiled-in default, any network client that copied the public source constant into X-WolfStack-Secret passed require_auth() as the synthetic cluster-node principal without a session, API key, or user account. That principal could call management endpoints, including POST /api/containers/{runtime}/{id}/exec, which passed attacker-controlled command text to sh -c inside the selected Docker or LXC container as root.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 2d2d371527bde1e9d72eadcd2ee3e7c0ee3adfbc replaced the parent implementation's per-node, randomly generated /etc/wolfstack/cluster.key with one source-published CLUSTER_SECRET shared by every installation and made load_cluster_secret() return that constant. The pre-existing request gate compared X-WolfStack-Secret with state.cluster_secret without any source-address or recorded-peer check, so this replacement converted possession of public source text into authentication.

audit_record.ai_marker: absent — the raw BIC commit object names human author and committer Paul C <paulc@wolf.uk.com> and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, AI attribution, or other trailer.

evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/wolfsoftwaresystemsltd/WolfStack/security/advisories/GHSA-r3mw-2wmq-j6jg states affected versions <=25.9.1, patched version 25.9.2, the any-source X-WolfStack-Secret bypass, the cluster-node identity, and the container exec impact. It limits affected configurations to nodes still using/falling back to the built-in default; nodes already rotated to a per-install secret were not affected.

git log -L 25,32:src/auth/mod.rs v25.9.1 and git log -S of the exact constant identify 2d2d371527bde1e9d72eadcd2ee3e7c0ee3adfbc as the first commit that writes CLUSTER_SECRET. Its focused diff replaces CLUSTER_KEY_PATH plus random UUID generation/persistence with the fixed source constant and CLUSTER_SECRET.to_string(); Cargo.toml changes 5.9.3 to 5.9.4 in the same implementation commit. An all-ref -S search found no earlier copy of the constant.

Direct parent-tree verification: git grep of the exact constant at a05c0870a84981d639067719de6be2395c958852 exits 1 with no match. parent:src/auth/mod.rs instead reads /etc/wolfstack/cluster.key, generates two random UUID-derived values when absent, persists the result, and chmods it 0600. Thus the public shared credential mechanism is absent in the immediate parent.

At the BIC tree, src/api/mod.rs require_auth() reads X-WolfStack-Secret, compares it against state.cluster_secret, and returns cluster-node on equality, with no peer/source check. At v25.9.1, src/api/mod.rs:7144-7153 shows POST /api/containers/{runtime}/{id}/exec guarded only by require_auth() before invoking sh -c with the supplied command.

Lifecycle history explains but does not replace the BIC: c8e3c7f08ba3c4a172e311ecd83b0419ebd4a6c1 temporarily removed the constant for a per-install secret in 11.26.3; 15772636355c6159d6c2dd6a608265ac65f4c208 restored it in 11.26.4 to repair inter-node communication. Because 15772636355c6159d6c2dd6a608265ac65f4c208 is a revert/reintroduction of lines first authored by 2d2d371527bde1e9d72eadcd2ee3e7c0ee3adfbc, it is not the smallest original BIC. Later custom-secret rotation retained the built-in value as a fallback, leaving unrotated/read-failure configurations exposed.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: ERC7984's encrypted uint64 total-supply update deliberately turns an overflowing mint into a zero transfer rather than reverting. ERC7984ERC20Wrapper's wrap and ERC-1363 callback paths transfer or have already received the underlying ERC-20 before calling _mint, ignore _mint's returned transferred amount, and still complete. Once confidential total supply is full, a user therefore pays underlying tokens but receives no wrapped confidential tokens.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The wrapper's incorrect success assumption originated in the first decomposed member of squash PR #11: it introduced both wrapper entry paths with an unchecked _mint after underlying custody had moved. causal_chain.bug_semantics: The remotely reachable GET /api/artifacts endpoint reads the attacker-controlled id query parameter and interpolates it into the path of a Cloudflare KV API URL. URL normalization resolves ../ segments before fetch sends the request, so seven traversal segments can escape /accounts/{account}/storage/kv/namespaces/{namespace}/values and select another Cloudflare API path under /client/v4. causal_chain.bug_semantics: Because app/mcp/actions.ts begins with the Next.js "use server" directive, its exported async addMcpServer(clientId, config) function is remotely invocable as a Server Action. The function performs no authentication, authorization, or ENABLE_MCP check; it persists the caller-controlled ServerConfig and immediately passes its command, args, and env to initializeSingleClient. That reaches createClient in app/mcp/client.ts, where StdioClientTransport launches the supplied executable when client.connect() runs, yielding unauthenticated remote OS command execution and persistence of the malicious server configuration.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 8aa9a500fdee762abe5fd8e0bba00065be1725f4 (feat: Optimize MCP configuration logic) is the smallest causal introducer: it first added exported addMcpServer to the already server-action-marked app/mcp/actions.ts and, in the same function, copied untrusted config into mcpServers, wrote it to disk, and called initializeSingleClient(clientId, config) without any access check. The pre-existing createClient process-spawn sink then made that new one-request path exploitable. Later commit 65810d918bb599716e35c8ea515a265da909cf2f changed status/async behavior but did not originate or remove the flaw.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An unauthenticated request to /api/<unrecognized-provider>/<path> reaches the provider route's default branch, which invokes proxyHandler. proxyHandler constructs fetchUrl by concatenating the entirely client-controlled x-base-url header with the requested path and query string, performs fetch(fetchUrl, ...), and streams the upstream response back to the requester. Because neither the fallback nor proxyHandler restricts schemes, hosts, loopback/private/link-local addresses, redirects, or allowed plugin origins, a remote caller can make the server request internal services, cloud metadata endpoints, or arbitrary external hosts and read the response, producing SSRF/open-proxy behavior.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit f652f7326070dfbffcc5f90a999e95df21f4c650 added plugin proxy/auth support as one single-parent commit. It created app/api/proxy.ts with the vulnerable x-base-url-to-fetchUrl data flow and, in app/api/[provider]/[...path]/route.ts, changed the switch so known OpenAI requests retain openaiHandler while every unknown provider is sent to the new proxyHandler. This made a feature intended to proxy configured plugin servers remotely selectable by any API caller without destination validation or authentication; the immediate parent had neither the proxy module nor this fallback.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: In non-export deployments, Next.js attaches Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * to every /api/:path* response and, by v2.16.1, also advertises wildcard methods and request headers. An attacker-controlled web origin can therefore read non-credentialed API responses and send normally preflight-restricted headers. In the reported high-impact chain, cross-origin JavaScript supplies x-base-url to the unauthenticated fallback proxy; app/api/proxy.ts builds the server-side destination from that header and injects the configured OpenAI key whenever the supplied value contains api.openai.com, allowing cross-origin SSRF and reflected key disclosure. The invalid Allow-Credentials: true plus wildcard-origin combination does not make credentialed wildcard fetches work in modern browsers, but credentials are unnecessary for the exposed read/proxy path.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 50cd33dbb2992066dae8c51c2da6ef4781e4500a first created nextConfig.headers for non-export builds and applied Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * (plus Allow-Credentials: true) to /:path*, thereby first granting every web origin read access across the application, including API routes. Its immediate parent had no response-header policy at all. Commit 0fb775d71a0fac5ce4aa802bc3eb0b066c12ed7b then scoped the rule to /api/:path* while widening Allow-Methods and Allow-Headers to * and adding a one-day max age, which intensified the later x-base-url attack but did not originate the permissive-origin flaw. Commit 6f83fbd21278c90cd978108abe54291c38ec10d7 only extracted the unchanged headers into CorsHeaders and is a move/refactor, not the BIC.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: When an administrator runs `fixfiles restore` or the non-full-cleanup path of `fixfiles relabel`, the DEFAULT restore path first has `find` select entries with an unlabeled or undefined SELinux context and then invokes a separate `chcon` process on each pathname. A local attacker controlling a searched directory can replace an intermediate path component with a symlink after `find` checks the entry but before `chcon` resolves the pathname. `chcon --no-dereference` protects only against dereferencing a symlink in the final pathname component; it does not prevent traversal through a swapped intermediate symlink, so the privileged process can change the SELinux label of an arbitrary target such as `/etc/shadow`.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The vulnerable find-then-chcon mechanism predates the repository's accessible Git history. The earliest relevant Git object, root commit 13cd4c8960688af11ad23b4c946149015c80d549, is explicitly an `initial import from svn trunk revision 2950` and already contains the `/tmp` and `/var/tmp` find/chcon commands. It has no parent and aggregates the prior Subversion history, so it is not the smallest BIC. Later commits changed details without creating the race: 5bd734dd7395a2f6c87546b8e7159b02544405f9 replaced hard-coded label types with `chcon --reference`, and 2608b4d6660af0fb8ad93f2cc144bdaab3c2afa8 added `--no-dereference` but retained the separate pathname lookup. The pre-r2950 Subversion changeset that first introduced the mechanism and its immediate predecessor are not present in the validated clone and could not be reconstructed from the available upstream history.

`git show --format=fuller a556538c2d5d2583273e025b45c02651fef47679` shows Stephen Smalley's direct upstream fix, `policycoreutils/scripts/fixfiles: drop /tmp cleanup`. Its patch deletes the vulnerable find/chcon block from policycoreutils/scripts/fixfiles, and its message explicitly explains that chcon re-looks up the full pathname and is subject to TOCTOU. `git rev-parse a556538c2d5d2583273e025b45c02651fef47679^` resolves the fix parent to 7fd20e48504069fe1541f809de7566283f8ec7db.

At 7fd20e48504069fe1541f809de7566283f8ec7db, policycoreutils/scripts/fixfiles lines in `restore()` show DEFAULT-mode find commands for /tmp, /var/tmp, /var/run, and /var/lib/debug executing `chcon --no-dereference --reference` on pathnames. The `process()` dispatch maps `restore` to `restore Relabel`; `relabel()` also reaches `restore Relabel` when /tmp is not fully deleted, proving the advisory attack path.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The PATCH /api/customers/:id endpoint is reachable without an authenticated admin or customer session and trusts the attacker-controlled path UUID as the record to update. Its only route-local middleware parses JSON; the handler selects that UUID, spreads attacker-controlled fields (including email and password) into the customer update, and returns the updated record without checking that the caller owns the customer, enabling unauthenticated account takeover and lockout.

The route then had no access property, so the new mutating handler was unauthenticated from its first executable revision. Commit 4b97829de4acc674cd2282af3d2b61ec3416f72b later changed the default to private but explicitly labeled this route public, preserving rather than originating the flaw.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: tcpliveplay accepts a user-supplied pcap, obtains an IPv4 header from libpcap's caplen-bounded packet buffer, and rewrites the packet before replay. fix_all_checksum_liveplay derives the TCP checksum length solely from the packet-controlled IPv4 total-length field (ntohs(ip_len) minus ip_hl) without proving that the claimed length fits the captured buffer. do_checksum_liveplay forwards that length to do_checksum_math_liveplay, whose loop reads successive 16-bit words until the claimed length is exhausted. A crafted pcap can therefore claim an IP length larger than caplen and make the checksum loop read past libpcap's heap buffer, causing the reported heap-buffer-overflow and denial of service.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 0b287ed9052f740ecb04df556dd07f03c4186e01 imported tcpliveplay.c as a new 1,303-line file and, in the same commit, added the complete vulnerable path: main calls rewrite on argv[2], rewrite consumes pcap_next_ex packet buffers and calls fix_all_checksum_newconn, fix_all_checksum_newconn trusts ip_len for the checksum length, and do_checksum_math_newconn walks that length without a caplen bound. Later commits only renamed the *_newconn helpers to *_liveplay or reformatted the same calculation, so the import commit is the smallest repository commit that first wrote the flawed mechanism.

audit_record.bug_semantics: tcpliveplay accepts a user-supplied pcap, obtains an IPv4 header from libpcap's caplen-bounded packet buffer, and rewrites the packet before replay. fix_all_checksum_liveplay derives the TCP checksum length solely from the packet-controlled IPv4 total-length field (ntohs(ip_len) minus ip_hl) without proving that the claimed length fits the captured buffer. do_checksum_liveplay forwards that length to do_checksum_math_liveplay, whose loop reads successive 16-bit words until the claimed length is exhausted. A crafted pcap can therefore claim an IP length larger than caplen and make the checksum loop read past libpcap's heap buffer, causing the reported heap-buffer-overflow and denial of service.
audit_record.evidence: Advisory lifecycle: GHSA-6cvx-mw62-87pq/CVE-2025-51005 and NVD identify tcpreplay 4.5.1, src/tcpliveplay.c do_checksum_math_liveplay, and a crafted-pcap heap-buffer-overflow; https://github.com/appneta/tcpreplay/issues/925 includes the ASan read at line 1175 and explains that ntohs(iphdr->ip_len) minus the IP-header length can be large. Decomposition: the BIC is a one-parent ordinary commit with no squash/member trailers; it imports an independently developed file (the file header credits Yazan H. Siam and dates it September 5, 2012), but the validated repository contains no smaller member SHA to decompose, so squash_decomposed is false and decomposed_shas is empty. audit_record.flaw_origin: Commit 0b287ed9052f740ecb04df556dd07f03c4186e01 imported tcpliveplay.c as a new 1,303-line file and, in the same commit, added the complete vulnerable path: main calls rewrite on argv[2], rewrite consumes pcap_next_ex packet buffers and calls fix_all_checksum_newconn, fix_all_checksum_newconn trusts ip_len for the checksum length, and do_checksum_math_newconn walks that length without a caplen bound. Later commits only renamed the *_newconn helpers to *_liveplay or reformatted the same calculation, so the import commit is the smallest repository commit that first wrote the flawed mechanism.
audit_record.reasoning: The vulnerability is reached before replay scheduling while rewrite processes the attacker's pcap: libpcap provides a finite captured buffer, but the imported checksum caller substitutes the IPv4 header's untrusted total length for the actual captured extent, and the checksum loop dereferences according to that larger value. Finally, the verdict uses only the BIC commit object: it has human author/committer Aaron Turner and no AI/bot/co-author/generated trailer. The source header's attribution to an earlier independent student project explains provenance but is not a commit-object AI signal. Therefore the closed causal verdict is NOT_AI.
audit_record.remaining_gap: Unpatched: no commit or release in the validated full history bounds attacker-controlled IPv4 ip_len by the pcap buffer's caplen before do_checksum_math_liveplay, so no fix_sha, direct_fix_sha, or patched version boundary exists to record. causal_chain.bug_semantics: HPE OneView exposes PUT /rest/id-pools/executeCommand without authentication. The controller deserializes attacker-controlled JSON into ExecutableCommand, passes exeCmd.getCmd() to RuntimeExecutorService.execute(), and that service calls Runtime.exec(command), giving an unauthenticated network attacker command execution in the appliance's unconfined Trusted RM Container context. The flaw is reachable only where the ID Pools endpoint is enabled.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The flawed mechanism originates in HPE's proprietary OneView appliance code, specifically guidserver.jar com.hp.ci.mgmt.guidpools.controllers.PoolController.executeCommand together with com.hp.ci.mgmt.guidpools.service.RuntimeExecutorService, not in rapid7/metasploit-framework. The assigned repository first added a post-disclosure exploit client for the already-existing HPE flaw; it contains neither the vulnerable HPE implementation nor the vendor fix history needed to select a real BIC.

The controller deserializes attacker-controlled JSON into ExecutableCommand, passes exeCmd.getCmd() to RuntimeExecutorService.execute(), and that service calls Runtime.exec(command), giving an unauthenticated network attacker command execution in the appliance's unconfined Trusted RM Container context. The flaw is reachable only where the ID Pools endpoint is enabled.
evidence: The HPE-authored CVE record at https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2025-37164 names HPE OneView as the affected product, marks versions less than 11.00 affected, and lists the rapid7/metasploit-framework URL only in CISA ADP enrichment with tag 'exploit'. It does not identify a source repository or commit.

Rapid7's first-party analysis at https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/ra-cve-2025-37164-analysis/ reports that the hotfix HPE_OneView_CVE_37164_Z7550-98077.bin adds 'RewriteRule ^/rest/id-pools/executeCommand$ - [R=404,L]' to /etc/httpd/conf.d/crypto/dynamic-ssl.conf. Its decompilation shows @DocAuthSpecial(SpecialAuthType.NO_AUTH), an optional Auth header, exeCmd.getCmd() flowing into runtimeExecutor.execute(), and Runtime.exec(command).

The same Rapid7 analysis demonstrates a PUT with attacker-controlled cmd returning HTTP 200 and an interactive shell as uid 1063 (trm3) with an unconfined SELinux context; it also explains that some non-6.x OneView VM editions do not enable ID Pools although the code is present.

Rapid7's mitigation article at https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/etr-cve-2025-37164-critical-unauthenticated-rce-affecting-hewlett-packard-enterprise-oneview/ states the vendor boundary as OneView 5.20 through 10.20, fixed by upgrading to 11.0 or applying the vendor hotfix. This verifies the product version boundary, but HPE publishes the remediation as a product release/binary hotfix rather than a Git commit.

In the assigned clone, exact search for com.hp.ci.mgmt.guidpools.controllers.PoolController and com.hp.ci.mgmt.guidpools.service.RuntimeExecutorService returned no matches. The clone contains an exploit module and documentation, not the vulnerable appliance classes.

git log --follow -- modules/exploits/linux/http/hpe_oneview_rce.rb shows the file first appears in a4dba967122de40dc3e4cba554dc4fa2be73ca48 (2025-12-19, 'add in the HPE OneView exploit'), whose immediate parent is 2bb30ba7a3eae4560a7e8ac34e09339804ddef2e. That is three days after the HPE CVE publication date 2025-12-16 and therefore cannot be the vulnerability introducer.

git diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-status -r a4dba967122de40dc3e4cba554dc4fa2be73ca48 reports both documentation/modules/exploit/linux/http/hpe_oneview_rce.md and modules/exploits/linux/http/hpe_oneview_rce.rb as added. git show of the Ruby file confirms it sends the malicious PUT to the HPE endpoint. This verifies only that the exploit module is absent from the Metasploit parent; it cannot establish absence of the vulnerable HPE lines from their unknown BIC parent.

Because no HPE source commit, parent tree, squash members, or source tag graph is available, git log -L/-S and direct-parent/tree verification for the real vulnerable lines cannot be performed in this repository. Likewise, neither the 11.0 remediation nor the binary hotfix has a public fix SHA that can be mapped to this clone.

Without those objects, parent absence and BIC-only AI attribution are genuinely unobservable.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Course-management authorization was enforced only by hiding navigation and buttons, not by guarding the management routes or the URL-controlled modal. A student who is a legitimate course member can supply a course ID and browse /courses/{id}/settings#share or /courses/{id}/people?add=true; the course layout admits any course member, the settings route renders its management component, and the add=true query value alone opens the invitation dialog containing tutor-selection and student invite-link controls.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The share/settings surface was already directly routable without a role guard when 103a2eda7b039f6ee1fb9ea524c41b0a85fe158e added src/routes/courses/[id]/settings/+page.svelte. causal_chain.bug_semantics: getRecommendTitleFromMarkdownString applies /#{1,6} {1,}(.*\S.*)(?:\n|$)/g to the complete Markdown string when choosing a filename during save/save-as. For a heading prefix followed by a very long run of spaces and then a newline, there is no required non-space character before the newline. The engine repeatedly repartitions that run between the adjacent ` {1,}` and `.*` repetitions and repeatedly scans for `\S`, producing super-linear (quadratic) backtracking and main-process CPU exhaustion before the save dialog can proceed.

Its sole original member commit ba9865a0fc7df8052b3cdd1b928aaa28215bcb64 first created the overlapping-quantifier failure mechanism in src/main/utils/index.js. causal_chain.bug_semantics: A crafted Juniper-Ethernet pcap can advertise unsupported extension media/encapsulation while still being long enough for dlt_jnpr_ether_decode() to treat the post-extension bytes as Ethernet. A successful en10mb subdecoder decode is followed by tcpedit_dlt_copy_decoder_state(), which assigns the subcontext-owned decoded_extra allocation directly to the outer context. Cleanup then traverses the outer context and the recursively owned subcontext; dlt_linuxsll2_cleanup() frees each context's decoded_extra pointer, so the aliased allocation is freed twice and tcprewrite aborts or corrupts memory.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 745a71184c9d739305d4319cf2e6bb3998cc27b6 introduced the Juniper subdecoder lifecycle as one cohesive feature: it created an en10mb subcontext, copied subdecoder state by borrowing the decoded_extra pointer without transferring or recording ownership, and recursively destroyed the subcontext during outer cleanup. It also continued to decode Juniper payloads as Ethernet without validating the extension-declared media type and encapsulation. Those combined lines first created the aliased-ownership double-free path; later aggregate/import commit 77387f1580220c1232a9091c79d0db83ba7ac5b0 merely reintroduced the already-existing mechanism into the 4.0 line.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The REST frontend registered an /engine-ui proxy whose request path supplied both the destination host and port. EngineUIProxyServlet parsed /engine-ui/<host>:<port>/..., then constructed and issued an HTTP request to that destination without an enable/disable gate or destination allowlist. A remote requester able to reach the proxy could therefore make the Kyuubi server contact arbitrary hosts reachable from the server, yielding SSRF/open-proxy behavior.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: AIT CSV Import/Export through 3.0.3 exposed admin/upload-handler.php as a directly reachable unauthenticated multipart upload endpoint. It neither restricted the uploaded file to safe CSV content/types nor prevented a PHP filename from being placed in WordPress's web-executable wp-content/uploads directory. Parsing could subsequently fail, but the file had already been retained; requesting that uploaded PHP file therefore produced unauthenticated remote code execution, even when the plugin was installed but inactive.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: ClassroomIO treated email-verification state and token contents as client authority. The profile table's existing own-row UPDATE policy allowed an authenticated user to set the newly added is_email_verified column directly through PostgREST. Independently, the emailed verification value was only Base64-encoded JSON containing a client-selected profileId and orgSiteName; /api/verify decoded it without a signature, expiry, one-time-use check, authenticated-user binding, or ownership check and used profileId in a privileged profile update. An attacker could therefore self-verify through the profile API or forge data for the verification endpoint to mark a chosen profile verified without controlling its mailbox.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: PR #215's first member commit, 69ba4c1a23504004f9d888312916862fb93003bf, created the verification-email route, the /api/verify route, and the profile verification columns. Member 947cfc06ca3a858972e8faafd096c7f662ef6086 later changed /api/verify to getServerSupabase, completing the arbitrary-profile service-role attack path, but it retained rather than originated the client-authoritative token and update mechanism. causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated Contributor who can create or edit a mep_events post can store quote-bearing payloads in event address fields (venue, street, city, state, postcode, and country) and related configurable registration labels. The save path used strip_tags() historically and later sanitize_text_field(), neither of which performs output-context encoding. Those stored values were subsequently returned from post/term metadata and inserted without escaping into single-quoted HTML value attributes and Google Maps iframe URLs (and labels into attribute contexts), so a quote could terminate the attribute and add an event handler that executes when a privileged user or visitor renders the affected event/admin page.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The vulnerable mechanism predates the assigned GitHub clone. Its root commit 644782aed278644a141d8d29ea5edfb4311ffad9 is a version-3.2.3/3.2.4 development import that already contains the raw metadata-return helper, so it is not the smallest real BIC. Decomposing that import through the plugin's first-party WordPress SVN history identifies SVN r1815482, represented by the full-history SVN-to-Git mirror commit 88a25a962d233d10851138f11d62b0b3160a9020, as the initial version-1.0 release that first added inc/mep_event_meta.php. That commit simultaneously stored the six address parameters using strip_tags() and echoed the stored values directly into quoted attributes; its immediate parent contains no mage-eventpress source.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated student who knows an enrolled course ID can request tutor/admin course routes directly. The application treats client-side navigation hiding and Svelte RoleBasedSecurity rendering/redirects as authorization, while route scripts and data services still execute course-ID-keyed reads without enforcing a tutor/admin role at the data boundary. As a result, all-course member profiles, attendance, submissions and answers, marks, and analytics can be returned before the client hides the slot or redirects, producing the advisory's transient sensitive-data disclosure.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: 07eba6b4e0838c8d7d44a133898f8aa4256cdd7b first established the flawed shared authorization mechanism: it added src/components/RoleBasedSecurity/index.svelte, derived the current role from client stores, and rendered its slot only when allowedRoles.includes(userRole); it also hid the Submissions navigation item for role 3 and wrapped admin UI in attendance, people, and submissions routes, but added no server/data-layer role check. Existing route scripts and Supabase services remained reachable and executed independently of that render-only gate, so a crafted course URL bypassed the intended role boundary.

It creates src/components/RoleBasedSecurity/index.svelte with only a client-store role lookup and {#if allowedRoles.includes(userRole)} slot rendering; it adds role-3 navigation hiding and wraps submissions/admin controls without adding any request-time authorization.

The same commit's attendance and people changes disable or hide controls client-side while their course data remains loaded.

Direct parent-tree verification: git cat-file -e '220f35b3db55f46bc42519b9e82d481c8325a3d6:src/components/RoleBasedSecurity/index.svelte' fails with 'path ... does not exist'; the BIC diff creates that file and introduces the role-based navigation/render checks. Thus the flawed client-only role boundary is absent from the immediate parent.
git tag --contains 07eba6b4e0838c8d7d44a133898f8aa4256cdd7b includes v0.1.0 through the advisory's v0.1.13 and later releases, proving the BIC predates and is contained in the affected release.

The repair is a three-commit linear sequence after v0.2.7: ac4fdf1dd35772a20899e36f5bf55decb1e0ebda migrates client Supabase course, people, submissions, marks, and related reads behind authenticated server endpoints and adds checkUserCoursePermissions; 97d9e490b00f8de355756bd6716d0b607b71712c updates the exercises endpoint and marks page; ac1a05f0068b638e18ed5473fd427506f64a7a1e moves course analytics to /api/courses/analytics and adds an authenticated permission check. git log --reverse v0.2.7..0.2.10 shows exactly that sequence.

Version boundary: git tag --contains ac4fdf1dd35772a20899e36f5bf55decb1e0ebda starts at v0.2.8, while git tag --contains ac1a05f0068b638e18ed5473fd427506f64a7a1e starts at 0.2.10. Therefore ac4fdf1 is the primary direct data-boundary fix and ac1a05f is the terminal fix SHA for the last named analytics route in release 0.2.10.

Existing route scripts and Supabase services remained reachable and executed independently of that render-only gate, so a crafted course URL bypassed the intended role boundary.
audit_record.reasoning: The vulnerability is an authorization-design failure, not merely a visible-navigation bug: course IDs are user-controlled route parameters, and hiding a link or a Svelte slot does not prevent the route script/data request from running. Earlier commits created individual course data reads, but 07eba6b is the smallest causal BIC for this advisory's shared role-bypass mechanism because it is the first commit that declared these functions/routes role-restricted while implementing that restriction solely in the browser across the named admin surfaces. Later Sapper-to-SvelteKit moves, the CourseContainer consolidation, and the May 2024 redirect cleanup preserve or refactor that mechanism and are not BICs. The immediate parent lacks the RoleBasedSecurity component and the newly introduced role-gating changes. The affected v0.1.13 tag contains the BIC. The December 2025 repair moves the sensitive reads to authenticated server endpoints in ac4fdf1, follows with marks/exercises adjustments, and closes the separately named analytics route in ac1a05f at 0.2.10. AI attribution is judged only from the BIC commit object: it has a human author/committer and no AI/bot trailer or marker, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated Lucee Web Administrator can create an HTTP scheduled task, then edit it with publish enabled and an attacker-chosen output file in the webroot. The scheduler fetches the remote response and copies it directly to that Resource without constraining the path or executable extension; naming the response .cfm turns attacker-controlled bytes into a server-executed CFML page running with the Lucee service account's privileges.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The vulnerable composition predates the recoverable commit history. The first public Railo Git snapshot split it across two import commits: 4b0d10b00807652c5b5b329dacdf417e8acdee63 added the administrator form that forwards url, publish, and arbitrary file values, and 99e969e528c6f5a9f726a229879a5e16a3112bdb added ExecutionThread's unrestricted HTTP-response-to-file write. The latter completes the visible mechanism, but it is a 2,414-file, 1,335,091-line source import rather than the real commit that authored the vulnerable code. Lucee later inherited the already-existing mechanism in its own root import 4e9afd8e48a71d89e7f34678edb7370c5d4b0b6c.

audit_record.ai_marker: unavailable: the smallest real BIC is behind the pre-2009 public-history boundary, so there is no BIC commit object whose author, committer, message, or trailers can be inspected; the visible import commit objects are not valid substitutes for BIC-only AI attribution
audit_record.bug_semantics: An authenticated Lucee Web Administrator can create an HTTP scheduled task, then edit it with publish enabled and an attacker-chosen output file in the webroot. The scheduler fetches the remote response and copies it directly to that Resource without constraining the path or executable extension; naming the response .cfm turns attacker-controlled bytes into a server-executed CFML page running with the Lucee service account's privileges.
evidence: NVD CVE-2025-34074 (https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-34074) describes the authenticated /lucee/admin/web.cfm path: fetch an attacker-controlled .cfm, write it to the webroot, then execute it as the Lucee service account; it identifies missing integrity checks, path restrictions, and execution controls.

The referenced Metasploit module (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rapid7/metasploit-framework/master/modules/exploits/multi/http/lucee_scheduled_job.rb) authenticates, creates a scheduled job, edits it with publish=true and file=<webroot>/<random>.cfm, executes the job, and requests that .cfm. Its metadata dates disclosure to 2023-02-10 and explicitly characterizes the behavior as inherent platform functionality.

In current Lucee, core/src/main/cfml/context/admin/services.schedule.edit.cfm passes publish=formBool('publish') and file=nullIfEmpty(form.file) to cfadmin; core/src/main/java/lucee/runtime/schedule/ScheduleTaskImpl.java only checks that the output is a file and its parent exists; core/src/main/java/lucee/runtime/schedule/ExecutionThread.java obtains task.getResource() and calls IOUtil.write or IOUtil.copy on the fetched response when publish is true.

In getrailo/railo public history, `git log --all --reverse -S'publish="#formBool' -- railo-cfml/railo-admin/admin/services.schedule.edit.cfm` and the analogous -S search for file=nullIfEmpty(form.file) both first return 4b0d10b00807652c5b5b329dacdf417e8acdee63 (2009-06-23, 'Initial version'). Its parent is 6b20542b4eeeec39064a4d38ea9fb88fa1d3fafe, and `git ls-tree` plus `git diff-tree --name-status` show the whole editor file absent in that parent and added by the commit.

`git log --all --reverse -S'IOUtil.copy' -- railo-java/railo-core/src/railo/runtime/schedule/ExecutionThread.java` first returns 99e969e528c6f5a9f726a229879a5e16a3112bdb, whose parent is 4b0d10b00807652c5b5b329dacdf417e8acdee63. Direct parent-tree verification shows ExecutionThread.java absent in the parent and added in 99e969e528c6f5a9f726a229879a5e16a3112bdb. The imported file performs an HTTP GET, takes task.getResource(), and copies the response stream to that resource whenever task.isPublish(), with no path or .cfm execution guard.

`git show --shortstat 99e969e528c6f5a9f726a229879a5e16a3112bdb` reports 2,414 files changed and 1,335,091 insertions under the generic message 'Initial version'. That aggregate import proves a public-history boundary, not a smallest real BIC. The preceding 4b0d10b00807652c5b5b329dacdf417e8acdee63 is likewise a 300-file, 20,455-line admin import. No earlier authoring commits are present to decompose.

Lucee root commit 4e9afd8e48a71d89e7f34678edb7370c5d4b0b6c (2015-09-11, 'initial commit') already contains the same publish and arbitrary-file controls, demonstrating inheritance rather than introduction in Lucee's repository.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: ClassroomIO loaded a course directly from the browser through Supabase/PostgREST and requested the course's entire group, every groupmember row, and every related profile. An authenticated student could therefore send or alter a request to GET /rest/v1/course with the same bearer token and nested select projection and receive other students' and staff profiles plus course/group metadata; UI role checks did not constitute server-side authorization.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 60f06d6ab1468dd276ba4b95fe9478d4f95ce3e7 first added src/utils/services/courses/index.js and its browser-side fetchCourse query: .from('course').select(...) included group(*, members:groupmember(*, profile(*))). Its immediate parent has neither that file nor any .from('course') query under src. Later moves and query expansion preserved the same mechanism, while permissive RLS imported in 2023 and course-member RLS added in 2025 failed to distinguish a student from staff when exposing nested course relations.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A locally supplied truncated pcap (wire length greater than captured length) processed by tcprewrite --fixlen pad reaches untrunc_packet, which reallocates the packet buffer and may free its old address. tcpedit_packet has already cached packet and IP-header aliases into that old allocation and does not rebase them after untrunc_packet returns; its later DLT merge path calls dlt_en10mb_l2len/get_l2len/get_l2len_protocol through the stale packet address, producing the reported heap use-after-free read (and other post-padding paths could likewise use stale header aliases).
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14 changed untrunc_packet from padding the caller-provided buffer in place to safe_realloc(packet, pkthdr->len), and changed the API/caller to pass u_char **pktdata, but tcpedit_packet continued retaining its pre-call local packet, ip_hdr, and ip6_hdr aliases. In that original commit untrunc_packet did not even assign the new packet back through *pktdata; b58b23a52ffd23c3b1a2e2fe8b868aff0239560d later added *pktdata = packet but still did not rebase tcpedit_packet's cached aliases, so it did not cure the causal stale-pointer mechanism. The smallest first-writer is therefore 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14, not the later headroom adjustment 64132c54c4000046b30f1fc3fe612db9b2f26860.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An unauthenticated client first requests /login.php to obtain an ICTBroadcast session cookie, then replaces the cookie value (observed as BROADCAST, although the applicable cookie name can vary) with shell metacharacters such as a backtick command substitution. ICTBroadcast passes the attacker-controlled session identifier into a shell-backed session-log command of the form sh -c echo "... Session read requested with id: <cookie> ..." >> gui.log. Because the cookie is not shell-neutralized, the shell evaluates the embedded backticks; a payload that base64-decodes and pipes a command to sh therefore executes arbitrary commands as the web-service account before authentication.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The causal flaw is in ICTBroadcast's product-side session read/logging implementation: it interpolates the untrusted cookie/session identifier into a shell command merely to append a diagnostic log line. The assigned rapid7/metasploit-framework repository does not contain that product implementation; it contains only a later exploit module and its documentation. ICTBroadcast's corresponding proprietary source repository and revision history are not publicly identified, so the commit that first introduced the shell interpolation cannot be reconstructed from this clone.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated user could bypass the profile image input's client-side accept hint and submit an SVG File. The profile flow uploaded the supplied bytes unchanged to the public Supabase avatars bucket, merely naming the object with a .webp suffix, then persisted its public URL. Directly viewing that stored object from the trusted storage origin caused JavaScript embedded in the SVG to execute, yielding stored XSS.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 05ed2b74ee25aaeddefc62121202ee97ed8637f0 introduced the profile-avatar upload end to end: a new UploadImage component accepted a File without validating its MIME type, extension, or contents, and src/routes/profile/[id].svelte uploaded that untrusted File directly to the public avatars bucket and stored its URL. The accept=".jpg, .jpeg, .png" attribute was only a browser file-picker hint, while forcing a .webp object name did not decode or transcode the uploaded bytes.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The public reproducer invokes tcpreplay with `-p -0.000001`. `tcpreplay_post_args` parses that nonzero string with `atof`, so the later `if (!n)` guard does not reject it, then scales it by 3600 and casts -0.0036 to the integer `COUNTER`, producing a zero packets-per-hour value. The packet-rate branch of `calc_sleep_time` subsequently divides its next-transmit-time numerator by that zero `pph`, raising SIGFPE and terminating the local replay process.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Single PR-member commit fb5c9c21064e799c8b77c61e282d39ea853e77b9 changed `--pps` from AutoOpts `arg-type = number` to an unrestricted string, parsed it with `atof`, stored `(COUNTER)(n * 60 * 60)` without validating sign/range or the post-conversion integer, and changed `calc_sleep_time` to divide by the resulting packets-per-hour value. Its immediate parent could not take the advisory's fractional string through this conversion path. The member was squash-landed as 175f7ed06c6ad6488020220f9917ca213c568251; a 2021 exact-zero check in ebed7dde22ef3b77ceb64eefa2c873b92b435dda did not repair negative or positive nonzero fractions whose scaled integer is zero.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: OpenClaw's ZIP extractor constructed an output path under the extraction directory, checked path and symlink state, and only afterward opened that pathname for truncating/writing. A local attacker able to mutate the extraction tree could replace a checked parent directory with a symlink during that gap, causing an entry such as slot/target.txt to resolve outside the extraction root and clobber the external target. O_NOFOLLOW protected only the final path component; it did not bind parent resolution to the object that had been checked.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Original feature implementation. Commit 3a6ee5ee00176c88aee32bb8bfd543780014c079 first added the production ZIP extractor in src/infra/archive.ts with lexical containment checking followed by mkdir and fs.writeFile(outPath, data). Subsequent streaming and symlink-hardening commits changed the sink but preserved the same check/use separation; in particular 4b226b74f5fd3b106a83a6347fd404172e2fd246 added parent checks and O_NOFOLLOW on the leaf without making parent traversal race-safe.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A tenant allowed to create or update Fission Function or Environment CRDs can put SYS_TIME in securityContext.capabilities.add on a tenant-controlled container or init container. The v1.24.0 admission validator and executor merge sanitizer reject only six named capabilities (SYS_ADMIN, NET_ADMIN, SYS_PTRACE, SYS_MODULE, DAC_READ_SEARCH, DAC_OVERRIDE), so SYS_TIME passes both layers and reaches the resulting pod. Without PSA restricted on the function-pod namespace, CAP_SYS_TIME permits clock_settime(CLOCK_REALTIME) against the node-wide, non-time-namespaced real-time clock, corrupting wall-clock-dependent state for co-tenants.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Incomplete remediation: PR #3391 introduced a fixed six-capability denylist while closing earlier PodSpec privilege-escalation advisories. The first PR member, 2db76f65dbfe4f657b4a4efb506ed63b24623e92, created dangerousCapabilities and deliberately allowed every capability outside that enumeration; later member c8a58b7a88448f55bdf3ff01e149e82370fcfd7d copied the same incomplete policy into the merge sanitizer. The underlying unconstrained SecurityContext merge already existed in the parent, but this advisory's specific flawed mechanism is the newly written, incomplete denylist defense.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated user who can create and execute workflows can stage a Git working repository whose configured push remote is another crafted local repository, then invoke the Git node's push or pushTags operation. Vulnerable releases permit the file transport for those write operations. The local git-receive-pack process runs receive-side hooks from the crafted target repository as the n8n process user. The earlier core.hooksPath=/dev/null mitigation protects hooks in the initiating working repository but does not suppress hooks in a local receive-pack target, so the result is arbitrary command execution on both self-hosted and cloud instances.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The public merge 3667b0dd01f82046549b795b98b88983bd7c7fbb is a squash of PR #1820, not the true BIC. Fetching refs/pull/1820/head and walking its member history identifies f81e76aca958dab7392942e8a74b7919e7db42b5 (:sparkles: Add Git-Node) as the smallest commit that first creates Git.node.ts, accepts a caller-selected base directory, constructs simple-git with default transport/hook behavior, and exposes git.push() without a file-transport restriction. Its direct parent 06dd4236482d345b1193b87b993c944b117698bd has no Git node file.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Whirlpool compatibility setup searched interpreter-controlled purelib, platlib, and user-site directories with broad whirlpool*.so, pywhirlpool*.so, whirlpool-py311*.so, and analogous .pyd globs, selected the first filename match without authenticating its bytes, created an importable whirlpool ABI-name symlink/copy to that match, and imported it. A matching attacker-planted native extension in a searched site-packages directory therefore executes its native initializer when openssl_encrypt imports crypt_core and setup_whirlpool runs. A later registry implementation added a second, even more direct Python-3.13 path that takes the first whirlpool*py313*.so match and executes it with ExtensionFileLoader.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: cb07e5f88a98f4459a5f828142e740c024810692 is the earliest causal first-writer: it created openssl_encrypt/modules/setup_whirlpool.py with the unauthenticated broad globs, first-match selection, symlink/copy, and subsequent import, and wired setup_whirlpool() into crypt_core's import path. f6770c1e774ff46a591257c1e62063f39a6f568b later independently duplicated the same trust failure in registry/hash_registry.py; it is the commit blamed for the exact advisory excerpt but is not the lifecycle BIC because the exploitable loader already existed.

audit_record.ai_marker: The BIC commit object itself contains both exact markers: '🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)' and 'Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>'. Author and committer are Tobi <tobster@brain-force.ch>; no later commit or PR metadata is needed for attribution.

The later exact advisory sink is independently attributable with `git log --all --reverse -S'whirlpool*py313*.so' -- ...`, which returns f6770c1e774ff46a591257c1e62063f39a6f568b; `git blame -L 565,590 v1.4.0 -- openssl_encrypt/modules/registry/hash_registry.py` shows f6770c1e7 authored the first-match ExtensionFileLoader/exec_module path. audit_record.flaw_origin: cb07e5f88a98f4459a5f828142e740c024810692 is the earliest causal first-writer: it created openssl_encrypt/modules/setup_whirlpool.py with the unauthenticated broad globs, first-match selection, symlink/copy, and subsequent import, and wired setup_whirlpool() into crypt_core's import path. f6770c1e774ff46a591257c1e62063f39a6f568b later independently duplicated the same trust failure in registry/hash_registry.py; it is the commit blamed for the exact advisory excerpt but is not the lifecycle BIC because the exploitable loader already existed.
audit_record.reasoning: The root cause is not Whirlpool hashing itself but trusting filename/location heuristics as authentication for native executable code. cb07e5f88 is the smallest true BIC because its new compatibility helper established the complete search-select-link-import attack path; the later f6770c1e registry code is a second sink, not a move and not an earlier origin. The immediate parent directly lacks both the helper and any equivalent glob/native-loader mechanism. Because the BIC's own immutable commit message explicitly says it was generated with Claude Code and co-authored by Claude, and that BIC creates the vulnerable trust decision rather than merely carrying or refactoring it, AI_ROOT_CAUSE is warranted. The advisory's 963d0d1 remediation is not a closing fix for its stated attacker model: an attacker-planted .so physically inside a searched site-packages directory passes the new realpath containment check, and the exact registry ExtensionFileLoader sink is untouched. audit_record.remaining_gap: Released versions remain unpatched for the advisory's stated arbitrary matching-file-in-site-packages attack model as of the clone history: no tag contains the complete fix fdb5d72999914f5604a419225949db669d4be3f2, and v1.4.0 through v1.4.9 retain the exact direct loader. A remote unauthenticated caller that causes or observes a database failure can therefore receive driver and connection details, including database hostnames, IP addresses, ports, parameters, versions, and potentially credentials embedded in an error.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: PluginImportGuard.restore_hidden_modules() restored entries, cleared self.hidden_modules, and only then logged len(self.hidden_modules), so every restoration audit event falsely reported zero. causal_chain.bug_semantics: IndexFile.from_tree appends caller-controlled treeish values after its own --index-output=<temporary-index> argument and invokes git read-tree without an unsafe-option guard or option/operand separator; reset delegates its caller-controlled commit to from_tree, while merge_tree appends caller-controlled base and rhs values to another unguarded read-tree invocation. Supplying --index-output=<attacker-chosen-writable-path> is therefore parsed as an option, and Git's last-occurrence-wins behavior overrides from_tree's temporary path, replacing the chosen file with a valid DIRC git-index blob. The attacker controls the destination, not arbitrary replacement bytes, yielding destructive arbitrary file overwrite rather than code execution.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A plugin executing without PluginCapability.READ_FILES was supposed to be confined to the sandbox temporary directory and explicitly safe paths. The sandbox enforced that policy only by replacing builtins.open with restricted_open. Plugin code could instead import pathlib or io and call pathlib.Path.read_text/read_bytes/write_text/write_bytes/open or io.open; those independent entry points never reached restricted_open, so the plugin could read or modify arbitrary host files, for example Path('/etc/passwd').read_text(), despite lacking the file capability. The repository advisory specifically describes the bypass in threading mode and notes that process isolation had a separate broader restriction failure.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef is the smallest public first-writer: it creates plugin_sandbox.py and the plugin subsystem, advertises file-system capability enforcement, but _restrict_file_operations patches only builtins.open. Its single parent 649f737a9f04645508d079c0c772a8a2b4c7457a has no plugin_sandbox.py at the affected path. Later commits 642fb2bdec8af6f1d592c322dfa98647e145fcef, 35499f201ae2dc531d1194f6810c953d8b9af78b, and ccb60e1a29ef67700128ca54eb25a95413d71ff1 revise restoration, allowed-path context, and AST validation while retaining the builtins-only restriction, so they are carriers/hardening changes rather than introducers.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A repository-controlled .gitmodules section name is parsed unchanged by sm_name(), assigned to Submodule._name, and, on Git versions using gitfile submodules, joined to <parent git dir>/modules. A name containing ../ components therefore escapes that directory. During submodule initialization, GitPython creates parent directories and clones with --separate-git-dir at the escaped location, allowing a malicious repository whose otherwise tree-validated submodule path is legitimate to create and populate a Git repository at an attacker-chosen filesystem path.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc introduced _need_gitfile_submodules() and _module_abspath(), whose modern-Git branch returned os.path.join(parent_repo.git_dir, 'modules', name), and changed update() to use that name-derived path for directory removal and Repo.clone_from(). The already-existing iter_items() flow obtained name by slicing the attacker-controlled .gitmodules section header with sm_name() and performed no validation. This commit created the first name-to-filesystem sink; later commit 67680a0877f01177dc827beb49c83a9174cdb736 refactored cloning into _clone_repo() and added --separate-git-dir but was not the first vulnerable implementation.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Stored same-origin XSS in the Form node completion page: renderFormCompletion always retrieved responseText and passed it to packages/cli/templates/form-trigger-completion.handlebars, whose triple-brace {{{responseText}}} sink rendered attacker HTML verbatim. Commit 7f651ca5a3162ba0f13242dc934047e32998b33c changed the formerly unconditional sandbox Content-Security-Policy into a respondWith !== 'redirect' conditional without also suppressing responseText for redirect responses. An authenticated member could retain populated responseText while making the expression-capable respondWith parameter evaluate to redirect; a public-form submitter then received the raw HTML without the sandbox CSP, so script ran from the n8n origin with the visitor's session context.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The smallest causal change is 7f651ca5a3162ba0f13242dc934047e32998b33c (fix(n8n Form Node): CSP headers should not be set on response with redirect (#20864)). It introduced a local respondWith variable and guarded res.setHeader('Content-Security-Policy', SANDBOX_CSP) with respondWith !== 'redirect', while deliberately leaving the pre-existing unconditional responseText read and raw template sink intact. This newly created the exploitable combination; it is a focused two-file implementation/test commit, not a move, refactor, revert, release/backport, or broad squash aggregate.

audit_record.reasoning: Before the BIC, responseText was already intentionally raw HTML, but the completion response always received SANDBOX_CSP; therefore attacker script was confined to the sandbox rather than executing as the n8n origin. causal_chain.bug_semantics: The unified FastAPI server supplied two publicly known, >=32-character defaults for KEYSERVER_TOKEN_SECRET and TELEMETRY_TOKEN_SECRET. validate_config() checked only length and cross-module inequality, so an operator who did not override the environment variables started the production server with those known HS256 signing keys. TokenAuth.verify_token() accepted a JWT when its signature and module issuer matched and returned the attacker-chosen sub/client_id without requiring that client to exist, allowing source-aware attackers to mint bearer tokens that passed the keyserver or telemetry route dependencies.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 8170b3e0be064cdaddbc8ef51c17e21c42d2d3f4 created the entire openssl_encrypt_server tree and, in the same atomic commit, added both hardcoded JWT defaults, the insufficient length-only startup validation, the HS256 encode/decode path, and the authenticated route wiring. This is the first writing of the vulnerable mechanism, not a move, refactor, revert, release commit, or merge.

A value such as --file=/path/secret is consequently parsed by Git as the tag-message file option, creates an annotated tag, and returns the file contents in-band through tagref.tag.message. Commit 3af0c251 later added a default unsafe-option check, but it called Git._option_candidates([], kwargs), so the positional path and reference were outside the check while keyword spellings were blocked.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated user who can run a workflow can supply crafted Edit Image / Draw Text input. The node line-wraps that value and passes it unchanged to gm.drawText(). gm 1.23.1 encloses text in an MVG quoted string and escapes double quotes but not attacker-supplied backslashes. A backslash can therefore alter the escaping of a following quote, terminate the intended text primitive, and inject another MVG primitive, causing GraphicsMagick to make a blind outbound request to an attacker-selected address or open a local file.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The @n8n/computer-use search_files tool accepted an attacker-influenced fast-glob pattern. It checked only the literal input for a leading slash or a slash-delimited '..' segment, then trusted fastGlob's expanded path strings for both filename results and content reads. A brace pattern such as '{a,..}/SECRET.txt' contains no literal '..' segment, passes assertPatternStaysInside(), but can expand to '../SECRET.txt'; path.join(resolvedDir, fp), fs.stat(), and fs.readFile() then access a file outside the configured base. An actor able to influence this tool call can disclose names and contents of arbitrary local files readable by the n8n daemon user.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: GitPython's unsafe-option guards reconstructed candidate options from kwarg names but did not inspect a single-character kwarg's value. causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated member who can edit a shared workflow can put a credential ID belonging to another user into an HTTP Request node and make genericAuthType (or the analogous nodeCredentialType) an expression that resolves to the real credential type only at execution time. CredentialsPermissionChecker statically computes active credential types from unresolved node parameters. The expression text is not equal to the credential object's real type key, so mapCredIdsToNodes drops the referenced credential and the project ownership/access query never sees its ID. The HTTP Request runtime later resolves the expression and loads that credential, allowing its use or exfiltration; the attacker must know the victim credential ID.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The smallest source commit is PR #25599 member 7d6023fe3478df86d88f3602f1ea5b53819a050b. It changed mapCredIdsToNodes from unconditionally mapping every node.credentials value to first computing getActiveCredentialTypes and then continuing past any credential whose type is not in that statically derived set. The new helper evaluated display conditions and copied the unresolved nodeCredentialType string, but did not fail closed for expressions. That created the authorization gap: an expression-selected credential could be active at runtime yet absent from the pre-execution permission query. The public squash merge 608e3bf214328e679c03da3e4a6e9c22ceaac9ca is not the smallest BIC; GitHub's public PR-commits endpoint reconstructs its two source commits. Later bundle 2d9a2ec76e180b54e8091e31b1e0638c909abd99 added raw genericAuthType to the same set, preserving rather than originating the expression mismatch.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: In the Microsoft Teams message handler, groupPolicy="allowlist" was meant to enforce both route admission and sender admission. When a configured channels.msteams.teams team/channel route matched but effectiveGroupAllowFrom was empty, the handler treated the route match as sufficient: the original condition skipped the empty-sender-allowlist rejection, and a later semantics-preserving refactor made that bypass explicit by passing ["*"] to evaluateSenderGroupAccessForPolicy. Consequently any sender in a matched Teams route could reach conversationStore/dispatch and trigger a reply despite not being sender-allowlisted.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Budibase automation actions accepted an automation-supplied URL and made a server-side HTTP request without applying the outbound IP blacklist. This allowed an automation author to target loopback, private-network, link-local/cloud-metadata, or other internal services. The related REST datasource check was also opt-in because an unset BLACKLIST_IPS produced an empty list. A first automation patch checked only the initial URL, so node-fetch's automatic redirects could still reach a blacklisted address; the closing patch manually followed redirects and checked every destination.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 3ae82b95a31bcb6b3803d3ad8d8c5accb7606ef3 first added the OUTGOING_WEBHOOK automation action and its run function, taking inputs.url and passing it to server-side axios with no address policy. The immediate parent has neither the file nor an outgoing-webhook request path. Commit 3d77163773d0ab37342e9e2be5d6b8797758e4eb merely replaced axios with node-fetch and is not the BIC; later Slack, Zapier, Discord, Make, and n8n actions replicated the already-existing flaw.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: TemplateContext.Reset() cleared output, global, culture, and source-file state but left the per-context CachedTemplates dictionary intact. IncludeFunction.Invoke() resolves an include through TemplateContext.GetOrCreateTemplate(); a cache hit returns the previously compiled Template without calling ITemplateLoader.Load(). An application that pools or reuses a TemplateContext across requests, users, or tenants can therefore prime an include under one authorization context and, after Reset(), expose that stale include content to a later context.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Direct atomic commit 2e95889099c3ee5e7a4c0147b7355ecd309200af added the public safe-reuse boundary TemplateContext.Reset() but omitted CachedTemplates.Clear() even though the cache and cache-hit include path already existed in its immediate parent. The vulnerability begins with this Reset contract, not with the older intentional within-context include cache; the commit is neither a move, refactor, revert, merge, nor squash aggregate.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: TemplateContext.GetMemberAccessor cached one accessor per runtime Type, while TypedObjectAccessor captured the context's then-current MemberFilter and eagerly precomputed the exposed field/property set. After a permissive render populated that cache, resetting and reusing the same TemplateContext under a tighter MemberFilter returned the stale permissive accessor. ScriptMemberExpression therefore continued to read, and potentially write, members that the later sandbox policy denied, enabling cross-request or cross-tenant policy bypass when contexts were reused.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit ace7a0ebafa6d01500f83c35975cde38d559fa3d added TemplateContext.MemberFilter and threaded it into the precomputed TypedObjectAccessor without changing the existing Dictionary<Type, IObjectAccessor> cache key or invalidation behavior. That commit is the first one in which a Type-only cached accessor can embody a context-specific filter policy.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: TemplateContext.LimitToString bounded only one ObjectToString conversion, not the cumulative rendered template. TemplateContext.Write(SourceSpan, object) converts each rendered expression through a fresh top-level ObjectToString call; ObjectToString resets _currentToStringLength whenever _objectToStringLevel is zero; and StringBuilderOutput.Write appends every resulting chunk without a cumulative cap. A template can therefore make a 1,048,575-character string, render it in each of the default 1000 loop iterations, pass the 1,048,576-character per-call limit every time, and accumulate roughly 1 GB in the output StringBuilder until the host process runs out of memory.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95 (Add TemplateContext.LimitToString) introduced the vulnerable safety mechanism: it added _currentToStringLength and reset it to zero at every top-level ObjectToString call, while leaving the already-existing output sink cumulative-unbounded. The older unconditional StringBuilderOutput append is a precondition, but b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95 is the smallest commit that created the advisory's LimitToString-bypass combination; b5ac4bf30459fdc76964e3f751e16f7e96079ea7 later changed the default LimitToString from disabled to 1,048,576 and made the bypass present under default 6.6.0 settings rather than introducing the reset.

The bundle maps that first-party advisory to CVE-2026-74786 / GHSA-w7vg-5328-m33q.

In the assigned clone, `git show b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95 -- src/Scriban/TemplateContext.Helpers.cs src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs` shows one focused non-merge commit adding LimitToString, _currentToStringLength, and exactly `if (_objectToStringLevel == 0) { _currentToStringLength = 0; }`; it initializes LimitToString to 0 and does not add cumulative accounting to the output path.

Both required history searches converge on the same BIC: `git log --all --reverse -S'_currentToStringLength' -- src/Scriban/TemplateContext.Helpers.cs src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs` returns b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95 as the first addition, and `git log b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95 -L 85,88:src/Scriban/TemplateContext.Helpers.cs` attributes the entire four-line top-level reset to that commit.

Direct parent verification: `git cat-file commit b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95` names sole parent d4d64f8f15df9683ec0d51d4906edc4b3cef5ff5. `git show d4d64f8f15df9683ec0d51d4906edc4b3cef5ff5:src/Scriban/TemplateContext.Helpers.cs` has _objectToStringLevel but has neither _currentToStringLength nor LimitToString nor the reset; ObjectToString simply increments the nesting level and returns ObjectToStringImpl. causal_chain.bug_semantics: The default object.to_json builtin recursively serializes IList/array elements and object members through a static local WriteValue function without a recursion-depth limit, execution-stack guard, or circular-reference detection. A template can create a ScriptObject that points to itself and pass it to object.to_json; WriteValue then revisits the same object until .NET raises the fatal, effectively uncatchable StackOverflowException, terminating the host process. Deep acyclic input can exhaust the stack by the same path.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The vulnerable ToJson/WriteValue implementation was first written in PR #533 member commit a65c891245e2c8550fb28fcd6e9d296c99ad6a2f. GitHub landed PR #533 as the one-parent squash f2f3cf41cde1ba7226760fd9b456f3d5d7aa1ca1, but the retained eight-member PR chain and identical head/squash trees permit decomposition; the second member is the smallest commit that adds object.to_json and both unchecked recursive calls.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Scriban's object-to-string rendering recursively formats every ScriptObject member value without tracking object identity. With the default ObjectRecursionLimit of 0 (unlimited), a ScriptObject that directly or indirectly contains itself repeatedly re-enters ObjectToString until the CLR throws an uncatchable StackOverflowException, terminating the host process and enabling denial of service wherever an attacker can influence the rendered object graph.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e is the smallest real introducer: it added the ScriptObject-specific pretty-print branch to ScriptValueConverter.ToString and the recursive call result.Append(ToString(span, keyPair.Value)). Its parent only handled ScriptObject through the generic IEnumerable path and did not recursively extract a KeyValuePair's Value, so the advisory PoC's self-referential ScriptObject path was absent. Later commits moved/refactored the formatter; a9affb64614358838aba16f28acb198f914e586d added an opt-in recursion guard but explicitly initialized ObjectRecursionLimit to 0, preserving the vulnerable default rather than introducing the already-existing recursion.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated remote caller controls baseUrl in POST /api/provider-nodes/validate. The route passes baseUrl-derived URLs to server-side fetches and forwards the caller's apiKey as Authorization credentials. assertPublicUrl parses the URL, but its IPv4-mapped IPv6 check expects a dotted quad after ::ffff:, whereas WHATWG URL parsing canonicalizes that input to hexadecimal hextets first. Thus mapped loopback and link-local literals such as http://[::ffff:7f00:1] and http://[::ffff:a9fe:a9fe] pass the guard and reach internal services. The custom-embedding path reflects the first 200 response bytes for non-2xx responses other than 401/403; the other paths expose blind status/timing/port-scan signals. /api/provider-nodes is protected by dashboard authentication by default, but dashboardGuard permits access when requireLogin=false.
