causal_chain.bug_semantics: A browser page on an attacker-controlled DNS name can rebind that same origin to the victim's loopback Paperclip server. Because Paperclip did not reject the attacker's Host header and the default local-trusted behavior treated requests without credentials as an instance-admin board actor, the page could create a company and a process-adapter agent with attacker-controlled command/args, then invoke the agent heartbeat/wakeup route; the server passed that configuration to child_process.spawn as the Paperclip OS user, yielding drive-by command execution.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: abadd469bc85e9fa5137ff5ffce433f1c2db2c0b is the first commit that completed the exploitable mechanism: it mounted an actor middleware which assigned every unauthenticated request a board actor, added board-accessible company/agent creation and heartbeat invocation routes, and added the process execution service that spawned attacker-controlled command and args, all without Host validation. The parent had only CRUD agent routes and no auth middleware, heartbeat service, invocation route, or command sink. e1f2be7ecff711f2f5db9a0f64dbd3133df4410e later named/defaulted the same implicit-admin behavior as local_trusted; 85c0b9a3dc3795bf33646ef128ad070181c7abec later added a hostname guard but enabled it only for authenticated/private deployments, preserving the already-existing local-trusted flaw rather than introducing it.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The API scope middleware derives write versus read permission solely from the HTTP method and therefore treats every GET as read-only. The GET runner registration-token handlers are not read-only: shared.GetRegistrationToken calls NewRunnerToken when no active token exists and returns the usable token. A leaked read:user token (or the corresponding read-scoped owner/repository token) can consequently mint or obtain a runner registration credential, register an attacker-controlled Actions runner, and receive workflow work exposing source and repository secrets.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The vulnerable GET-plus-create design first appears in PR #27144 source member eec5ed07521ffc767c0dd1bdccdece8a7f54fe3f, which added the shared state-mutating handler and reachable organization/admin GET routes; member bba250f3e99bef12bbd9a1d9d790ab8155c999d5 then added the user and repository GET routes. GitHub squashed the 22-member PR into mainline aggregate baf0d402d9cb47849394202fcfc7c2e23b0faac3, so that aggregate is not the smallest BIC.

evidence: Mechanism: at the BIC tree, `grep` of https://raw.githubusercontent.com/go-gitea/gitea/eec5ed07521ffc767c0dd1bdccdece8a7f54fe3f/routers/api/v1/api.go shows tokenRequiresScopes initializes `requiredScopeLevel := auth_model.Read` and changes it to Write only for POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE (lines 241-264). `gh api repos/go-gitea/gitea/commits/eec5ed07521ffc767c0dd1bdccdece8a7f54fe3f --jq` shows its new routers/api/v1/shared/runners.go calling GetUnactivatedRunnerToken and, on missing/inactive token, NewRunnerToken, then returning the token; its api.go patch registers GET organization and admin registration-token routes. Thus the state change was reachable through a request authorized as read from the first causal source commit.

Attack path: `routers/api/actions/runner/runner.go` Register lines 41-103 accepts the supplied registration token with actions_model.GetRunnerToken, rejects only missing/inactive tokens, creates an ActionRunner scoped by the token OwnerID/RepoID, and returns the runner's operational token. This directly connects the disclosed GET token to registration of an attacker-controlled Actions runner; the advisory/NVD description records the resulting workflow access to repository source and secrets.

Mainline trace and squash: `git log --all -S'm.Get("/registration-token"' -- routers/api/v1/api.go` identifies baf0d402d9cb47849394202fcfc7c2e23b0faac3 as the addition and 716a800f500348e10a663ad749398d230c5bb7ad as the removal; `git log -L 1048,1048:routers/api/v1/api.go 716a800f500348e10a663ad749398d230c5bb7ad^` traces the user GET line to baf0d402d9cb47849394202fcfc7c2e23b0faac3. `gh api repos/go-gitea/gitea/pulls/27144` reports 22 commits, head f0e7edf97244ec02c4e07213043a6a676ca5364f, base 4c29c75968f520123f125e8305b2c29198664251, and merge_commit_sha baf0d402d9cb47849394202fcfc7c2e23b0faac3, proving baf0d402... is the squash aggregate.

Decomposition: `gh api 'repos/go-gitea/gitea/pulls/27144/commits?per_page=100'` lists eec5ed07521ffc767c0dd1bdccdece8a7f54fe3f first. `gh api repos/go-gitea/gitea/commits/eec5ed07521ffc767c0dd1bdccdece8a7f54fe3f` shows that member adding routers/api/v1/shared/runners.go plus the organization/admin GET routes. The same endpoint for bba250f3e99bef12bbd9a1d9d790ab8155c999d5 shows the later user handler and both user/repository GET route additions. eec5ed... is therefore the earliest and smallest already-vulnerable member, while bba250... only expands the affected scopes.

Direct parent absence: the Git commit object for eec5ed07521ffc767c0dd1bdccdece8a7f54fe3f names sole parent 24a215e317103471aeb864f365089a36076efc1d. `gh api 'repos/go-gitea/gitea/contents/routers/api/v1/api.go?ref=24a215e317103471aeb864f365089a36076efc1d' --jq '.content | @base64d | contains("/registration-token")'` returns false, and requesting routers/api/v1/shared/runners.go at that parent returns HTTP 404. The mainline squash parent independently has no matching route or handler: `git grep -n 'registration-token\|GetRegistrationToken' 4c29c75968f520123f125e8305b2c29198664251 -- routers/api/v1` returns no matches.

Version boundary: `git grep -n 'registration-token' v1.21.11 -- routers/api/v1/api.go routers/api/v1/shared/runners.go` returns no matches. At v1.22.0, `git grep -n 'm.Get("/registration-token"\|requiredScopeLevel := auth_model.Read\|NewRunnerToken'` finds the read-default classifier, three GET routes, and the token creation call, so v1.22.0 is the first affected stable release. `git tag --contains baf0d402d9cb47849394202fcfc7c2e23b0faac3 --sort=version:refname` likewise starts at v1.22.0.

Fix and closing boundary: `git show 716a800f500348e10a663ad749398d230c5bb7ad` (PR #36801, 'Remove API registration-token') deletes all GET registration-token routes and their GET handlers while retaining the separate POST creation API; its sole parent is 7889b78c8736a8a03bff423f7dfb535ac15281d7 and still contains those GETs. `git tag --contains 716a800f500348e10a663ad749398d230c5bb7ad --sort=version:refname` starts at v1.26.0-rc0 and then v1.26.0. `git grep -n 'registration-token' v1.26.0 -- routers/api/v1/api.go` shows POST routes only, establishing v1.26.0 as the first fixed stable release.

Referenced-tag caveat, directly verified: despite appearing in the advisory references, v1.25.5 is not fixed. `git grep -n 'm.Get("/registration-token"' v1.25.5 -- routers/api/v1/api.go` returns the repository/owner, user, and admin GET routes; `git tag --contains 716a800f500348e10a663ad749398d230c5bb7ad` does not include v1.25.5. The reproducible code/tag boundary is therefore affected v1.22.0 through v1.25.5, fixed in v1.26.0 stable.

BIC-only AI check: `gh api repos/go-gitea/gitea/git/commits/eec5ed07521ffc767c0dd1bdccdece8a7f54fe3f` returns author and committer Lunny Xiao <xiaolunwen@gmail.com> and the one-line message 'Add get actions runner registration token for API routes, repo, org and global level'. The exact source-member commit object has no Co-authored-by trailer, Generated-with trailer, bot identity, Copilot attribution, or other AI marker. The later squash object's human trailers and the fix object's metadata are not used for the verdict.

First-party closure: GitHub PR #36801 is the direct removal PR and merged as 716a800f500348e10a663ad749398d230c5bb7ad on 2026-03-02. Its discussion explicitly focuses on the GET-only endpoints and the existence of POST creation endpoints, matching the deletion diff and the method/scope mismatch described by CVE-2026-24059/GHSA-M7QQ-F4RG-V5M5.

audit_record.reasoning: The vulnerability was already real in the first PR source member: scoped-token middleware predated it and classified its GET as read, while that GET could create and disclose a registration credential. Because PR #27144 was squashed, the mainline commit is only an aggregate; decomposing the PR makes eec5ed07521ffc767c0dd1bdccdece8a7f54fe3f the smallest BIC, with direct parent absence proven. bba250f3e99bef12bbd9a1d9d790ab8155c999d5 expanded the same flaw to the headline user and repository routes but did not originate it. The direct fix removes the unsafe GET surface, and tag contents establish the actual first-fixed stable version independently of the advisory's anomalous v1.25.5 reference. The BIC commit object is wholly human-attributed and contains no AI marker, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated non-site-admin user with perm_template could request the event-template add page (or edit a writable template), causing EventTemplatesController::__setBuilderConfig() to fetch every enabled Galaxy row without the Galaxy visibility conditions. The resulting galaxy type and description values were JSON-embedded in window.ET_BUILDER_CONFIG, disclosing private, organisation-only galaxy metadata belonging to other organisations.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 47bf71cc78d13c06e1eaa4d9842e6f94ddce4bea introduced the galaxy-type picker and its server-side Galaxy::find('all') query with only 'Galaxy.enabled' => true. causal_chain.bug_semantics: A scoped access token carrying only profile:read is accepted by PUT /user because that state-changing route is guarded with RequireScopes(ScopeProfileRead). UpdateUser derives the target from the token viewer, checks only that the target user is an administrator, and permits a supplied password to replace the administrator password. The attacker can then log in with that password; login issues a session-typed JWT, and RequireScopes deliberately bypasses all scope checks for session tokens, yielding an unrestricted administrator session.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: PR #195 introduced the scoped-token authorization feature. Its atomic member b47fa1c75d890cd080e3f6699bbfca8cd8d4b939 first wrote the security-significant mismatch in internal/router/user.go by binding the write-capable PUT /user handler to ScopeProfileRead. GitHub later squashed the PR into main as 3f8fb150158723aca31df2ae937a1aa7b31ac254; that aggregate is a carrier, not the smallest BIC.

JWT authentication supplied the admin user's identity, and the comment service's requireAdmin check verified only the database role, not token capabilities, so the limited token could list comment/setting data and approve, reject, hot-mark, batch-modify, delete, or change/test comment settings.

Those routes were not a scope bypass before scope-limited credentials existed. PR #195 was squash-landed as 3f8fb150158723aca31df2ae937a1aa7b31ac254; decomposition identifies bf994ebfd5fe2e16b85ff64ad25147abd9ba99d7 as the smallest true BIC because it first defined comment and other scopes and changed CreateAccessToken to accept, validate, embed, and persist caller-selected scopes while the nine existing comment routes remained unguarded. Its parent 387667192911c86db1e1bcb3f544ce12d340ffdb had typed session/access JWTs but no Scopes/Audience fields in AccessTokenSettingDto and minted only unscoped access tokens. causal_chain.bug_semantics: Second-order Oracle SQL identifier injection in the post-CREATE/post-UPDATE row lookup. Oracle table names are read verbatim from user_tables.TABLE_NAME and carried into the external-table query metadata. When Oracle returns response.lastRowid, OracleIntegration.query constructs SELECT * FROM "<table name>" WHERE ROWID = '<driver-produced ROWID>' by direct interpolation. An embedded double quote in the table name terminates the quoted identifier and makes the remainder SQL syntax. A user able to write that external table can trigger the lookup; the injected SQL runs with the configured Oracle datasource user's privileges and can cross Budibase's table/row authorization boundary. response.lastRowid is not the attacker-controlled part.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: 115fc08aa4d08ca08c65c84e3805c6df0e1ea0b8 is the smallest real origin: it replaced the prior returning implementation with a post-write ROWID lookup and first wrote the raw quoted-identifier interpolation, initially using json.endpoint.entityId. At that revision ExternalRequest derives endpoint.entityId directly from tableName, while Oracle schema introspection stores row.TABLE_NAME verbatim, so the original line already has the same identifier-injection semantics. dbe9eedcbadc6d164447078039801a53a2dcfa65 later changed the expression from json.endpoint.entityId to json.table.name but preserved the unsafe double-quote interpolation; it is a source-name rewrite, not the BIC.

evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/Budibase/budibase/security/advisories/GHSA-xj29-x47g-9w2c names packages/server/src/integrations/oracle.ts's post-write ROWID SELECT as the sink, explains that json.table.name comes from user_tables.TABLE_NAME, identifies the embedded-double-quote attack, declares affected <3.40.0 and patched 3.40.0, and describes quoteOracleIdentifier as remediation.

In the read-only clone, `git show 115fc08aa4d08ca08c65c84e3805c6df0e1ea0b8 -- packages/server/src/integrations/oracle.ts` shows that this commit adds the response.lastRowid branch and `sql: `SELECT * FROM \"${json.endpoint.entityId}\" WHERE ROWID = '${response.lastRowid}'``. `git log -S'WHERE ROWID' -- packages/server/src/integrations/oracle.ts` identifies 115fc08aa4d08ca08c65c84e3805c6df0e1ea0b8 as the introduction; `git log -L 430,439:packages/server/src/integrations/oracle.ts 115fc08aa4d08ca08c65c84e3805c6df0e1ea0b8` likewise attributes the new lookup to that commit.

At the BIC, `git grep -n 'entityId: tableName' 115fc08aa4d08ca08c65c84e3805c6df0e1ea0b8 -- packages/server/src/api/controllers/row/ExternalRequest.ts` returns lines 162 and 646. `git show 115fc08aa4d08ca08c65c84e3805c6df0e1ea0b8:packages/server/src/integrations/oracle.ts` lines 155-208 shows schema SQL selecting from user_tables and mapColumns assigning `const tableName = row.TABLE_NAME` and storing `{ name: tableName }`. These establish the original sink's identifier source rather than relying on the later variable name.

Direct parent check: `git grep -n -E 'lastRowid|WHERE ROWID|json\.endpoint\.entityId' 78de4719482c86e7d4178b9445eb82acd16cc5d1 -- packages/server/src/integrations/oracle.ts` returns no matches. The BIC commit object has exactly one parent, 78de4719482c86e7d4178b9445eb82acd16cc5d1, so this is direct parent absence rather than inference from a release diff.

Lifecycle persistence: `git show dbe9eedcbadc6d164447078039801a53a2dcfa65 -- packages/server/src/integrations/oracle.ts` changes only the identifier expression in this sink from `${json.endpoint.entityId}` to `${json.table.name}` and leaves it raw inside double quotes. `git log -S'SELECT * FROM "${json.table.name}" WHERE ROWID' -- packages/server/src/integrations/oracle.ts` then shows dbe9eedcbadc6d164447078039801a53a2dcfa65 adding that exact spelling and 36c9d61de69957243f121883aed07f44951dfcaa removing it.

Closing fix: `git show 36c9d61de69957243f121883aed07f44951dfcaa -- packages/server/src/integrations/oracle.ts packages/server/src/integrations/utils/sqlIdentifiers.ts` adds `quoteOracleIdentifier`, implemented as a double-quoted identifier with every embedded `"` replaced by `""`, and changes the sink to `SELECT * FROM ${quoteOracleIdentifier(json.table.name)} ...`. This one-parent, two-file commit directly closes the identifier breakout; it is not merely a release/version commit.

Introduction release edge: `git grep -n -E 'lastRowid|WHERE ROWID' v0.9.190-alpha.9 v0.9.190-alpha.10 -- packages/server/src/integrations/oracle.ts` has no alpha.9 match and shows the vulnerable lookup in v0.9.190-alpha.10. `git for-each-ref --contains=115fc08aa4d08ca08c65c84e3805c6df0e1ea0b8 --sort=creatordate refs/tags` shows v0.9.190-alpha.10 as the first containing tag, followed by stable v0.9.190 and v1.0.0.

Observed fix tag edge: `git tag --contains 36c9d61de69957243f121883aed07f44951dfcaa --list '3.*' --sort=version:refname` begins at 3.39.25. `git grep -n -E 'SELECT \* FROM|quoteOracleIdentifier' 3.39.24 3.39.25 -- packages/server/src/integrations/oracle.ts packages/server/src/integrations/utils/sqlIdentifiers.ts` shows the raw interpolation in 3.39.24 and the helper plus quoted call in 3.39.25. The corresponding release commits are 3c86b6ab5d3f36c2bb668d6b44a17cfc32082785 (3.39.24) and a5c08bf7d989e531cc54f640a504fe9306cdfe1b (3.39.25). Tag 3.40.0 resolves to 661fe55d609404d073eea86702e0bde7942c3f10 and also contains the fix. Thus the advisory's supported/public boundary is 3.40.0, while the frozen Git tags demonstrate that the code fix first shipped in 3.39.25.

BIC-only AI check: `git cat-file -p 115fc08aa4d08ca08c65c84e3805c6df0e1ea0b8` shows human author and committer `Rory Powell <rory.codes@gmail.com>`, one parent, subject `Improve returning logic for oracle`, and no body trailers at all. causal_chain.bug_semantics: Scoped access tokens are JWTs for an admin user and are supposed to enforce least privilege, but authorization was split between authentication, opt-in route scope middleware, and service-level IsAdmin checks. A deliberately narrow admin token such as echo:read therefore authenticated to privileged routes that omitted RequireScopes, including /api/inbox and /api/panel/comments. The public /api/backup/export route was worse: its handler accepted a query JWT, parsed it, and rebuilt a viewer with only claims.Userid, discarding typ, scope, audience, and JTI, after which the backup service saw an admin identity and returned a full database/log ZIP.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The scoped-token capability first became real in decomposed PR #195 member bf994ebfd5fe2e16b85ff64ad25147abd9ba99d7: it added Scopes/Audience to the token-creation DTO, validated and persisted them, and minted JWTs with those claims, while the contemporaneous authentication middleware still reduced every parsed JWT to viewer.NewUserViewer(mc.Userid) and existing privileged routes had no scope guard. A later member, 1b280c252d1ef2ee69bf09f890d2da673b4b0a68, preserved token metadata in the viewer, and b47fa1c75d890cd080e3f6699bbfca8cd8d4b939 added RequireScopes only to echo/file/setting/user routes, leaving the advisory's privileged surfaces unguarded. causal_chain.bug_semantics: Budibase's datasource read APIs returned the stored datasource config to an authenticated caller. The later removeSecrets control only replaced fields declared PASSWORD (and, from May 2026, SENSITIVE_LONGFORM), while MongoDB connectionString and Firestore privateKey remained declared STRING. Consequently GET /api/datasources/:datasourceId, authorized only for TABLE/READ in affected code, returned a live MongoDB URI or Firebase service-account private key in plaintext; the builder-only list/read responses were affected by the same schema/redactor mismatch.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The complete exploitable path first appears in merge-resolution commit 29b51bc6c2fc8874ab7aa7a0c849ff5f205aec5a: it creates the datasource controller and a TABLE/READ GET /api/datasources/:id route, and find performs database.get(id) followed by ctx.body = datasource with no secret removal. MongoDB's STRING connectionString already existed from fbf501aebc0a4b16e5715e0b4fc875a4998f319b, so 29b51bc6c2fc8874ab7aa7a0c849ff5f205aec5a is the smallest first commit that completed the low-privilege disclosure path. Firebase commit c2d48bebd7100d7949de4555759de543a00b9256 later added privateKey as STRING. Partial-redaction commit b659060beb4246ad943b4660fb06f7a823d12a3d routed reads through removeSecrets but masked only PASSWORD fields, preserving rather than originating the already-exploitable leak.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Ech0 installed internal/i18n.Middleware() on the global Gin router, so every unauthenticated request supplied its raw, trimmed Accept-Language header to NewLocalizer. NewLocalizer passed that unbounded value directly to go-i18n, whose tag parsing reaches golang.org/x/text/language.ParseAcceptLanguage. The x/text CVE-2022-32149 guard counts '-' separators but the scanner also aliases '_' to '-', so a near-1 MiB header made from malformed underscore-separated subtags bypasses the guard and exercises quadratic gobble/memmove behavior. The same unbounded parser was also reachable through X-Locale and the lang query parameter via ResolveLocale, with those explicit-locale paths potentially adding another parse. This is an unauthenticated CPU denial of service on public routes.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Application-boundary flaw first created by b55edabd228d3de41e781bd3100f2e1ee0835516: that single ordinary commit added the i18n implementation, directly forwarded acceptLanguage to goi18n.NewLocalizer, read Accept-Language from the request without a size/shape bound, and globally registered the middleware. The underlying parser behavior pre-existed in dependencies, but Ech0's remotely reachable unbounded data path did not exist in the immediate parent.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Authenticated users remain inside their configured filesystem scope but can bypass administrator path deny rules because authorization compares the uncanonicalized virtual path literally while the backing filesystem resolves an equivalent name differently. On case-insensitive filesystems, a case variant such as /secret.TXT names denied /Secret.txt without matching its case-sensitive rule. On Windows, a mixed-separator traversal such as /allow\..\Secret.txt likewise misses the slash-based rule while filepath/afero resolves it to the denied file. The affected operations include reads and, subject to the user's ordinary permissions, modification, deletion, copying, and sharing; internally generated OS-separated paths also caused nested recursive/archive checks to miss rules on Windows.

Commit 41828f18050c3e90fc54ea2468324246b45e7d85 then activated that primitive at the HTTP resource gate and directory-listing checks. The regression first shipped in 3.39.4. causal_chain.bug_semantics: The authenticated TUS PATCH endpoint appended the entire request body with io.Copy even after the server had parsed and cached the Upload-Length declared at upload creation. The cached length was consulted only after the write to decide that an upload was complete. A create-capable user could therefore declare a 1 KiB upload and stream an arbitrarily large PATCH body, which was fully written before HTTP 204, allowing disk exhaustion. The fix bounds each write to Upload-Length minus Upload-Offset, rejects an already-excessive offset, and truncates and returns 413 when the body is over-length.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The smallest causal commit is PR #5270 member 6337c4452529dfc018885a7d05cc4f1e217316c5, not its later GitHub squash 0f27c91eca581482ce4f82f6429f5dac12f8b64e and not the 2023 commit that originally added io.Copy. Member 6337c4452529dfc018885a7d05cc4f1e217316c5 first parsed Upload-Length, registered that accepted length, retrieved it in PATCH, and compared newOffset against it only after the pre-existing unbounded copy. Before that member, the endpoint had an unbounded upload operation but no accepted/cached per-upload declared bound; consistent with the first-party advisory's out-of-scope distinction for uploads without such a bound, that older behavior is not this specific bypass.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: In filebrowser v2, an authenticated user confined to an otherwise-authorized scope but configured with Perm.Download=false can send GET /api/resources/<same-scope-file>?checksum=md5|sha1|sha256|sha512. resourceGetHandler invokes FileInfo.Checksum, which reads the file, and renderJSON returns the digest without checking Download. This bypasses only the Download permission, not scope/path authorization: it exposes a content-hash oracle usable for known-content confirmation, change detection, or offline guessing of low-entropy content, and forces a full-file read. The vulnerable v2 implementation is present from v2.0.0-rc.1 (and stable v2.0.0) through v2.63.18; v2.63.19 closes it.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The canonical master landing 12b2c215221696de58431093e01eeff7a5414471 ('feat: v2 (#599)') is a one-parent aggregate of the v2 pull-request history, not the smallest BIC. Decomposing the still-public refs/pull/575/head history identifies member 42227d9edd7ce613e8b6c0ad62c8cad16cf77266 ('feat: many updates (see PR)') as the first writer: in one patch it creates types/user.go with Permissions.Download and creates http/resource.go with the /api/resources checksum branch, which calls file.Checksum and returns JSON without consulting that new permission. Its direct parent c01ebf33efed835680373668e54d9ddafc90a6b1 has neither the v2 /api/resources handler nor any Download permission, so the bypass is semantically absent. causal_chain.bug_semantics: When no password was configured, check_auth deliberately authorized every request, including POST /api/settings. The settings writer nevertheless accepted the private _set_password field, hashed it into persistent password_hash, and thereby enabled authentication with an attacker-chosen password. A remote unauthenticated client reaching the WebUI during first run could therefore claim ownership, then authenticate with that password; from 8b857d9efc121586f2ef79ca4b8f92d8ad373b5b onward the same bootstrap response also created and returned a valid session cookie immediately.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: b8b62722ec2f6b3cd394737ab409c35650f29ca6 introduced the complete unsafe bootstrap primitive in one ordinary commit: api/auth.py made all routes pass while auth was disabled and exposed public password login, server.py applied that middleware, and api/config.py made save_settings consume _set_password and persist password_hash without a local-origin gate. The pre-existing generic POST /api/settings route supplied the remotely reachable sink.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The withdrawn report alleged that, after beginning an OAuth sign-in and reaching an OTP challenge, an attacker could alter the attempt request's authentication strategy (for example, swap an email-code attempt to another factor) and have the server complete authentication without the correct code. The public clerk-js 5.88.0 UI does send the factor strategy and entered code to the Frontend API, but that client-controlled request is not an authentication trust boundary; the alleged bypass requires the server to accept a strategy that was not valid for the sign-in attempt. The CNA later rejected CVE-2025-63700 because further investigation established that this was not a security issue.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: No verified flaw exists in the audited repository. The allegation depended on improper state/factor validation by Clerk's non-public Frontend API backend, while clerk/javascript only constructs and sends the client request. The relevant client request behavior predates 5.88.0 and was unchanged by that release, and the authoritative CVE record plus Clerk's first-party vulnerability history state that the report was investigated, withdrawn, and never a real vulnerability.

audit_record.reasoning: The report's proposed attack crosses the browser/server boundary: changing a browser request is always possible, so a bypass exists only if the Frontend API fails to bind an OTP attempt to the prepared factor and sign-in state. The public SDK at 5.88.0 passes the UI-selected factor strategy and code to that API, but contains no server-side authentication decision. Git diff shows 5.88.0 did not introduce the relevant request path, and git log -L shows the generic path existed years earlier. There is no closing patch or first patched package version; 5.89.0's OTP work only changes the input UI. Most decisively, on 2025-12-23 the CNA withdrew the CVE after determining it was not a security issue, and Clerk's first-party history says it was never a real vulnerability. Since no true BIC exists, there is no parent-absence claim and no BIC commit object on which an AI marker may be judged. EVIDENCE_GAP is used rather than NOT_AI because a closed NOT_AI verdict requires a real BIC; it is used rather than BLOCKED because the repository and public lifecycle are accessible, but the reachable evidence does not establish any vulnerability to attribute.
audit_record.remaining_gap: A closed AI/non-AI attribution would require a reproducible authentication bypass plus the actual code and history of the server-side factor/state validation that caused and fixed it. No such reproducer, vulnerable backend line, fix commit, or patched version is present in the cited report or public repository, and the CNA/vendor instead affirmatively concluded that the report was not a security issue. causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated attacker can send PUT /api/supplier/{victim_id}. The route has only auth:api middleware and SupplierRequest::authorize() merely checks Auth::check(); SupplierUpdateController then resolves the identifier globally with Supplier::find($id), updates it from $request->all(), and returns the resulting supplier. Because Supplier::$fillable includes company_id while the request rules do not constrain that field and sensitive supplier fields are not hidden, the attacker can read and modify another tenant's supplier and reassign it by supplying company_id.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The unsafe SupplierUpdateController method body was present but dormant from b03c8c6f5fde097cbe44552464c56469b60a4369 (APP_VERSION 4.0.0): neither that revision nor tagged v2.0.1/v4.6.0 registered a supplier PUT API route. The smallest commit that completed the externally reachable vulnerable mechanism was b233f27910f32c264243d03021e4f25dbef5f403, which imported SupplierUpdateController and added the auth-only PUT /supplier/{id} route while leaving the pre-existing unscoped lookup and mass assignment intact; it set APP_VERSION to 4.15.0.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Stored graph-configuration XSS. An authenticated low-privilege user could POST a config_json object containing a style such as mispStyles.Event.svgIcon. The save route checked only that the string parsed as JSON and persisted the complete object; the list route returned the stored string unchanged. When a viewer with access to the saved row (notably an administrator, because administrators list every user's configs) loaded it, graphConfigModal.js parsed config_json and applyConfig() spread every property of each stixStyles/mispStyles entry into GRAPH_CONFIG. A subsequent graph render passed that style map to Pivotick as nodeStyleMap. The bundled Pivotick renderer treats svgIcon as markup (both a template path using template.innerHTML = i.svgIcon.trim() and node rendering using an SVG element's innerHTML), so a crafted SVG event handler executes in the viewer's browser. Loading/applying the saved configuration is the victim interaction.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit a0a9834b21b40ab570db54e1c6e6c2cf100b5f9a is the atomic first writer of the vulnerable cross-user path. causal_chain.bug_semantics: Authenticated cross-tenant IDOR/BOLA in the web ticket CRUD: GET /ticket/update/{id} loaded Ticket::find($id) and exposed another tenant's ticket content and attachments; POST /ticket/save accepted an attacker-selected ticket id, loaded that record without company_id scoping, then overwrote company_id with the attacker's company and saved it; GET /ticket/delete/{id} loaded and deleted any numeric ticket id without tenant scoping, and its generic Request parameter bypassed the authorization implemented by TicketDeleteRequest.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The original ticket CRUD commit 2feef9f35593dba39525f6a8a07b4cd3f74f19bd directly introduced the first vulnerable read and save endpoints and their unscoped Ticket::find lookups. Commit 946a0c5e43a1178534e5b013ea2608d565686220 later expanded the same flaw class by adding the unscoped GET delete endpoint. Commit 65f6b9f961efe533b4d3f20f1eddad132fe8ef1d only moved the already-vulnerable save lookup into TicketRepository and is not a BIC. Commit c837c80a4f7de40348e142af7d15e60c39ebcaf1 later created TicketDeleteRequest but did not wire it into TicketDeleteController, so it was incomplete hardening rather than the origin.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The public POST routes /fetch_misp_event and /misp_search_events accepted a caller-controlled HTTPS MISP base URL and API key, then made server-side requests and returned the remote JSON response or selected event data. _validate_misp_url rejected unsafe IP literals but treated every syntactically ordinary hostname as safe without DNS resolution. The direct fix resolves domain names, requires every resulting address to be globally routable, and requires authentication on both routes.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The authenticated GET /download-export endpoint accepted an attacker-controlled filename query parameter, concatenated it directly to export_path(), checked only file_exists(), and passed the resulting path to response()->download(). Traversal components such as ../ therefore escaped the exports directory and disclosed any application-readable file; the issue was an arbitrary read only, not file write or code execution.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 0813dca72e26bca7f091bb7ffa2da3f3c18d7ac8 created FileDownloadController.php and first wrote the vulnerable expression `$path = export_path() . $_GET['filename'];` plus the unchecked download sink. The controller became remotely reachable when 5eda5fcf38a87a1ceb39762474df6c2211def9fb added /download-export inside the auth middleware group. Later commit 9049917b3807924bb301f35635d17958b23888cd retained the vulnerable method while adding unrelated import/export UI functionality; it did not originate the flaw.

audit_record.bug_semantics: The authenticated GET /download-export endpoint accepted an attacker-controlled filename query parameter, concatenated it directly to export_path(), checked only file_exists(), and passed the resulting path to response()->download(). evidence: First-party repository advisory https://github.com/rconfig/rconfig/security/advisories/GHSA-m5rw-jcrm-mmwc describes an authenticated export-download path traversal allowing reads outside the export directory, requires authentication, and names 8.2.13 as patched. Its displayed affected-version constraint `<8.2.12` conflicts with its own remediation text and repository history: `git grep -n -F 'export_path() . $_GET['\''filename'\'']' core-8.2.12 -- app/Http/Controllers/FileDownloadController.php` finds the vulnerable line at line 23, while core-8.2.13 contains the basename and containment checks. Thus core-8.2.12 is affected and 8.2.13 is the first fixed release.

`git show --format= --find-renames 0813dca72e26bca7f091bb7ffa2da3f3c18d7ac8 -- app/Http/Controllers/FileDownloadController.php app/Http/Helpers.php` shows a new controller whose download_export() directly concatenates `$_GET['filename']` to export_path(), calls file_exists(), then response()->download(), and a new export_path() helper. `git log -L 20,28:app/Http/Controllers/FileDownloadController.php cc83dc07b9a011fcabb50cb916a91b393e8ad4f3` traces those vulnerable lines through 9049917b3807924bb301f35635d17958b23888cd back to their creation in 0813dca72e26bca7f091bb7ffa2da3f3c18d7ac8.

The independent pickaxe check `git log --all -S"export_path() . \$_GET['filename']" -- app/Http/Controllers/FileDownloadController.php` returns only introduction 0813dca72e26bca7f091bb7ffa2da3f3c18d7ac8 and removal d133a466a2df9d065177de9a8ed50f1bfe438aee. The introducer is a small ordinary three-file feature commit (35 insertions and 5 deletions), not a merge, refactor, move, revert, release commit, or squash aggregate.

Direct-parent verification: `git ls-tree -r 09fa5a4eac1abb8ee5010bb85b39411f36a6fa5e -- app/Http/Controllers/FileDownloadController.php` produces no entry, and `git grep -n -E 'download_export|export_path\(\).*filename|\$_GET\[' 09fa5a4eac1abb8ee5010bb85b39411f36a6fa5e -- app routes` produces no match. The parent therefore lacks both the new controller and the vulnerable data flow.

`git show --unified=30 5eda5fcf38a87a1ceb39762474df6c2211def9fb -- routes/web.php` shows `Route::get('/download-export', ...@download_export)` added inside `Route::group(['middleware' => 'auth'], ...)`, establishing the authenticated HTTP attack path. `git tag --contains 0813dca72e26bca7f091bb7ffa2da3f3c18d7ac8` and the equivalent route-commit containment include core-8.0.0 through core-8.2.16; `git tag --contains d133a466a2df9d065177de9a8ed50f1bfe438aee` begins at core-8.2.13. `git rev-parse core-8.2.12^{} core-8.2.13^{}` resolves the adjacent release commits to 28b88100001c277f30a46ef8f512af2e0f59928b and 72b60a41d9589f3b2e0c5ea0062734b6a0b5a86d.

`git show d133a466a2df9d065177de9a8ed50f1bfe438aee -- app/Http/Controllers/FileDownloadController.php` removes raw $_GET concatenation, reduces the request value with basename(), and requires the real path to be a file under the resolved export directory before download, closing both traversal and symlink escapes. Follow-up 25d6d2f4314f3c38186d98df9c11da8fe0222862 centralizes the already-effective check in PathContainmentService; it is a refactor, not the first direct fix. The first-party core-8.2.13 release notes likewise state that export downloads are contained to the export directory.

BIC-only AI check: `git cat-file -p 0813dca72e26bca7f091bb7ffa2da3f3c18d7ac8` shows author and committer `danielrConfig <daniel@rconfig.com>` and only the subject `feat: add file download functionality and export path helper`; there is no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI marker in the commit object. The later direct fix d133a466a2df9d065177de9a8ed50f1bfe438aee does contain a Claude co-author trailer, but the protocol excludes fix-only AI evidence from the introducer verdict.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: POST /company/save accepted a company logo without server-side type, extension, size, or SVG-content validation. An authenticated user satisfying the route's create company and update company permission gates could upload an SVG containing an embedded script; the controller derived a .svg destination name and wrote it to public storage. The resulting /storage/company/{slug}/{file} resource was served statically outside Laravel authentication, so direct navigation by any visitor executed attacker-controlled JavaScript in the application origin.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: dbd8f149062223fd50bc0fdb3467c285868b388c is the smallest true BIC: it first added the logo multipart field (explicitly accepting image/svg), copied an uploaded logo under the public webroot using the content-derived extension, and performed no validation. Later controller extraction, formatting, repository refactoring, and the 2026 public-disk rewrite preserved the same unrestricted-upload decision rather than introducing it.

audit_record.ai_marker: absent: `git cat-file -p dbd8f149062223fd50bc0fdb3467c285868b388c` shows human author and committer Gustavo Novaro <gnovaro@gmail.com>, the sole message `Company custom logo.`, and no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI trailer, or bot identity.
audit_record.bug_semantics: POST /company/save accepted a company logo without server-side type, extension, size, or SVG-content validation. An authenticated user satisfying the route's create company and update company permission gates could upload an SVG containing an embedded script; the controller derived a .svg destination name and wrote it to public storage. The resulting /storage/company/{slug}/{file} resource was served statically outside Laravel authentication, so direct navigation by any visitor executed attacker-controlled JavaScript in the application origin.
evidence: The Secur0 CNA record https://secur0.com/en/cna/cve-list/cve-2026-78337-unrestricted-upload-company-logo-svg-xss identifies CompanySaveController::save at POST /company/save, the authenticated create-company plus update-company permission prerequisite, direct-navigation stored SVG XSS, affected versions before 5.15.13, BIC dbd8f149, and patch aaa4fc76. It also states that every existing tag is vulnerable and that the fix is not tagged.

In the validated clone, `git show --format=fuller --patch dbd8f149062223fd50bc0fdb3467c285868b388c` shows the BIC adding `request->file('logo')->extension()`, copying the upload to `public/asset/upload/company/{slug}/{timestamp}.{extension}`, saving the filename, and adding a multipart file input whose accept list includes image/svg. `git log --all -S"request->file('logo')" -- app/Http/Controllers` returns dbd8f149062223fd50bc0fdb3467c285868b388c as the first writer.

Direct parent verification is reproducible with `git show 4f6c90f21a3b1c826f65d554572c87647994e055:app/Http/Controllers/CompanyController.php`: save() only copies scalar company fields and has no logo field, file access, extension derivation, public write, or equivalent upload path. `git cat-file -p dbd8f149062223fd50bc0fdb3467c285868b388c` confirms that exact commit's sole parent is 4f6c90f21a3b1c826f65d554572c87647994e055.

Lifecycle checks: `git show --find-renames 3f8ead9e0aafe1293253eab52eb72adb80be5b87` shows the existing vulnerable method renamed/extracted from CompanyController to Company/CompanySaveController; `git log -L 41,52:app/Http/Controllers/Company/CompanySaveController.php 54713abef6a89fdd3d9534c06f232dcecae4f6ca` traces the upload through the formatting-only caef09bb28dd80b8e19802b2c4a07ee619df0e84 change back to dbd8f149 and shows 4c15d20a57c4225bb3853bad2c5b01b3da11121f merely replacing the public-webroot copy with `storeAs(..., 'public')` while retaining the unvalidated extension. Thus neither the move nor later rewrite is the BIC.

At vulnerable parent 54713abef6a89fdd3d9534c06f232dcecae4f6ca, `routes/module/company.php` chains `can('create company')` and `can('update company')` on POST /company/save; CompanySaveController also checks create versus update authorization and company ownership. Its upload block calls `storeAs($folder, $filename, 'public')` with no validation. `config/filesystems.php` maps the public disk to storage/app/public, URL APP_URL/storage, and public/storage symlink; the logo views use /storage/company/{slug}/{logo}.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The Markdown and PDF evaluation-export routes authorized only access to the conversion, then build_evaluation_report() selected every non-deleted evaluation comment without applying the already-established per-comment privacy rule. On a public conversion, any viewer, including an anonymous viewer, could therefore export a private evaluation comment belonging to another author and receive both its content and the author's first name; only the conversion owner, comment author, or an administrator should see such a comment.

Later conversion-model renames and refactors preserved that omission; blame immediately before the fix still traces the query, loop, author, and content lines to c5d258d59530292bb17ab602d3b799373540596f.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The MISP-to-STIX page lets an operator connect cti-transmute to a remote MISP server. The server-side /misp_search_events proxy copied remote event id, info, date, organization, attribute count, threat level, tag name, and tag colour into JSON, after which the browser interpolated those values into tr.innerHTML, tag/TLP badge HTML, distribution-label HTML, and flash HTML. A malicious or compromised remote MISP instance could therefore return crafted markup or script-capable attributes that execute in the cti-transmute origin when the operator browses or imports events; unvalidated remote tag colours also reached CSS background values.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48 introduced the remote-MISP browser end to end: the proxy that returned remote fields and the first HTML-interpolating renderers (showFlash, showTlpWarning, miTagBadges, and miRenderRows). Commit 26ecb7e6a608b5be73fa552928e00bef7cac4f22 later expanded the same vulnerable rendering to multi-select IDs and sharing-group/distribution labels, but it did not originate the vulnerability because exploitable remote event fields already reached innerHTML in b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: rConfig deliberately disabled self-registration with Auth::routes(['register' => false]), but a later bare Auth::routes() registered Laravel's default POST /register route again. An unauthenticated request could therefore reach RegisterController, whose create() inserted name, email, and password without a role; the users.role database default was Admin. The framework registration trait then authenticated the newly created full-Administrator account, exposing device credentials, users, and API-token functionality without invitation, approval, or email verification.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 5ae01b3781de867baad1a8aa8aebfc3448812f68 is the smallest true BIC: during the multiple-SSO-provider feature it directly added the second bare Auth::routes(); below the already restrictive call in routes/web.php. causal_chain.bug_semantics: Authenticated path traversal and arbitrary file read in GET /download-export. routes/web.php places the endpoint inside the auth middleware group, but FileDownloadController::download_export() formed $path as export_path() . $_GET['filename']; file_exists() was the only gate before response()->download($path). A low-privilege authenticated caller could therefore supply ../ segments (for example, ../../.env relative to storage/app/rconfig/exports/) to escape the exports directory and download any file readable by the web-server process, exposing secrets such as application keys and database or mail credentials.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 0813dca72e26bca7f091bb7ffa2da3f3c18d7ac8 is the atomic first writer of the flawed sink: it created app/Http/Controllers/FileDownloadController.php with download_export(), the raw $_GET['filename'] concatenation, the file_exists() check, and response()->download(), and added export_path(). Its direct parent 09fa5a4eac1abb8ee5010bb85b39411f36a6fa5e has no FileDownloadController, no export_path() helper, and no download-export route; only DeviceInventoryExporter already emitted a link to that not-yet-routed endpoint. causal_chain.bug_semantics: In HTTP-auth mode, an unauthenticated client-controlled Bearer token was used as a filesystem path component. The exact reserved token `telegram` was rejected, but separators and `..` were accepted: with the default directory, `../fast-mcp-telegram/telegram` made both SessionFileTokenVerifier and the Telegram client loader select `~/.config/fast-mcp-telegram/telegram.session`. Existence/authorization of that legacy session therefore authenticated the attacker without a generated bearer secret; downstream account-prefixing did not restore the lost authentication boundary.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The flaw originated in the initial multi-user Bearer implementation, commit 763b3e781d8fb0067fbedd85ea0f25d53a951a2e: it accepted the raw Authorization token and added `session_path = SESSION_DIR / f"{token}.session"` before opening an authorized Telegram session. Commit 1be7e62feb6160ecbe32d15f0ab940769f094968 later added exact, case-insensitive reserved-name rejection but no token-shape or path-containment validation, leaving traversal aliases. audit_record.bug_semantics: In HTTP-auth mode, an unauthenticated client-controlled Bearer token was used as a filesystem path component. The exact reserved token `telegram` was rejected, but separators and `..` were accepted: with the default directory, `../fast-mcp-telegram/telegram` made both SessionFileTokenVerifier and the Telegram client loader select `~/.config/fast-mcp-telegram/telegram.session`. Existence/authorization of that legacy session therefore authenticated the attacker without a generated bearer secret; downstream account-prefixing did not restore the lost authentication boundary.

Run `git show --format=fuller --patch 763b3e781d8fb0067fbedd85ea0f25d53a951a2e -- src/client/connection.py src/server.py pyproject.toml`: the commit introduces raw Bearer extraction in `src/server.py`, passes it to request context, and introduces `_get_client_by_token` with `session_path = SESSION_DIR / f"{token}.session"` followed by TelegramClient connection and `is_user_authorized()`; it simultaneously changes project version 0.1.4 to 0.2.0.

Run `git log master -L :_get_client_by_token:src/client/connection.py`: line history follows the function back to its addition in 763b3e781d8fb0067fbedd85ea0f25d53a951a2e, including the vulnerable raw token join. Run `git log master -S 'session_path = SESSION_DIR / f"{token}.session"' -- src/client/connection.py` as the independent pickaxe cross-check; its earliest result is the same commit (later hits add similar cleanup paths or remove the vulnerable join).

causal_chain.bug_semantics: In clusters configured to use Flannel's experimental Extension backend, the Kubernetes subnet manager turns the flannel.alpha.coreos.com/backend-data Node annotation into Lease.Attrs.BackendData. On remote lease add/remove events, the Extension backend JSON-decodes that attacker-controlled value, supplies it on stdin to the configured SubnetAddCommand or SubnetRemoveCommand, and executes the configured command through sh -c as the privileged flannel daemon. Thus a principal able to set Node annotations can feed malicious backend data into shell-based extension command processing on every watching flannel node, yielding cross-node root-level command execution. Non-Extension backends do not traverse this sink.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit fb4a25e6089829ec68620f5a770da3fdfc41491e first introduced the entire Extension backend, including JSON decoding of remote BackendData, forwarding it to command stdin, and the sh -c SubnetAddCommand/SubnetRemoveCommand invocations. The later 7722da5eb9a08e3daf8ee5bd510c62b548dd2240 only allowed empty BackendData while retaining the already-vulnerable data-to-shell path, so it is not the BIC.

audit_record.ai_marker: Absent. `git cat-file commit fb4a25e6089829ec68620f5a770da3fdfc41491e` shows human author and committer Tom Denham <tom@tomdee.co.uk>, one parent, a PGP signature, and only the message `backend/extension: Introduce new extension backend` followed by `WIP`; it has no Co-authored-by, Generated-with, AI-tool, or bot marker. causal_chain.bug_semantics: The Express dashboard exposes GET /api/session-summary and GET /api/session-events without authentication. Each handler takes attacker-controlled req.query.sessionId, embeds it in `session-log-${sessionId}.jsonl`, joins that string to the hooks data directory, and reads the resulting path. A sessionId containing a slash followed by `..` components causes Node path normalization to escape the intended directory while retaining a caller-selected .jsonl suffix, so an unauthenticated network client can read any process-readable reachable JSONL file.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The smart_user MCP tool accepts a caller-controlled username for operation get-user-info and passes it unchanged through SmartUser.run() -> getUserInfo() -> getUserDetails(). On Unix, getUserDetails() interpolated that value into the shell command string `getent passwd "${username}" || grep "^${username}:" /etc/passwd`, which promisified child_process.exec executed through a shell. POSIX command substitution remains active inside double quotes, so a username such as `$(id > /tmp/marker)` executes as the MCP server user before getent or grep processes the argument.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: awxkit's custom PyYAML Loader registers !include and !import and passes attacker-controlled scalar, sequence, or mapping values to extractFile(). Before the fix, extractFile() joined that value to the importing YAML file's directory, expanded it with glob.glob(), converted matches to absolute paths, and opened them without rejecting absolute paths, '..' traversal, or symlink escapes. A user who runs 'awx --conf.format yaml import' on a crafted YAML document can therefore cause the local client to read and parse arbitrary YAML-formatted files outside the document directory. The attack is local/client-side, requires the victim to import the malicious file, and compromises confidentiality.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The vulnerable extractor first appears in ansible/awx's public Git history only in 9616cc6f7856523ebf6d1580443313296c9f6507 ('import awxkit'), an aggregate import of 101 files and 10,479 lines. Pull request #4451 is titled 'open source awxkit', and its discussion refers to the pre-existing code as towerkit and says awxkit will replace tower-cli. Thus 9616cc6f7856523ebf6d1580443313296c9f6507 is a public-history gateway/copy, not the smallest authoring commit that created the flawed path handling. The source authoring history is not present in the validated clone or exposed by the import PR, so the true BIC cannot be named without substituting an excluded aggregate import.

In the admin static handler, an unauthenticated request header was inserted verbatim into served HTML, JavaScript, and CSS; attacker syntax could therefore execute on the admin origin, and the absence of Vary/no-store let a URL-keyed intermediary cache distribute a poisoned representation. Separately, the legacy /p/:pad/timeslider route put a character-filtered but otherwise attacker-controlled proxy path at the start of a 302 Location. Because the filter retained slashes and did not collapse a leading //, x-proxy-path: //evil.example produced //evil.example/p/<pad>, which browsers resolve as a protocol-relative cross-origin redirect.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The unauthenticated GET /tokenTransfer/:token handler treats knowledge of a random transfer UUID as sufficient authority. POST stores the originating author's token and createdAt under that UUID, but GET neither checks createdAt nor removes the record, so a leaked URL remains redeemable indefinitely and repeatedly. GET also serializes the stored record, including the raw author token, in its response body, defeating the HttpOnly boundary and enabling persistent authorship impersonation. The attacker needs a legitimate user to create a transfer and must obtain its UUID out of band, but needs no Etherpad authentication to redeem it.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The released introduction 41cb6803d2ac71cadf42f4aa88f37c85275a3879 is a squash of PR #7228. causal_chain.bug_semantics: On Linux/Unix, an attacker-controlled RAR entry such as `..\..\tmp\evil.txt` is first checked as a child of the extraction directory while backslashes are literal filename characters, so `getCanonicalPath().startsWith(destination.getCanonicalPath())` accepts it. `makeFile()` then splits that same name on backslashes, joins the components with the platform `File.separator` (`/`), creates the resulting directories/file, and `extract()` writes attacker-controlled entry bytes through `FileOutputStream`. The validation and the write therefore interpret the same pathname differently, enabling traversal and arbitrary file overwrite outside the destination. Windows is not affected by this bypass because canonicalization already treats backslashes as separators.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The soffice-backed import/export paths placed working files in the shared directory returned by os.tmpdir() under names derived from non-cryptographic Math.random(), without exclusive creation or no-follow protection. A local user able to predict or race a token could pre-create a symlink at an export source path (or a converter destination path); ExportHandler's fs.writeFile then followed the link and truncated/wrote the linked target with exported HTML, subject to the Etherpad process's filesystem privileges. The import conversion destination was likewise predictable and could receive partially attacker-controlled converted upload content. Shared-host local access and a target writable by Etherpad are required.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The smallest semantic BIC is eeddf1348f351c92355d010ced56c3b511ca8f46: it created node/ExportHandler.js with Math.floor(Math.random()*new Date().getTime()), /tmp/eplite_export_<token> source/destination paths, fs.writeFile(srcFile, html), and in the same commit registered GET /p/:pad/export/:type in node/server.js. Its direct parent had neither the handler nor route. b13fbbfd73ab18f69d45de382ffb1fc51fe96f1f added the analogous import path two days later. 4fc4a3538148bc995fff989794e91779ed4c847f (export) and b0976a292f70c2c6d344bafd2793aed09027f74b (import) later changed the already-insecure token formula to Math.floor(Math.random()*0xFFFFFFFF); they narrowed/rewrote an existing flaw and are not BICs.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated low-privilege environment API-key holder can send PUT /api/v1/runs/:runId/metadata with an operation such as {type:"set",key:"$.__proto__.polluted",value:"PWNED"}. UpdateMetadataRequestBody accepted operation.key as an unrestricted string and applyMetadataOperations passed the path to @jsonhero/path without rejecting __proto__, constructor, or prototype. JSONHeroPath.set therefore writes through __proto__ to Object.prototype in the shared webapp process. Inherited attacker data then contaminates unrelated Prisma and prom-client objects across tenants, breaking worker authentication and allowing a repeatable process-wide denial of service.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The Admin Console gadget endpoint embeds the request parameter in gf.getGadgetModule("#{param.gadget}", ...). JSFTemplating Handler.getInputValue resolves that outer expression through ComponentUtil.resolveValue; after param.gadget becomes an attacker string, resolveValue treats a resulting #{...} string as another ValueExpression and evaluates it. causal_chain.bug_semantics: The authenticated GlassFish Administration Console uses JSFTemplating as its view-description/templating engine. JSFTemplating accepted and evaluated EL from console request processing with the ordinary Faces ELContext and no resolver in front of the standard resolver chain to reject dangerous reflective/static constructs. A crafted authenticated panel request could therefore reach static methods or constructors, getClass()/class traversal, and static fields; an attacker could reach Java process-execution facilities and run operating-system commands as the GlassFish service account. The closing component change installs RestrictedELResolver ahead of PageSessionResolver and rejects ELClass method invocation/constructors, getClass(), the class property, and (in the immediately following hardening commit) static fields.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The unsafe EL design predates the available Git history. In eclipse-ee4j/glassfish-jsftemplating, blame of VariableResolver.java attributes the request-parameter datasource, method-expression creation, and general variable-resolution machinery to root commit 18d9b835fa98caec01ef026aab5ed907567dec0d, an 'Initial Contribution' importing 300 files and 141,910 lines whose source headers date the implementation to 2006. In eclipse-ee4j/glassfish, root commit 571714739b23e16c4c90d5229b806433920b3bcb is likewise an aggregate 'Initial Contribution' and already pins vulnerable jsftemplating 2.1.3. Neither aggregate is the smallest commit that originally wrote the flaw, and neither has a parent/history from which that commit can be decomposed.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: With the admin API enabled, a database-backed principal holding gateways.read can submit an attacker-controlled hostname to POST /admin/gateways/test. Validation resolves that hostname and rejects private, loopback, link-local, reserved, and metadata addresses, but the accepted URL retains the hostname. ResilientHttpClient/httpx then resolves the hostname again when connecting. An attacker-controlled DNS server can therefore return a public address for the validation lookup and a private or metadata address for the connection lookup, bypassing the SSRF checks and returning internal response content.

PR #3115 was squash-landed on the release line as d549137791f10c59c00ec3e89cb55cd560a8248f. Later hardening 2b5b9e9a145304c466966c560e82d4682849b13a added an allowlist and an explicit ICACF-15 rebinding TODO, and fb4d9a2616f22dcc64239b250b1c6389b638de4f consolidated validation into validate_gateway_test_url(), but both retained independent connection-time DNS resolution. causal_chain.bug_semantics: DownloadFileRequestHandler derives fileName from the /file/* path, then accepts the request's version parameter and passes it unchanged to BaseUtils.replaceFileNameAndExtension. That helper returns FilenameUtils.getFullPath(fileName) + version, and FileUtils.readFile/createFile ultimately opens new File(APP_DOWNLOAD_FOLDER_PATH, fileName) without canonical containment checking. On the unauthenticated /file/static/noauth/** route, a request to /file/static/noauth with a version such as ../../... therefore replaces the benign basename with a traversal path and reads a server file outside the download folder.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit b34987f7b37b5fd6a03b9dd9092bd18efc936d46 first added both the unsafe replaceFileNameAndExtension helper and the three handler lines that read the untrusted version parameter and replace fileName without validation. Its direct parent 51dd90c21ec7e7b289fde206208106cf80b835f8 has neither the version read nor replacement. Commit 87b7b9e81d8ebdf52b0480cfcad78c5817603883 later exposed /downloadFile/static/noauth/** without authentication, and 256ae9dcb19d8762b1cb43f2d1e688d46592581c renamed that public endpoint to the advisory's /file/static/noauth/**; these later exposure/rename commits did not write the unsafe version-to-path logic and are not the BIC.

A sid containing parent-directory components therefore escaped the intended upload directory; choosing a JSP upload name let an unauthenticated attacker place executable content in a web-accessible location and then request it.

Later moves, package renames, and the 2022 FileUtils storage refactor preserved that trust decision and are not introducers.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: ZPan v1's Token constructor globally initialized jwtutil with the literal HMAC signing secret "123". The same utility issued and verified RoleClaims containing attacker-relevant Subject and Roles fields, and LoginAuth trusted a verified z-token cookie for identity and RBAC. Anyone knowing the repository value could therefore sign an HS512 token claiming an arbitrary uid and the admin role and remotely reach administrator-only APIs; issue #219 demonstrates GET /api/system/options/core.email with a forged admin cookie.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: When archive unpacking is enabled for received mail, or when MakeUnzipFileAction is invoked, an attacker-controlled ZIP/RAR entry name is appended to a temporary output-directory path without canonical containment validation. A traversal name can therefore make FileOutputStream write outside the staging directory; the subsequent cleanup of outputFile can then delete the escaped target after overwriting it. The shared ZipUtils implementation ultimately exposed the same sink to both EmailReceiver and MakeUnzipFileAction.

Commit ce3cf594f118e720279abdb78116a597956bbe41 later independently added the same unsafe pattern to MakeUnzipFileAction. Commit 4950d66839375b11a4706fe1b5bd5f28ec9abf17 was a refactor that deleted both local implementations and centralized their still-vulnerable behavior in ZipUtils, so it is not the BIC.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An unauthenticated federated ActivityPub server can send a Create/Note whose sanitized content contains an emoji shortcode and whose attacker-controlled Emoji tag supplies icon.url and name. NodeBB replaces the shortcode after the content sanitization pass with an HTML img string containing those values in quoted attributes, then stores that generated HTML. The remote-post display path can return the stored HTML without a subsequent markdown/sanitize-html pass, so an attribute-breaking value becomes persistent same-origin XSS for viewers. The first exploitable sink interpolated icon.url; commit 3968c822a2291d32d79a86ba625858a90e8496f9 subsequently added the unescaped title from tag.name.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: @cleverbrush/deep deepExtend recursively copies every enumerable source key into a fresh ordinary object without rejecting __proto__. From ece027428a9a5755916f159a5760665be9cc89a6 onward, the merge loop uses Reflect.has(o1, key). For attacker-controlled JSON containing an own __proto__ object, Reflect.has sees the inherited __proto__ accessor on an ordinary target; o1[key] resolves to Object.prototype, both sides satisfy the object checks, and extendObject recurses into Object.prototype. Attacker-chosen inner properties are then assigned as own properties of Object.prototype and become inherited by every ordinary object in the realm. An application reaches the sink by passing parsed request/config/query data to deepExtend; the resulting realm-wide inherited values can corrupt authorization or configuration logic, cause denial of service, or feed a secondary gadget. The disclosed working route is __proto__; constructor is a function on the ordinary receiver and therefore does not take this recursion branch, although the closing defense rejects __proto__, constructor, and prototype.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The smallest true BIC is ece027428a9a5755916f159a5760665be9cc89a6, a normal one-parent source commit. In libs/deep/src/deepExtend.ts it replaced the parent's own-property decision !o1.hasOwnProperty(keys[i]) with the prototype-chain-aware !Reflect.has(o1, keys[i]) while retaining recursive descent and unfiltered property names. That semantic change made inherited __proto__ appear to be an existing object and redirected recursion into Object.prototype. The absence of an unsafe-key denylist was older, but the immediate parent assigned __proto__ on the local merge receiver instead of recursively writing attacker properties into Object.prototype, so the realm-wide primitive reported in issue #213 begins at this commit. Later commits only reformatted, typed, or documented the same vulnerable loop until the fix.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Authenticated Project Managers or Owners can store an attacker-controlled repository git_url beginning with a Git option such as --upload-pack=... . With the default cmd_git client, the server-side schedule commit-hash poller passes that value to git ls-remote before the repository operand and without --end-of-options. Git interprets it as an option and invokes the supplied upload-pack command through a shell, yielding command execution in the Semaphore server process. Repository validation checked only that GitURL was nonempty while branch validation did not delimit the URL argument.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The exploitable schedule-poller data flow was introduced by a30df1527e15c4c0060979bc2b7b120a8234111f (fix(be): bug with getting remote commit), which changed GetLastRemoteCommitHash from git ls-remote origin <branch> in a repository directory to git ls-remote <Repository.GetGitURL()> <branch> in the temporary directory. This was the first write that put attacker-controlled GitURL into the ls-remote option-parsing position; later file moves and client refactors only preserved it.

With the default cmd_git client, the server-side schedule commit-hash poller passes that value to git ls-remote before the repository operand and without --end-of-options. Git interprets it as an option and invokes the supplied upload-pack command through a shell, yielding command execution in the Semaphore server process. Repository validation checked only that GitURL was nonempty while branch validation did not delimit the URL argument.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/semaphoreui/semaphore/security/advisories/GHSA-xp7j-h7jc-4w8p describes the Manager/Owner repository and schedule API path, default cmd_git trigger, `git ls-remote` argv injection via `--upload-pack=`, affected releases 2.18.12/2.18.13/2.18.16, and patched release 2.18.20. The bundle's alias CVE-2026-73682 is rejected by NVD in favor of CVE-2026-73294, but its supplied description and first-party reference identify this same git_url mechanism.

At the BIC, `git diff 1993a14fb6b484d4ac323700ee19cc0aaf20086f a30df1527e15c4c0060979bc2b7b120a8234111f -- lib/GitRepository.go` shows the decisive replacement: `r.output(GitRepositoryRepoDir, "ls-remote", "origin", r.Repository.GitBranch)` became `r.output(GitRepositoryTmpDir, "ls-remote", r.Repository.GetGitURL(), r.Repository.GitBranch)`. `git show 1993a14...:lib/GitRepository.go` directly verifies that the immediate parent used literal `origin`, so the vulnerable git_url flow was absent.

`git log -L '/func (r GitRepository) GetLastRemoteCommitHash/,/^}/':lib/GitRepository.go a30df152...` identifies a30df152... as the write that substituted GetGitURL; it traces the function itself to 208e615a6e5718f98e9e33f4d0814ba87bde0eb8, where ls-remote still used literal `origin`. `git log --all --reverse -S'ls-remote'` and `-S'GetGitURL()'` corroborate the same history; df4932a5..., 58850e912..., and 40e018aaa... are refactor/move commits, not introducers.

At a30df152..., api/projects/repository.go AddRepository binds a request body and stores Repository.GitURL, db/Repository.go Validate rejects only empty name/url/branch, and services/schedules/pool.go loads schedule.RepositoryID then calls GetLastRemoteCommitHash. This reconstructs source, persistence, scheduled server-side trigger, and sink from the historical tree.

Release edge: `git tag --points-at 1993a14...` returns v2.8.46 and `git tag --points-at a30df152...` returns v2.8.47, establishing v2.8.47 as the first tagged vulnerable release. The first-party advisory scopes its enumerated supported affected releases to 2.18.12, 2.18.13, and 2.18.16 and declares 2.18.20 patched.

Immediately before the direct stable fix, `git grep -n 'ValidateGitURL\|end-of-options' eb841c8d5891189b13fedbd269bbcf2d5e4e319d -- db db_lib` has no matches, while that tree's db_lib/CmdGitClient.go:170 passes GetGitURL(false) directly to ls-remote and db/Repository.go validates only URL non-emptiness plus the branch. `git show a7a7a33a64aea382a0726b3722856f298663eacf` adds ValidateGitURL and inserts `--end-of-options` before URLs in clone/ls-remote and before the branch where relevant, directly closing the mechanism.

The same direct patch exists on develop as 7e8a9434bd81b82cf42220151c74801ea97542d6. On the 2.18 stable line, `git tag --contains a7a7a33...` starts at v2.18.17; the advisory nevertheless designates v2.18.20 as the supported patched boundary. The bundle-referenced v2.18.20 tip 5d87656a680600125fe78edec1f7a0d10484b52c is a descendant release commit and is therefore retained as fix_sha, while a7a7a33... is the actual direct git_url fix.

`git cat-file -p a30df152...` proves a single parent, the human author/committer identity, and the complete marker-free commit message. The BIC changes one file by replacing the remote operand and adding error handling; it is neither a merge nor a squash aggregate, so no decomposition is needed.
audit_record.flaw_origin: The exploitable schedule-poller data flow was introduced by a30df1527e15c4c0060979bc2b7b120a8234111f (fix(be): bug with getting remote commit), which changed GetLastRemoteCommitHash from git ls-remote origin <branch> in a repository directory to git ls-remote <Repository.GetGitURL()> <branch> in the temporary directory. This was the first write that put attacker-controlled GitURL into the ls-remote option-parsing position; later file moves and client refactors only preserved it.
audit_record.reasoning: The vulnerability is causally attributable to the small 2022 commit that first routed stored GitURL into schedule-driven `git ls-remote`, not to later moves/refactors and not to the 2026 fix. Direct parent comparison proves absence, line history and string searches converge on the BIC, and release ancestry establishes both the historical introduction and supported patch boundary. The BIC commit object contains only a conventional human identity/message and predates modern coding-agent markers; under the BIC-only evidence rule, the closed verdict is NOT_AI.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The local MCP request-approval path accepts caller-controlled categoryName and passes it to ApprovalStorage.createApproval. Vulnerable versions used join(this.approvalsDir, categoryName), then recursively created that path and wrote `${id}.json` beneath it. A categoryName containing parent components and platform separators (the first-party Windows reproduction used `..\..\..\spec-workflow-poc-outside`) therefore normalized outside `.spec-workflow/approvals`, allowing a locally authorized MCP caller to create a directory and approval JSON file outside the intended storage root. The separate filePath checks did not constrain categoryName.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The vulnerable data flow and sink were created together in the repository's root commit b66281c495aa93e58da69c9227ac5506c16d0ca4: src/tools/request-approval.ts accepted categoryName as an unconstrained string and passed it directly to ApprovalStorage.createApproval, while src/dashboard/approval-storage.ts created `join(this.approvalsDir, categoryName)` and wrote an approval JSON file there. This is the earliest and smallest commit present in the complete reachable history that writes the vulnerable lines; it is an initial 0.0.1 root commit rather than a later move, refactor, revert, release backport, or squash merge.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An initialized XKB client can send two SetMap requests with XkbSetMapResizeTypes. The first can grow xkb->map->num_types to 255; the second can use firstType=255 and nTypes=10. CheckKeyTypes accepts firstType because its check is firstType > num_types, computes the client-controlled sum nMaps=265 without bounding it to the 256-entry mapWidths array, and writes mapWidthRtrn[i + firstType] for each supplied type. That writes mapWidths[255..264], nine bytes beyond the fixed stack array in _XkbSetMapChecks and into adjacent stack state, enabling server crash and potentially privilege escalation when the X server is privileged.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A caller able to reach GET /api could supply an arbitrary http(s) url. The route passed that value into extractWeb, whose timeout wrapper called the server's fetch implementation directly, with no destination-address validation and ordinary redirect behavior. PullMD could therefore request loopback, private, link-local, CGNAT, or cloud-metadata resources from its own network position and return the retrieved content as Markdown; the reported concrete payload targeted Alibaba-style metadata at http://100.100.100.200/latest/user-data. The same unguarded extraction primitive was also reachable from MCP read_url and stale-share refresh paths.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Public-history root commit 196cdd4e4191b073cd4f1762a35936471d1f2a5d, 'Initial public release', created server.js with app.get('/api') forwarding req.query.url to extractWebFn and created lib/web.js with extractWeb wrapping globalThis.fetch and executing await fetchFn(url, { headers }) without any scheme, DNS, address-range, or redirect-hop guard. It also created the MCP read_url caller. This is the first and smallest Git commit object that writes the vulnerable route/sink in the available repository: git -L and -S both terminate at that root, and the root has no parent object to contain the lines. It is not a later move, refactor, revert, release carrier, or identifiable squash carrier; there are no member commits in the available history to decompose.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: When AUTH_ENABLED=true, is_internal_request() checks an external request's optional X-Internal-Service header against the defaultless INTERNAL_SERVICE_SECRET with direct equality. If the environment variable is unset and the attacker omits the header, both lookups return None, so None == None is true. verify_api_key() then returns the trusted internal principal with scopes ["all"] before requiring an API key; that scope satisfies require_scope("admin") and permits unauthenticated creation (including admin-scoped keys), enumeration, and revocation of API keys. The /admin/generate-master-key route is not itself reachable through this bypass because it additionally requires is_master_key=true, contrary to that part of the issue/advisory impact wording.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: CWE-918 SSRF: an unauthenticated proxy caller could supply x-headroom-base-url and make Headroom issue the request to a caller-selected http(s) destination. The original catch-all route passed that value directly to handle_passthrough, which appended the inbound path, copied all inbound headers except Host (including Authorization), sent the request with httpx, and returned the upstream response. Later OpenAI and Azure/passthrough resolution paths preserved the same trust error. Without rejecting loopback, link-local, RFC1918, metadata, or other non-public addresses, a remotely exposed proxy could disclose internal-service responses and forward caller credentials to the chosen host.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated X client can use SetFontPath to expose a crafted PCF font, OpenFont to load it, and text drawing on a glamor-backed drawable to reach glamor_font_get(). The function sizes each heap-atlas slot from the PCF-declared font maxbounds but, before the fix, copied each glyph using the untrusted per-glyph GLYPHWIDTHBYTES and GLYPHHEIGHTPIXELS values without checking that they fit the slot. Because libXfont2's PCF parser does not recompute maxbounds from the glyph metrics, an oversized glyph writes attacker-controlled bytes beyond the heap allocation; negative width or height can also wrap the memcpy size or unsigned loop bound. Only glamor-backed Xorg/Xwayland servers are on this path.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 732e3b9c08532f40656010eac9d128601cc88c3f replaced one glTexSubImage2D upload per glyph with a CPU-side atlas: it allocated bits using overall_width * overall_height derived from maxbounds, then introduced a row loop whose memcpy length and iteration count came directly from each glyph. That newly combined mismatched allocation/copy geometry is the smallest source change that created the reported heap overflow.

audit_record.ai_marker: No AI marker in the BIC commit object. `git cat-file commit 732e3b9c08532f40656010eac9d128601cc88c3f` shows human author Michel Dänzer, human committer Keith Packard, Reviewed-by and Signed-off-by trailers only; it has no Co-Authored-By, Assisted-by, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI disclosure.
