In the assigned clone, `git show --format=fuller --no-renames fbf7bac22e2c6bd627fb042742a23318263edae1 -- glamor/glamor_font.c` shows the direct repair: reject non-positive maxbounds dimensions; compute gw/gh once; reject negative per-glyph dimensions or gw > glyph_width_bytes / gh > glyph_height; otherwise use the checked values in the loop and memcpy. The commit message independently explains that PCF maxbounds are trusted and that malformed per-glyph dimensions overflow or wrap.

`git log -L ':glamor_font_get:glamor/glamor_font.c' fbf7bac22e2c6bd627fb042742a23318263edae1^` traces the vulnerable atlas allocation/copy back to 732e3b9c08532f40656010eac9d128601cc88c3f. `git log --all -S'memcpy(dst, src, GLYPHWIDTHBYTES(glyph))' -- glamor/glamor_font.c` independently identifies that commit on main history (alongside equivalent objects on other refs) as the addition of the exact unchecked memcpy and the 2026 fixes as its removal.

`git show --format=fuller --no-renames 732e3b9c08532f40656010eac9d128601cc88c3f` shows the BIC adding `bits = malloc(overall_width * overall_height)` and replacing the parent's glTexSubImage2D call with `for (y = 0; y < GLYPHHEIGHTPIXELS(glyph); y++) memcpy(dst, src, GLYPHWIDTHBYTES(glyph))`, while the atlas dimensions remain derived from maxbounds. causal_chain.bug_semantics: When the optional webhook server is enabled, it listens on all interfaces and treats an empty configured token as authenticated. An unauthenticated remote POST to the configured hook path can therefore supply a JSON exec value; handleHook dispatches that value to executeShell, which passes it as the command string to the configured shell. Thus an enabled deployment with the documented empty-token setting exposes arbitrary command execution in the cc-connect process context.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Single-parent feature commit 6ae088a658077a2f11a83ded6ac53c0dbddefd38 introduced the entire vulnerable surface in one coherent change: WebhookConfig documented token empty = no auth, an externally bound HTTP server, WebhookRequest.Exec, authenticate's empty-token allow branch, handleHook's Exec dispatch, and exec.CommandContext(ctx, "sh", "-c", req.Exec). This is the first writer, not a move, refactor, release/backport, revert, or merge carrier. Later commit 6feaf90f2f8cccec2203169b4d0edc3edd538837 only generalized the shell helper and preserved the attacker-controlled command sink.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Authenticated iframe injection in the Web Previews visual inspector. An authenticated user can supply an absolute or scheme-relative external URL in the inspector's `path` query parameter. ContentLinkContext copied that untrusted value directly into `iframeState.path`; UI then put it unchanged into the configured draft-mode endpoint's `redirect` parameter and used that endpoint URL as the iframe `src`. When the draft-mode endpoint follows `redirect`, the iframe leaves the configured frontend and loads the attacker-selected external origin, bypassing the frontend-origin restriction. The advisory states Web Previews <1.0.31 is affected; repository and npm history narrow the actually present visual-editing path to published 1.0.29 and 1.0.30, with 1.0.31 the first fixed release.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 0fdfe73f8552e3fd5dcbc126ad9602346e3a1672 (`Visual Editing`) is the smallest first-writer. It created `web-previews/src/entrypoints/Inspector/ContentLinkContext/index.tsx` with `new URLSearchParams(ctx.location.search).get('path')` flowing unsanitized into `iframeState.path`, and created `web-previews/src/entrypoints/Inspector/UI/index.tsx` with `url.searchParams.set('redirect', iframeState.path)` followed by the resulting URL as the iframe source. Later commit 04aa5d9ad0506751b305cf86d18a8ca07358a906 only selected among visual-editing frontends and renamed the URL source to `currentVisualEditing`; it did not originate the untrusted redirect sink. causal_chain.bug_semantics: In the Xorg DRI2 request path, a client controls the attachment list passed by ProcDRI2GetBuffers or ProcDRI2GetBuffersWithFormat to do_get_buffers. The vulnerable code allocates count + 1 DRI2BufferPtr slots but treats requested attachment multiplicity as arithmetic: every DRI2BufferBackLeft increments need_real_front, while one DRI2BufferFrontLeft decrements it only once and also increments need_fake_front for a window. With at least two BackLeft entries and one FrontLeft, both counters remain positive after the count input entries are stored, so the function appends both an implicit real-front and an implicit fake-front buffer. causal_chain.bug_semantics: An XKB-capable local client can use XkbSetMap to replace a non-canonical key type with wire numLevels=255. CheckKeyTypes accepted every positive CARD8 width and stored it without enforcing XkbMaxShiftLevel=63. A later core ChangeKeyboardMapping reaches XkbUpdateKeyTypesFromCore; XkbKeyTypesForCoreSymbols derives groupsWidth from the attacker-controlled num_levels and uses XKB_OFFSET(g,l)=(g*groupsWidth)+l against a stack KeySym tsyms[XkbMaxSymsPerKey] buffer of 252 entries. With four groups and width 255, indices reach 1019, 767 entries beyond the buffer; the related fixed-size symbol/action temporaries make this a set of stack-overflow paths capable of server crash and, for a root X server, privilege escalation.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: With ActivityPub enabled, a remote sender can submit a signed inbound Create whose object.id is on the sender's origin but whose object.attributedTo is an attacker-chosen bare number such as 1. The inbound path does not bind attributedTo to the authenticated activity actor. Mocks.post/_normalize carries attributedTo into the internal uid, while Actors.qualify later filters numeric IDs out as already-local rather than rejecting or re-deriving the author. Public note assertion therefore creates a post under that local uid. The non-public path added later likewise turns attributedTo into the message payload uid and uses it to create/send a chat message, allowing forged posts or DMs attributed to a local user, including the administrator.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: f74775365a57262488434c920c7b805608b761c7 is the smallest functional BIC. Earlier f1e5e5a0ad4cc6d5a02bf9bc952e524fe2f58458 only stubbed the post mock and 06e1583461f034d68c8c3c6d69547b06ad6ab3b5 only moved it; neither exposed inbound Create. f74775365a57262488434c920c7b805608b761c7 simultaneously added the controller's Create dispatch and inbox.create, which fed the untrusted object through Mocks.post and into note creation without comparing object.attributedTo to req.body.actor. b82e20dfc79659c741155a866bdb48ae1b423f13 later extended the same trust flaw to non-public notes/chat, but the public-post vulnerability already existed, so it is not the BIC.

That handler calls `activitypub.mocks.post(object)`, then `activitypub.notes.assert(1, [postData])` and `assertTopic`. `git show 756548520401e1f920d358ad61ec1f28451173d5:src/activitypub/inbox.js` has follow/accept/undo only, and its controller switch has no Create case, directly proving parent absence.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The unauthenticated POST parameter request at /cgi-bin/api.values.get is parsed character by character by the Grandstream firmware's 32-bit ARM /app/bin/gs_web service. Non-colon bytes are copied into a 64-byte stack buffer and a terminator is appended without checking that the current colon-delimited component is at most 63 bytes. An overlong component therefore overwrites the stack; repeated colon-delimited components permit multiple strategically placed NUL writes, enabling a ROP chain and unauthenticated command execution as root.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A remote discovery report can carry a 255-byte EIR/advertising-data block whose first name element has field_len 254, so eir_parse derives data_len 253 and passes it to name2utf8. name2utf8 copies len attacker-controlled bytes with strncpy into utf8_name[HCI_MAX_NAME_LENGTH + 2], only 250 bytes because HCI_MAX_NAME_LENGTH is 248. The resulting three-byte stack overwrite can crash bluetoothd and can also leave the local array unterminated for subsequent strtoutf8/g_strstrip/g_strdup reads, with potential code execution depending on the build and architecture.

That new EIR-specific function introduced the fixed 250-byte stack buffer and the attacker-sized strncpy without a length clamp. Although the subject says 'Move', this is not a mere relocation of an already-vulnerable EIR sink: the parent has no name2utf8 in src/eir.c and rejects malformed EIR names; the copied event.c pattern used a fixed MGMT_MAX_NAME_LENGTH count rather than the EIR element's variable len.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated member of workspace A can send a request body containing a resource identifier owned by workspace B (for example connectionId, sourceId, or destinationId) plus an otherwise undeclared workspaceId for workspace A. AuthorizationServerHandler parses the raw JSON before endpoint-schema binding and copies both values into X-Airbyte-* headers. AuthenticationHeaderResolver.resolveWorkspace gives X-Airbyte-Workspace-Id priority over all resource-derived headers, so RBAC checks the caller's permission in A while the endpoint later acts on the B resource identifier. Because no later ownership comparison binds that resource to the authorized workspace, the caller can read configuration, trigger or cancel syncs, or delete cross-workspace resources at the privilege level held in A.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The exploitable authorization mismatch first became real in afca4a0a9861af2f5f35141fad183e65f911832d. That commit added AuthenticationHeaderResolver with WORKSPACE_ID_HEADER as the first resolveWorkspace branch, ahead of connection/source/destination lookup, and changed KeycloakTokenValidator from unconditional ADMIN to request-scoped permission lookup using that resolver. It composed unsafely with the already-present raw-body-to-header extractor introduced by ec53cc9f8267b9fda31219ecc10827f6965c6f3f. The immediate parent had the extractor and workspaceId enumeration but no AuthenticationHeaderResolver and no request-header-derived workspace RBAC decision, so it lacked the specific split between authorized workspace and acted-on resource.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: When the Management API is enabled with its token omitted or empty, its middleware treats every request as authenticated and its HTTP server listens on all interfaces. A remote caller can POST an arbitrary exec string to /api/v1/cron; that string is persisted as CronJob.Exec and executed by the cron scheduler through shellExecCommand with the shell command flag (-c on Unix). Scheduled execution is sufficient for RCE, and later commit c580b68716a7cdc6a0e6702e5782c17d074a7978 also added POST /api/v1/cron/{id}/exec for immediate execution. No shell metacharacter neutralization or command allowlist intervenes.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Single-parent feature commit c2681402a7686294174a263e31245a52d4fea380 first added the externally reachable Management API and, in the same commit, added the empty-token allow-all branch plus the cron POST endpoint that copies untrusted req.Exec into a shell cron job. Its direct parent already had cron shell execution but had no core/management.go and therefore no Management API attack path. This is the smallest commit that completed the advisory's remote unauthenticated command-execution chain; it is not a move, refactor, revert, release/backport, merge, or decomposed squash.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: When persistent proxy memory is enabled, the proxy used the client-controlled x-headroom-user-id header verbatim as the memory partition key. That value flowed into search_memories and save/update/delete operations and into context/tool handling, without authentication or any binding between the selected partition and the caller. A client able to reach a data-plane route could therefore choose another user's identifier, retrieve that user's stored LLM memory through context/search, and write or alter memory in that partition. The flaw began on the original Anthropic memory-enabled proxy path, was later copied to OpenAI Chat Completions, Gemini, OpenAI Responses, and OpenAI websocket paths, and was practically network-reachable in the reference compose deployment because it bound the proxy to 0.0.0.0 and published port 8787 without requiring HEADROOM_PROXY_TOKEN. Fix 1f96dabc19130947770353cd6e814db4fd96e6a0 centralizes identity selection in resolve_memory_identity: the header is honored only for a loopback peer (or by a deployment-supplied authenticated resolver); a remote peer instead gets the configured proxy-token fingerprint or OS-user fallback. The same fix requires a proxy token in the shipped compose file.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The smallest public-history BIC is da743418584725e8b9c3315dc1aea7cf5e949192, not the April OpenAI handler additions or the later handler split/refactors. In headroom/proxy/server.py it added memory_user_id = headers.get("x-headroom-user-id"), required only that the caller supply a nonempty value, then passed that untrusted value to MemoryHandler.search_and_format_context and MemoryHandler.handle_memory_tool_calls. The same commit created headroom/proxy/memory_handler.py, where the user_id argument directly scopes backend search_memories and save_memory operations. causal_chain.bug_semantics: SPIP 4.4.20's analyse_resultat_skel() parsed each PHP block and applied an anchored header() regular expression with the PCRE m modifier. Because m makes ^ and $ match individual lines, an attacker-controlled newline followed by header("X-Spip-Filtre: intval|_request|system") inside a larger compiled PHP block was accepted as if the whole block were an intended SPIP header emission. X-Spip-Filtre was then interpreted as a pipe-delimited callable filter chain: intval produced key 0, _request read attacker-controlled POST parameter 0, and system executed that value, yielding unauthenticated remote command execution.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The vulnerable product code is in upstream SPIP's spip/ecrire repository, not rapid7/metasploit-framework. On the SPIP 4.4 branch, d369f5a49c3593f18b1c81fc3a3051bd0bed1e1d replaced the old whole-body header extractor with CollecteurPhp plus an anchored per-PHP-block /ims matcher. This was the 4.4.20 remediation for the preceding all-version RCE, but carrying m into the newly anchored matcher created the CVE-2026-77806 bypass. The Rapid7 commit referenced by the advisory, b16eca819abb8f1401f21d115e71e3dfc67b847c, only adds a Metasploit exploit module and documentation and is neither the BIC nor the fix.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: With OAuth enabled behind a reverse proxy that terminates browser-facing HTTPS and forwards to Temporal UI Server over HTTP, authentication cookies used c.Request().TLS != nil to choose Secure. Because that request describes only the proxy-to-server hop, the server emitted the user* access/ID-token cookies and, later, refresh-token cookies without Secure even though the browser authenticated over HTTPS. Exploitation additionally requires steering the UI hostname to attacker-served HTTP, preventing HTTPS, and receiving a later same-site plaintext request while the credential is live; a malicious page alone or passive observation of the successful TLS session is insufficient.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: temporalio/ui-server PR #219 moved the OAuth user session into browser cookies. Its sole source commit 8bca548c78fcadc737626bea96ef1e16075792d6 introduced the sensitive user* cookie and set Secure from c.Request().TLS. GitHub squash commit 821cf598371353f1b579dfe1e87aeb3638b041d6 landed the identical tree and patch. The code was later imported into temporalio/ui, and the 2026 refresh-token work extended the same incorrect transport inference to a longer-lived HttpOnly refresh cookie; those moves and extensions are not the first BIC.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: When LiquidJS renders attacker-controlled template source with memoryLimit enabled, evalRangeToken meters a range as high - low + 1. A reverse range such as (100000000..1) therefore passes a large negative count to Limiter.use(); the vulnerable limiter accepts it and subtracts it from its cumulative base. Later positive allocations then satisfy base + count <= limit despite exceeding the configured budget. Repeated append operations can build a 134217728-character V8 cons-string, and replace forces flattening into a contiguous buffer, producing an uncatchable V8 fatal error and process-wide denial of service.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 2af297f81ac465feb3277ba7b92f7236409370b0 attempted to fix unmetered ranges in for tags by adding exactly ctx.memoryLimit.use(high - low + 1) to evalRangeToken, but assumed low <= high. Its direct parent already had the generic Limiter, whose signed accumulator did not reject negative counts, but did not meter ranges and therefore lacked this reverse-range counter-poisoning path. The BIC is the smallest commit in which the advisory's signed range charge and permissive limiter coexist; it is a direct one-parent change, not a move, refactor, revert, release commit, or squash aggregate.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: CVE-2026-44645 / GHSA-8xx9-69p8-7jp3 is a CPU/event-loop denial of service in LiquidJS's renderLimit control. The for and tablerow parsers store their bodies as Template[] arrays. An empty body therefore makes each collection iteration call Render.renderTemplates([], ctx, emitter). In vulnerable releases, the only ctx.renderLimit.check(...) was inside `for (const tpl of templates)`, so an empty array executed no check while the outer for/tag or tablerow/tag loop still traversed the entire attacker-selected collection; tablerow additionally emitted table markup. A low-privileged author of an untrusted Liquid template could use an empty `{% for i in (1..N) %}{% endfor %}` or empty tablerow to consume CPU far beyond the configured time budget, bounded only by other resource controls such as memoryLimit.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The smallest true BIC is e443068cb9281883ff0fe9f755a15f52ada4e7e2 (`feat: DoS prevention, #250`). That commit introduced the renderLimit option, its Limiter state, the documented security guarantee, and the sole enforcement call in src/render/render.ts inside the per-template loop. causal_chain.bug_semantics: The default-registered strip_html filter runs a lazy-alternation regular expression directly over caller-controlled template data. For inputs containing many '<script', '<style', '<!--', or generic '<' openers without their required terminator, V8 retries a tail-spanning lazy match at each opener, producing O(N^2) work and blocking Node's single event loop. At the last vulnerable revision, src/filters/html.ts charges only str.length to memoryLimit (whose default is Infinity), so that accounting neither caps nor interrupts regex CPU consumption.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The smallest true BIC is 8e9e10fdb4c7f00ffa3997d3e2c0a0bfa48ce887. It changed filters.js strip_html from /<\/?\s*\w+\s*\/?>/g to /<script.*?<\/script>|<!--.*?-->|<style.*?<\/style>|<.*?>/g, first introducing the repeated tail scans responsible for this ReDoS. Later commits only transported or modified the already-vulnerable expression: 677e8511e60a7cc789dd33a4f295a46beeaf1137 copied it into src/builtin/filters/html.ts during the TypeScript refactor, 42d25902e855d3c06d5ead071bf55604f495c205 broadened three alternatives to [\s\S], and 26ea2856c7a90aec892b98d94a9b7a3e18539045 broadened the generic tag alternative. None is the first causal writer.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: LiquidJS formed include/render/layout candidate names beneath configured root, partials, or layouts directories and then opened those names without canonicalizing them. An attacker who can place a symlink under an allowed template directory can point it at any readable file outside the directory: the lexical pathname passes the root check, Node follows the symlink during stat/read, and the external target is parsed and rendered. This affects async and sync loading and can disclose arbitrary readable content; the advisory records liquidjs <=10.25.2 as vulnerable and 10.25.3 as the first patched release.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: LiquidJS strip_html used a regular expression that did not consume attacker-controlled HTML tags containing line terminators. For example, <img\nsrc=x\nonerror=alert(1)> survives the filter, while a browser treats the newlines as attribute whitespace and executes the event handler when the rendered result is inserted as HTML, enabling stored or reflected XSS in applications that rely on strip_html as a sanitizer.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The vulnerability began when 4595e2872e7800b93b0d6e487430431a0402f0b2 first added strip_html using /<\/?\s*\w+\s*\/?>/g. That implementation only removed simple attribute-free tags, so the advisory payload with newline-separated attributes already survived. Commit 8e9e10fdb4c7f00ffa3997d3e2c0a0bfa48ce887 later replaced it with the Ruby-Liquid-style alternatives including <.*?>; this is the exact dot-does-not-match-line-terminators mechanism described by the advisory, but it is not the causal BIC because the same payload also survives its parent. Commit 42d25902e855d3c06d5ead071bf55604f495c205 made script, style, and comment alternatives multiline-aware with [\s\S] while leaving the generic <.*?> branch vulnerable. Refactors and moves through 2024 preserved that branch.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Preact's client renderer accepts only genuine VNodes, whose createVNode path gives them an own constructor value of exactly undefined. The regression changed the JSON-injection gate in src/diff/index.js from newVNode.constructor !== UNDEFINED to the coercive newVNode.constructor != UNDEFINED (and similarly softened related VNode checks). An attacker-controlled JSON object can therefore supply constructor:null: because null == undefined, the loose inequality is false and the gate does not reject the object. If unvalidated JSON-derived data is passed as a child/render value, an object such as {type:'span',props:{children:'Malicious'},__v:1,constructor:null} is treated as a VNode and can inject HTML, potentially script-capable markup absent CSP. The server-side preact-render-to-string path was not affected.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: SRS accepts an unauthenticated RTMP publisher when vhost security is absent or disabled. A remote client on TCP/1935 can complete RTMP negotiation and a publish command without credentials; SRS returns NetStream.Publish.Start and accepts publisher traffic. Later functional media fanout permits content injection, stream-name occupation, and resource/bandwidth abuse. The referenced reporter PoC uses connect -> createStream -> publish and treats NetStream.Publish.Start as confirmation. The public report expressly says this is missing authentication/insecure default configuration, not memory corruption or code execution; therefore the NVD/GHSA arbitrary-code-execution wording is not supported by its cited technical report or by the audited source path.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The smallest causal BIC is 33c586181de6b3a0cee61022066cb6e61c666972. It is the first commit that decodes the RTMP publish command, receives the FMLE publish request, and emits onFCPublish/onStatus NetStream.Publish.Start without an authentication decision. Its parent had only preliminary releaseStream/FCPublish negotiation and rejected the resulting publisher type in SrsClient's switch. Follow-on commits made the accepted publisher fully useful: ed371d6e7e6e03415865d032a59c41c410ac58fe integrated the publish service loop, 940d2f02eb6149fcd93b2a6e338cf8bbf2484e56 connected audio/video to a source, 150489af51ebc26551b69808b4d750fb2f557e43 implemented working consumer queues/fanout, and 359c7da19ba1fc95be0a0a46ba3ccb9bc7d8de74 added the direct createStream -> publish path used by the published PoC. Commit 75f2607685814b86ad030df703834cf06f91447f later added optional allow/deny security, but deliberately preserved the already-vulnerable default (security off means allow all), so it is mitigation history rather than the BIC.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: In the administrator-only Downloads deletion action, a nonce-authenticated POST supplied file_id, file, file_name, and unlinkfile. The handler sanitized file only as text and, when unlinkfile was 1, passed the attacker-controlled value directly to unlink($file_path . $file). sanitize_text_field() does not remove ../ traversal components, so an authenticated user with the manage_downloads capability (assigned to administrators) could replace the hidden file field with traversal sequences and delete an arbitrary file reachable by the PHP process. Deleting a critical file such as wp-config.php can cause availability/integrity loss and may enable code execution through reconfiguration. The nonce and capability check prevent an unauthenticated path but do not bind the posted pathname to the selected database row.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The smallest true first-writer is WordPress Subversion changeset r7446 (2007-01-21, GamerZ, log 'WP-DownloadManager First Commit'), which added trunk/downloadmanager/download-manager.php with the posted file value flowing to unlink($file_path . The assigned Git repository's 2013 commit 8c862546f81e81283cb2afeea193a6b7ac522b50 is a later import of already-vulnerable version 1.61 and is therefore not the BIC.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated WordPress administrator with the plugin's manage_downloads capability can submit a download_path such as WP_CONTENT_DIR . '/../../etc'. Versions 1.68.11 through 1.69 compare only the uncanonicalized string prefix with WP_CONTENT_DIR, so the traversal-bearing value passes and is persisted. The Add/Edit File browser then recursively enumerates that resolved directory, an administrator can register a selected file, and the download handler concatenates the persisted base path with the selected relative name and serves it with readfile(), exposing files outside wp-content (subject to the configured per-file permission). Before 1.68.11 the setting was even less constrained and accepted arbitrary paths directly.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: a141c14127eb8d72413ac6a11dd3e7ad66aef9b1 is the smallest single-parent commit that first added the vulnerable WP_CONTENT_DIR prefix validator. Its substr($download_path, 0, strlen(WP_CONTENT_DIR)) comparison is lexical, not canonical filesystem containment, so '..' components retain the approved textual prefix while resolving outside it. The commit simultaneously identifies itself as release 1.68.11. Its immediate parent directly stores download_path and contains no prefix-validator lines; thus the specific prefix-check bypass is absent there, although the older unrestricted setting already allowed the same confidentiality impact without needing traversal.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A local attacker can create a filesystem entry whose name contains terminal control bytes such as ESC-led OSC or CSI sequences. When a victim runs the interactive TUI, marks that entry, and quits, dua-cli tears down the TUI/terminal guard and then prints each remaining marked PathBuf with println!("{}", path.display()) to stdout without encoding or filtering control characters. On an attached terminal those bytes are interpreted rather than displayed, permitting terminal-title spoofing, clipboard manipulation, and terminal-dependent integrity/confidentiality effects; ratatui's protected in-TUI rendering is bypassed because this output occurs after the TUI exits.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Feature commit 017cbd7b4c3e57e1a98fbc595159be39bc97c708 implemented issue #87's request to print marked paths on interactive exit. It simultaneously added MarkPane::into_paths(), extracted marked paths from the app, and introduced the raw post-TUI println!("{}", path.display()) sink without terminal-safe escaping. Later commits only reorganized or reformatted this already-vulnerable path.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated backend user holding backend.manage_editor can store attacker-controlled LESS in Editor Settings -> Markup Styles (html_custom_styles). A payload such as .x { content: ~"</style><script>alert(1)</script><style>"; } makes Less_Parser preserve literal closing-style/script markup. In vulnerable releases the compiled string is emitted unescaped inside the backend-wide <style> block, so the injected script executes for later backend-page visitors. The compiled raw value is also cached, making this a stored XSS path.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit c9dab67bc819b791df8432a898dd976f19388a87 reintroduced the flaw by changing modules/backend/layouts/_custom_styles.php from <?= strip_tags(EditorSetting::renderCss()) ?> to <?= EditorSetting::renderCss() ?> while ostensibly improving exception-message escaping. causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated backend user who can reach a list view supplied by a plugin with a Backend\Widgets\Filter numberrange scope and a conditions string can send attacker-controlled JSON numbers to onFilterUpdate(). numbersFromAjax() used /\d/ as its entire validation rule, so any string containing one digit (for example, a numeric prefix followed by SQL syntax) survived unchanged. applyScopeToQuery() then used strtr() to splice the two values into the configured conditions and passed the resulting SQL to whereRaw(), making the suffix executable SQL. causal_chain.bug_semantics: A backend user granted backend.manage_branding can persist custom_css through Settings -> Customize Backend -> Styles. BrandSetting::compileCss() concatenates that value into LESS input; LESS escape syntax such as .x { content: ~"</style><script>alert(1)</script><style>"; } preserves attacker-controlled HTML delimiters in the compiled output. modules/backend/layouts/_custom_styles.php places BrandSetting::renderCss() verbatim inside a <style> element from the shared backend head/auth layouts, so the injected </style><script> sequence becomes stored script executed for later backend-page viewers. The prerequisite is trusted backend access with the specific branding permission, but the victim need only load a backend page.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 1203043a457dee3c298d7dd54289a866234cbb74 is the smallest first-writer: in modules/backend/models/BrandSettings.php it changed the LESS parse input from only the bundled custom.less file to that file concatenated with self::get('custom_css'). Its immediate parent already had the settings field, compiler, and style sink, but did not feed custom_css to the parser, so attacker-controlled markup could not reach rendered_css. The same commit also stored compiled CSS for the layout; it is an ordinary one-parent commit, not a move, revert, release carrier, or squash aggregate.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated backend user holding any one granular Theme Editor permission could enter Cms\Controllers\Index because the controller authorization was an OR gate, while its AJAX handlers trusted the request-supplied template type and performed no permission check for that type. Such a user could open, save, create, delete, commit, or reset pages, partials, layouts, content, or assets outside the granted scope. The constructor also registered AssetList without cms.manage_assets, and its upload path lacked the theme validation used by other mutating asset handlers, permitting an otherwise unauthorized user to upload an allowed file into the active theme's assets.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The public history first acquires the vulnerable authorization design in 71a5dd67ab9e0d0da7caabd3fb5aaa3d86bb45e5: that commit adds the CMS controller and AssetList, registers the distinct cms.manage_* permissions, sets the controller gate to cms.*, unconditionally constructs all per-type widgets, and implements request-type-driven handlers without a corresponding per-type authorization check. Commit 55848e400cea002491a29820e5387bce0dd44362 later replaces cms.* with an explicit five-permission list but retains hasAnyAccess OR semantics and all missing handler checks. Commit c03fd66aeb8a6f10290381a76db0867fabe881e6 later exposes the pre-existing upload-processing body as public onUpload() without adding validateRequestTheme(), extending the same access-control defect rather than originating the cross-template flaw.

audit_record.ai_marker: No AI marker. `git cat-file -p 71a5dd67ab9e0d0da7caabd3fb5aaa3d86bb45e5` shows human author and committer `Sam Georges <sam@daftspunk.com>` and only the message `Welcome to the world, October :-)`; there is no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer in the BIC commit object.
audit_record.bug_semantics: An authenticated backend user holding any one granular Theme Editor permission could enter Cms\Controllers\Index because the controller authorization was an OR gate, while its AJAX handlers trusted the request-supplied template type and performed no permission check for that type. Such a user could open, save, create, delete, commit, or reset pages, partials, layouts, content, or assets outside the granted scope. The constructor also registered AssetList without cms.manage_assets, and its upload path lacked the theme validation used by other mutating asset handlers, permitting an otherwise unauthorized user to upload an allowed file into the active theme's assets.
evidence: The assigned first-party GHSA bundle states that versions <= 1.2.12 are vulnerable and 1.2.13 is first patched; it describes the five-permission controller OR gate, missing per-template checks, unconditional AssetList registration, and missing validateRequestTheme() in onUpload().

Run `git show 55848e400cea002491a29820e5387bce0dd44362^:modules/backend/classes/Controller.php` around line 213: controller authorization calls `hasAnyAccess($this->requiredPermissions)`, proving OR semantics. `git show 55848e400cea002491a29820e5387bce0dd44362 -- modules/cms/controllers/Index.php` shows only the gate changing from cms.* to the explicit five permissions, with handlers and unconditional widget construction left unchanged.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Any authenticated Winter CMS backend user could send a crafted My Account/My Settings save request for their own Backend\Models\User record and make the form behave as an administrative update form. The self-service action was deliberately exempted from backend.manage_users, while FormController treated the POST form_context value as authoritative. Selecting the update context caused normally excluded role, group, permission, and superuser fields to enter the widget save data, and the User model had no actor-aware authorization invariant before persistence. The user could therefore assign their own higher role/permissions or superuser status.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Inherited pre-fork October CMS code supplied the unsafe combination's prerequisites in 71a5dd67ab9e0d0da7caabd3fb5aaa3d86bb45e5 (the generic form context came from post('form_context') and the current-user save endpoint reused the administrative FormController). The smallest real commit that completed the advisory's any-backend-account attack path was the later, focused one-file commit 94a4ccb6abccd025e7e201590999061574ffdeb9: it cleared Users::$requiredPermissions specifically for mysettings, exposing that unsafe save path to accounts without backend.manage_users. A later attempt in b121e03608135c921673d3b02d9ca293ca28c66a to pass the mysettings context did not close the issue because the posted form_context still overrode it.

audit_record.reasoning: The initial 2014 import is a broad prerequisite, not the smallest commit completing the advisory-scoped flaw: before 94a4ccb6abccd025e7e201590999061574ffdeb9, an ordinary backend account without backend.manage_users could not enter the Users controller. The focused BIC deliberately removed that gate for self service without isolating the administrative form context or enforcing authorization in the model. causal_chain.bug_semantics: ScpClient.Download(string, DirectoryInfo) accepts C (file) and nested D (directory) record names from the remote SCP protocol stream, extracts the server-controlled filename without validation, and combines it with currentDirectoryFullName. A malicious, compromised, or MITM server can supply ../ components or an absolute/drive-qualified path so Directory.CreateDirectory or FileInfo.Open/Create operates outside the caller's destination, enabling arbitrary file creation or overwrite wherever the client process can write. Exploitation requires the victim to initiate a recursive directory download from the attacker-controlled endpoint.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The flaw originated in the initial ScpClient feature commit: d96c93abb2f9409281bfb12d2da8622470a4b3e3 added recursive SCP download parsing and both local filesystem sinks, directly concatenating the untrusted D/C record filename below currentDirectoryFullName with no plain-name or containment check. Later commits only restyled, moved, or refactored these already-vulnerable lines.

audit_record.ai_marker: BIC commit-object check: `git cat-file -p d96c93abb2f9409281bfb12d2da8622470a4b3e3` identifies both author and committer as `olegkap_cp <olegkap@gmail.com>` at Unix time 1323285149 and contains only the three-line message `Minor fix to ASCIIEncoding`, `Add ScpClient to support SCP feature with limited featres supported in silverlight and WindowsPhone environment`, `Add ScpClient test`; it has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-assistant, or bot marker.

Exploitation requires the victim to initiate a recursive directory download from the attacker-controlled endpoint.
evidence: First-party GHSA-q939-rpr3-3284 states the affected API is `ScpClient.Download(string directoryName, DirectoryInfo directoryInfo)`, the attack is a malicious/compromised/MITM SCP server returning traversal or absolute names, affected versions are >= 0 and <= 2025.1.0, patched version is 2026.0.0, and remediation commit is 600be0de543765995a189b5d7cd4efac5007f3ce.

At 600be0de543765995a189b5d7cd4efac5007f3ce^ (c66b9f8fb06c12e71761e58a577b1e796026310f), `src/Renci.SshNet/ScpClient.cs` parses `${filename}` from DirectoryInfoRegex/FileInfoRegex and passes it unvalidated to `Directory.CreateDirectory(Path.Combine(currentDirectoryFullName, filename))` and `new FileInfo(Path.Combine(currentDirectoryFullName, fileName))`, after which the file is opened with FileMode.Create/FileAccess.Write.

`git show 600be0de543765995a189b5d7cd4efac5007f3ce -- src/Renci.SshNet/ScpClient.cs` shows the direct closure: it adds EnsureValidLocalName and invokes it immediately before both Path.Combine sinks. The helper rejects empty, `.`, `..`, and any character in Path.GetInvalidFileNameChars, covering separators and platform-specific drive qualifiers before filesystem access.

`git blame` of the pre-fix sinks first points to the 2023 merge/refactor 42ff9206d22d90af4083ffe8483276daee289bfe; inspecting that commit shows it moved the same InternalDownload implementation out of ScpClient.NET.cs, so it is not the BIC. Exploitation additionally requires the relevant c3p0 datasource, a susceptible JDBC driver, and an automatic bean-property-reading carrier on the classpath.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An attacker-controlled imported Typebot could contain a Script block whose code was returned as a client-side action and compiled and executed by @typebot.io/js in the preview page with AsyncFunction/Function. Preview ran under the victim's authenticated app.typebot.io browser context, so the script could issue same-origin credentialed requests. It could enumerate the victim's credentials and call credentials.getCredentials to obtain decrypted OpenAI keys, Google tokens, SMTP secrets, and other stored credential data, then exfiltrate them. The user-scoped getCredentials branch did bind the record to user.id; the workspace branch checked that the victim could write the supplied workspace but fetched the credential by id without additionally binding it to that workspace. Either way, arbitrary script in the victim's session defeated the intended principal boundary. The missing control was distrust/sandboxing of imported client-executed code during privileged preview, not JavaScript syntax validation.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The affected @typebot.io/js executor lineage was created by pull-request member commit 3487850b9f4808617d347ddde4d9701f56662894. It added packages/js/src/features/blocks/logic/code/utils/executeCode.ts with Function(...args, content) and invoked it for server-supplied code actions, with no import provenance, preview trust decision, consent, or sandbox. GitHub squash commit 1a3869ae6d9fa92fc71ef9d981bfffb8e4ee4ecc has the same parent and tree, so it is only the landed aggregate object, not the smallest recoverable commit object. A still earlier legacy bot-engine Code-step executor existed in e3e07ddd4dbae6e7b893a0d6be9f12b80d1a6c9c, but it is not the affected @typebot.io/js file/package lineage: 3487850b created the distinct V2 embed package implementation that was subsequently released as @typebot.io/js.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: PyBlade evaluates expressions embedded in templates as Python. In the v0.1.4-alpha tag (and still in v0.1.8-alpha/v.0.1.9-alpha), PyBlade.render calls Parser.parse, whose directive handlers pass template-controlled @if/@for and other expressions to eval(..., {}, context); because the globals mapping omits __builtins__, Python inserts the normal builtins, so a template can call __import__ and execute commands. The v0.2.0-alpha rewrite keeps the vulnerability through Processor.render_variable -> ExpressionEvaluator.evaluate -> safe_eval -> eval(expression, {"__builtins__": SAFE_BUILTINS}, context); expressions containing parentheses take that direct-eval path, and Python object-model chains can recover dangerous classes/globals. The advisory's narrower claimed v0.1.8/v.0.1.9 _is_safe_ast Constant bypass is contradicted by the tagged source: for every ast.Attribute whose value is not ast.Name, including ''.__class__, the function reaches its unconditional return False, and no released engine code imports or calls sandbox.safe_eval. Thus the releases are vulnerable, but through reachable raw eval rather than the alleged AST-validation bypass, and the tracked vulnerable tag boundary is at least as early as v0.1.4-alpha.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: b8dc54a607b9c4e420e648e2a31b2667e48e68bb is the smallest first-writer: it creates pyblade/engine/directives.py and writes the raw eval in _parse_if (plus another raw eval in _handle_for). Its direct parent b764131c740566b1f82d7c411dc13b3a804c6b8f has neither PyBladeDirectives nor an eval sink under pyblade/engine. Commit 4b193b1aa86d146eebeae442c4fd871c7a93515f subsequently wires PyBladeDirectives into PyBlade.render, so it is the activation commit, not the first writer. causal_chain.bug_semantics: getFilenameFromUrl treats a textual publicPath prefix as containment. With a non-slash-terminated publicPath such as /assets, /assets../.env passes pathname.startsWith('/assets'). The 2024 UP_PATH_REGEXP guard tests path.normalize('./' + pathname), where the only '..' is embedded in the segment 'assets..' and therefore is not rejected. Slicing at publicPathPathname.length then changes the same characters into the standalone relative path '../.env'; path.join(outputPath, '../.env') escapes one directory above outputPath. The escaped file is disclosed when the selected outputFileSystem exposes physical files (not the default isolated memfs), notably writeToDisk === true or a supplied filesystem. URL parsing/normalization limits this particular bypass to one parent level; publicPath 'auto' maps to '/' and is not affected.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: OliveTin registered dashboard stream subscribers in a shared client collection and sent every action's execution-start, execution-finish, and output payloads to every subscriber. The subscriber's identity was retained but never checked against that action's log ACL before delivery, so a low-privilege authenticated dashboard user could receive protected action metadata, tracking IDs, usernames, live chunks, and final command output. Ordinary log APIs did enforce per-action authorization.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit e5a870ed9443d315a1cc95fd3acfd75e7ed9e1d3 first made execution output a global live broadcast: it created internal/websocket/websocket.go, registered every websocket connection in clients, and made OnExecutionFinished serialize the complete LogEntry (including Stdout and Stderr) and call broadcast, which iterated all clients without an action/user authorization decision. Its parent had action-view ACL enforcement but only a passive websocket stub and no execution-output broadcast. Commit db5de9be9793be65e2a77ab71656713f97bc779b later added the explicit Logs permission and filtered GetLogs while leaving the broadcast unfiltered; ac0f3ab6f8346157b1b2a47737ef237e0ae3af8f added globally broadcast live output chunks. The 3k API port a62d58f11955fe192f45da13e23ba996a2759404 carried the existing flaw into Connect EventStream rather than originating it.

The closing fix also handles OAuth2's separate registeredStates store.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: OliveTin separately authorizes action execution and access to action logs. A caller with exec:true and logs:false can invoke the synchronous StartActionAndWait or StartActionByGetAndWait RPC; each vulnerable handler waits for execution, retrieves its InternalLogEntry, converts it to the protobuf LogEntry (including stdout/stderr-derived Output and execution metadata), and returns it without the logs authorization used by GetLogs, GetActionLogs, ExecutionStatus, and EventStream. This is a post-execution authorization bypass and confidentiality disclosure, not an execution-ACL bypass.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A Shell-mode action may declare an argument type beginning with regex:. The custom pattern is checked with regexp.MatchString, but checkShellArgumentSafety historically compared only exact names in a fixed unsafe-type map and therefore allowed every regex:-prefixed type. The accepted attacker value is inserted without shell quoting into the configured command and executed through sh -c. causal_chain.bug_semantics: The unauthenticated GET /images endpoint accepted an attacker-selected http(s) src, fetched the response into a Buffer, detected SVG through sharp, and rasterized it at density 300 with limitInputPixels explicitly disabled before encoding with toBuffer(). A crafted SVG containing deeply nested use-element shadow trees or enormous pattern tiles therefore drives unbounded CPU/memory consumption in sharp/libvips and can deny service. The public attack described by the advisory chains the unrestricted external fetch with this unsafe SVG rasterization.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 5ed5ba31913ae69d617089988aa4ffe8015d6143 created both packages/evershop/src/modules/cms/pages/frontStore/images/images.ts and packages/evershop/src/modules/cms/services/imageProcessor.ts. It first wrote the arbitrary external fetch and the SVG branch using density: 300 and limitInputPixels: false. Its immediate child a839543becedb75324a16c38194eb4c64ba5f635 added route.json for GET /images, activating the newly written handler; merge commit 871308d68bfdefd934045ab16aa19e6239d6cb1e then merged that ordinary two-commit PR branch. The smallest source-writing origin is 5ed5ba31913ae69d617089988aa4ffe8015d6143, not the route activation or merge aggregate.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The public storefront GraphQL order query accepts a caller-controlled order UUID and loads the matching order without authenticating the caller or constraining the query to the current customer or guest session. A remote unauthenticated caller who obtains a valid UUID can therefore read another customer's order and nested PII-bearing fields such as customer identity, billing/shipping addresses, purchased items, totals, payment status, and shipment data.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 685f3baf290024133c45986100fc7296ee14c85e is the smallest true first-writer of the authorization flaw. In packages/core/src/modules/checkout/graphql/types/Order/Order.resolvers.js it removed tokenPayload-derived customerId/sid ownership predicates from Query.order and replaced the protected order_id lookup with only query.where('uuid', '=', id). The original resolver commit 44a884b59e51d29f5022aa5b482b6c12e56ebfaa was protected, and immediate parent b398f43d4d2eedf39abf9e3658820941cbd4babd still contains that protection. Later commit 52db55816458c657a7ed49dfb27daf9f280e2169 merely removed the now-unused tokenPayload parameter, and 72d478a748e7994b46f7aecee9a849a9ef15db43 renamed the public schema argument from id to uuid; neither is the BIC.

audit_record.bug_semantics: The public storefront GraphQL order query accepts a caller-controlled order UUID and loads the matching order without authenticating the caller or constraining the query to the current customer or guest session. A remote unauthenticated caller who obtains a valid UUID can therefore read another customer's order and nested PII-bearing fields such as customer identity, billing/shipping addresses, purchased items, totals, payment status, and shipment data.
audit_record.evidence: Advisory and attack path: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c73g-mx2w-cc93 identifies CVE-2025-12919, @evershop/evershop <=2.1.0, and `Patched versions: None`; https://github.com/ictrun/Evershop-Order-leak/blob/main/README.md gives an unauthenticated GraphQL request using order(uuid: $uuid) and enumerates the returned order PII. In the clone, packages/evershop/src/modules/graphql/api/graphql/route.json declares GET/POST `/graphql` with `access: public`; Order.graphql declares `order(uuid: String!): Order`; and Order.resolvers.js builds getOrdersBaseQuery(), applies only `where('uuid', '=', uuid)`, loads it, and returns camelCase(order), without consulting request identity or the tracking-token status. BIC: from the clone run `git log --all --follow -S"query.where('uuid'" -p -- packages/evershop/src/modules/oms/graphql/types/Order/Order.resolvers.js`; it identifies only 685f3baf290024133c45986100fc7296ee14c85e for first insertion. `git log -L 8,18:packages/core/src/modules/checkout/graphql/types/Order/Order.resolvers.js 685f3baf290024133c45986100fc7296ee14c85e` traces the protected origin through 44a884b59e51d29f5022aa5b482b6c12e56ebfaa and the authorization-removing change at 685f3baf290024133c45986100fc7296ee14c85e. Parent absence: `git diff b398f43d4d2eedf39abf9e3658820941cbd4babd 685f3baf290024133c45986100fc7296ee14c85e -- packages/core/src/modules/checkout/graphql/types/Order/Order.resolvers.js` shows deletion of `const { customerId, sid } = tokenPayload`, `where('order_id', '=', id)`, `andWhere('customer_id', '=', customerId)`, and `or('sid', '=', sid)`, replaced by the UUID-only predicate. Merge shape: 685f3baf290024133c45986100fc7296ee14c85e has one parent and is a preserved member of PR #130; `git show --no-patch --format=raw c6022cedb0a86f4af2c394b2af9aa804177a0f8e` shows a two-parent merge, so there is no squash aggregate to decompose. Versions/fix: `git tag --contains 685f3baf290024133c45986100fc7296ee14c85e --sort=version:refname` lists every available release tag from 1.0.0-rc.9 through v2.2.1. `git show 1.0.0-rc.9:packages/evershop/src/modules/oms/graphql/types/Order/Order.resolvers.js` and the same command at v2.2.1 both show the UUID-only lookup with no ownership condition. Thus the advisory's <=2.1.0 range is stale relative to later tags: v2.1.1, v2.1.2, and v2.2.1 remain vulnerable. HEAD ac7a6e66f4017a0386e59a2550511e98c85ce6f0 also retains the same resolver, and full-ref `git log --all --follow -S'tokenPayload' -p -- .../Order.resolvers.js` shows the protection removed at the BIC and never restored. Marker: `git cat-file commit 685f3baf290024133c45986100fc7296ee14c85e` reproduces the human identity and marker absence.
audit_record.flaw_origin: Commit 685f3baf290024133c45986100fc7296ee14c85e is the smallest true first-writer of the authorization flaw. In packages/core/src/modules/checkout/graphql/types/Order/Order.resolvers.js it removed tokenPayload-derived customerId/sid ownership predicates from Query.order and replaced the protected order_id lookup with only query.where('uuid', '=', id). The original resolver commit 44a884b59e51d29f5022aa5b482b6c12e56ebfaa was protected, and immediate parent b398f43d4d2eedf39abf9e3658820941cbd4babd still contains that protection. Later commit 52db55816458c657a7ed49dfb27daf9f280e2169 merely removed the now-unused tokenPayload parameter, and 72d478a748e7994b46f7aecee9a849a9ef15db43 renamed the public schema argument from id to uuid; neither is the BIC.
audit_record.reasoning: The vulnerability is an authorization regression, not the initial existence of an order lookup: the first implementation required the requested order to match either tokenPayload.customerId or tokenPayload.sid, while 685f3baf290024133c45986100fc7296ee14c85e deleted both constraints and made UUID existence the sole condition. The immediate parent directly proves absence, -S and -L converge on the same smallest first-writer, later argument renames and refactors preserve the mechanism, and the commit is a preserved PR member rather than a squash merge. Upstream has not closed the flaw: the newest available release tag and clone HEAD still expose it, so both fix fields are null. Under the required BIC-commit-object-only AI rule, the BIC has a human author/committer and no explicit AI attribution or bot marker; therefore the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
audit_record.remaining_gap: Unpatched upstream as of clone HEAD ac7a6e66f4017a0386e59a2550511e98c85ce6f0 and latest available release tag v2.2.1 (abfdabcacfc49ad0df1f262c34bc46af721f2537); consequently no fix commit or direct fix commit exists to record. This is an unpatched boundary, not an unresolved causal or AI-evidence gap.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Reflected XSS in the legacy Rucio WebUI: an attacker-controlled account (or another request value) is included verbatim in a Rucio exception; generate_http_error_flask serializes it as ExceptionMessage in the response body and headers; error callbacks concatenate jqXHR.responseText/ExceptionMessage into markup passed to jQuery.html(), so a victim opening a crafted authenticated WebUI URL executes attacker HTML/JavaScript in the WebUI origin. The exposed JavaScript token and non-HttpOnly session cookie amplify the result to credential theft or actions as the victim.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: 045193619da3087de74d77ec0f715ce57c1ed035 is the smallest commit that creates the advisory's demonstrated account_rse_usage flow. Its new account_rse_usage.js reads url_param('account'), sends it to get_account_limits/get_account_usage, and on either error executes $("#results").html('<font color="red">' + jqXHR['responseText'] + '</font>'); the new file and page do not exist in its immediate parent. Later edits retained those two sinks until the security fix. A still earlier 2014 direct-query-parameter subbar XSS family was also closed by the companion fix commit, but it does not create the advisory's specifically described 500 ExceptionMessage path and is therefore not substituted for this BIC.

audit_record.ai_marker: Absent on the BIC commit object. `git cat-file -p 045193619da3087de74d77ec0f715ce57c1ed035` shows human author and committer Thomas Beermann <thomas.beermann@cern.ch>, subject `[RUCIO-640] add new account usage page + add human readable file sizes`, and only a Gerrit `Change-Id: I127ad60197cde1848035a1878b3369dec2f67c86` trailer; there is no AI Co-Authored-By, Generated-with trailer, bot identity, or other AI attribution.

(2) `git log -L '/^load_data = function/,/^};/':lib/rucio/web/ui/static/account_rse_usage.js 574a0b4787ab7dfd29ee0536c7da55b34e902788` traces the unchanged sinks through 045193619da3087de74d77ec0f715ce57c1ed035; `git log --all --reverse -S"jqXHR['responseText']" -- lib/rucio/web/ui/static/account_rse_usage.js` independently reports that commit as the first addition. (3) `git show 35.8.2:lib/rucio/web/rest/flaskapi/v1/common.py` shows ErrorHandlingMethodView forwarding `error.args[0]` to generate_http_error_flask, `_error_response` placing the raw string under `ExceptionMessage`, and generate_http_error_flask rendering that dictionary in the response while also adding ExceptionMessage headers. (6) `git cat-file -p 045193619da3087de74d77ec0f715ce57c1ed035` supplies the BIC-only metadata quoted in ai_marker; the commit has one parent and creates the feature directly, so no squash or merge decomposition is applicable.

Its new account_rse_usage.js reads url_param('account'), sends it to get_account_limits/get_account_usage, and on either error executes $("#results").html('<font color="red">' + jqXHR['responseText'] + '</font>'); the new file and page do not exist in its immediate parent. audit_record.reasoning: The causal unit is not the longstanding server convention of returning exception text by itself: executable behavior begins when the new WebUI page accepts an attacker-controlled account and passes the resulting response text into jQuery's HTML parser. Commit 045193619da3087de74d77ec0f715ce57c1ed035 introduces that complete, independently exploitable source-to-sink chain in one ordinary one-parent feature commit, while its direct parent lacks the page. History -L and -S reject later plotting changes, moves, and release backports as introducers. causal_chain.bug_semantics: picklescan trusted its extraction and denylist classification of pickle GLOBAL/STACK_GLOBAL references to decide whether a file was dangerous. A cloudpickle payload can instead serialize a reconstructed Python function: its visible globals are cloudpickle.cloudpickle helpers such as _make_function and _builtin_type, while a CodeType bytecode object implements getattr(builtins, "eval")(payload). Before the fix those reconstruction primitives were not in _unsafe_globals, so they were at most Suspicious and did not increment issues_count or infected_files. A consumer relying on that clean result could then unpickle the attacker-controlled file, reconstruct and invoke the hidden function, and execute the attacker payload on the loading host.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit c1d5abdcc740e0d08a0d12d015d08e1e6f29a67e first introduced the scanner and its vulnerable blacklist-only decision: scan_pickle_bytes extracted global names, looked each module up in _suspicious_globals, and incremented issues_count only for an explicit module/name match. The direct parent contained no scanner source at all. Later refactors retained the same security boundary by making unlisted imports merely Suspicious rather than Dangerous, so they did not create the bypass.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: nltk.data.find() normalized and checked the still-encoded resource name, then passed it to urllib.request.url2pathname() while constructing a filesystem path. url2pathname() turns percent-encoded dot and separator sequences such as %2e%2e and %2f into ../ and / after the textual safety decision. A caller controlling the resource name supplied to nltk.data.find() or nltk.data.load() could therefore make the resulting path escape nltk.data.path and read any process-readable file. The attack requires an application to pass untrusted resource names into those APIs.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 51ceb7517237d78b843a95db56629b11d41ede2b changed find() from os.path.join(path_, resource_name) to os.path.join(path_, url2pathname(resource_name)) (and made the analogous zipfile-name change) to convert resource names into Windows paths. That new late decoding step is the smallest change that made a percent-encoded traversal become a real traversal at filesystem access. causal_chain.bug_semantics: OpenAM's shipped iPlanetDirectoryPro SSO-session cookie is script-readable because com.sun.identity.cookie.httponly defaults to false and, through 16.0.6, has no shipped SameSite value. Any same-origin XSS can therefore read and replay the authenticated SSO token; cross-site delivery is also broader without SameSite. The OAuth/OIDC consent implementation compounded this by using that same SSO token value as the csrf form value, so script that obtains the session token also satisfies the consent check.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Stored XSS in the authenticated WebUI RSE-management flow. A privileged attacker can create an RSE with HTML/JavaScript in city, country_name, or ISP; add_rse.js serializes those values unchanged into POST /rses/<RSE>, and the backend persists them. Later, the /rses listing supplies the server values directly to DataTables, while /rse?rse=<RSE> builds table-row HTML by concatenating the returned values into jQuery append calls. Either sink parses the stored metadata as markup, so merely viewing the listing or detail page executes attacker JavaScript in the victim's WebUI origin. The advisory notes JavaScript-readable session/API tokens and same-origin privileged requests as impact amplifiers.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Direct, single-parent feature commit 8f1a24a568331b10f9d8fb099ef233af340b7735 added the RSE create/list/detail WebUI in new files. It simultaneously introduced the persistence path in add_rse.js, the raw DataTables listing sink in rses.js, and the raw string-concatenation table sink in rse.js; this is original vulnerable code, not a move, refactor, revert, backport, or merge carrier.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Stored XSS in the legacy Rucio WebUI account-identity table. A privileged attacker can use Admin > Account Management > an account > Add Account Identity (POST /proxy/accounts/<account>/identities) to persist an identity such as <script>alert(document.cookie)</script>. When a victim opens /ui/account?account=<account>, load_identities() obtains the stored identity through r.list_identities() and used to pass the returned objects directly to jQuery DataTables as `data: data`; the `identity` and `type` columns were therefore rendered as HTML rather than output-encoded text. JavaScript executes in the WebUI origin with the viewing user's authority, permitting token/cookie theft or authenticated actions. The closing change constructs a separate display object and HTML-encodes identity/type with `$('<div>').text(String(value)).html()` while retaining raw `$identity`/`$type` only for API operations.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 4f67434304e5bd445c01a636d88113b76a68ef78 (`[RUCIO-2849] RucioUI account admin pages`) is the smallest public first-writer. It created lib/rucio/web/ui/static/account.js and the account page, adding both the identity creation flow and load_identities(), whose DataTable consumed the server-returned identity objects without encoding. It is a normal one-parent feature commit, not a move, revert, release/backport, merge wrapper, or reconstructable squash; its parent had the identity-list API client but no account page, identities table, or vulnerable display sink.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The default metadata-filter converters for Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, and GemFire interpolate a Filter.Key into a Lucene/query_string expression. An embedded tab, newline, carriage return, or ideographic space (U+3000) was not backslash-escaped, so attacker-controlled key text could terminate or split the intended field token and inject Boolean/query syntax. The generated string is passed to Elasticsearch/OpenSearch queryString queries (including OpenSearch delete-by-query) or to GemFire as filterQuery, permitting execution of an arbitrary query rather than the intended metadata predicate.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The earliest affected implementation is Elasticsearch support commit 9334d7d540f8d0ee7cb09e44b272c95c2c159627, which created ElasticsearchAiSearchFilterExpressionConverter.doKey and appended the trimmed metadata-prefixed key directly to the query string without syntax escaping. OpenSearch later copied the same unsafe doKey shape in 46e47849cec4b8a6fffbd13997f3cce4f886347b, and GemFire filter support introduced it in 78c5e001d39e40f0da1f5b7b2b78a38f2047c01f. March 2026 hardening routed these keys through emitLuceneString, but that helper still escaped only ordinary ASCII space and Lucene punctuation, leaving tab, LF, CR, and U+3000 exploitable until the advisory fixes.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The volume-target PATCH handler authorized baremetal:volume:update, loaded the complete existing VolumeTarget, applied even an unrelated permitted patch such as one to extra, persisted it, and serialized the returned object with convert_with_links without either enforcing baremetal:volume:view_target_properties on the response or masking password-like values in properties. A project-scoped caller allowed to update a target but forbidden to view target properties could therefore use the 200 PATCH response to read pre-existing iSCSI credentials. POST also returned properties unredacted, but those values had just been supplied by that caller and are not the confidentiality escalation at the root of this CVE.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The response-sanitization omission was introduced with the original volume-target REST API in c380e05dbf84079b01fb3b0ea099ef9b293b9b3d (released in 9.0.0). It became a privilege-boundary vulnerability when project-scoped volume target access was added in e870bd34d0ccacbaef7f4e4def2535eb28f822b9, which is contained in 17.0.0 but no 16.* tag. Later commit 000bc72cc29b8637df496f2e6768281606a27058 only converted the endpoint representation and preserved the same unsanitized PATCH response, so it is a refactor rather than the BIC.

evidence: First-party OSSA-2026-023 (https://security.openstack.org/ossa/OSSA-2026-023.html) describes valid POST/PATCH access to /v1/volume/targets returning sensitive properties such as iSCSI credentials; its note says the code path existed since 9.0.0 but became a privilege escalation after 17.0.0 with project-scoped owner/lessee access. It declares affected ranges >=17.0.0 <29.0.6, >=30.0.0 <32.0.2, >=33.0.0 <35.0.2, and >=36.0.0 <37.0.1, and links the master and stable fixes.

In the read-only clone, `git log 00eda8b9c6391574ec8226a8c560aa51651d2019 -L 323,407:ironic/api/controllers/v1/volume_target.py` follows the PATCH function back to c380e05dbf84079b01fb3b0ea099ef9b293b9b3d, where the new file first loaded the whole target, applied a patch, updated it, then executed `api_target = VolumeTarget.convert_with_links(new_target)` and returned it without redaction. The history also shows 000bc72cc29b8637df496f2e6768281606a27058 merely changing the representation while preserving that behavior.

The independent pickaxe `git log --all -S'api_target = VolumeTarget.convert_with_links(new_target)' -- ironic/api/controllers/v1/volume_target.py` returns only c380e05dbf84079b01fb3b0ea099ef9b293b9b3d (addition) and 000bc72cc29b8637df496f2e6768281606a27058 (representation rewrite), corroborating c380e05dbf84079b01fb3b0ea099ef9b293b9b3d as the smallest public-history origin rather than the later refactor.

Direct parent verification: `git ls-tree -r --name-only ddcd97714cd5b27ac43ac0ef1138c13392223b90 -- ironic/api/controllers/v1/volume_target.py ironic/api/controllers/v1/volume_connector.py` produces no output, while `git show c380e05dbf84079b01fb3b0ea099ef9b293b9b3d -- ironic/api/controllers/v1/volume_target.py` shows the file as `new file mode 100644` with the vulnerable POST/PATCH implementations. Thus the vulnerable lines are absent from the immediate parent.

Release-boundary checks: `git tag --contains c380e05dbf84079b01fb3b0ea099ef9b293b9b3d --list '9.0.0'` returns 9.0.0 and the corresponding '8.*' query returns nothing. `git tag --contains e870bd34d0ccacbaef7f4e4def2535eb28f822b9 --list '17.*'` includes 17.0.0 while the '16.*' query returns nothing. For a released stable boundary present in the clone, direct backport 49bff4c09acfdf195f40f911236b9ac5c6def3c5 is contained in 29.0.6 and in no earlier 29.0.* tag. The remaining first-patched versions are those declared by OSSA/GHSA; their direct backports are present on the corresponding remote stable branches even where this frozen clone has no resulting release tag.

Fix verification: parent 00eda8b9c6391574ec8226a8c560aa51651d2019 has view_target_properties checks on read paths but PATCH line 404 directly converts new_target and has neither target_sanitize nor mask_dict_password. `git show dd2df520fe0ae019cb247a8295542abc2d4b46dd -- ironic/api/controllers/v1/volume_target.py` adds target_sanitize using strutils.mask_dict_password for all serialized properties and adds a PATCH-time baremetal:volume:view_target_properties check that invokes _redact_target_properties before conversion. The advisory directly references dd2df520fe0ae019cb247a8295542abc2d4b46dd, so fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are identical.

BIC-only AI check: `git cat-file -p c380e05dbf84079b01fb3b0ea099ef9b293b9b3d` shows author Satoru Moriya, committer Hironori Shiina, three named human Co-Authored-By trailers (Tomoki Sekiyama, David Lenwell, Hironori Shiina), Change-Id and Partial-Bug trailers, and no bot identity, AI co-author, Assisted-By, Generated-with, or other AI marker. No later commit's marker is used for the verdict.

Later commit 000bc72cc29b8637df496f2e6768281606a27058 only converted the endpoint representation and preserved the same unsanitized PATCH response, so it is a refactor rather than the BIC.
audit_record.reasoning: The original 2017 volume-target API commit is the causal code origin because it first created the PATCH response path that serialized the full updated object without secrecy enforcement; its parent has no volume-target API file. Line history and pickaxe both distinguish that origin from the 2020 plain-JSON refactor. Project-scoped RBAC later made the omission exploitable across a real privilege boundary, but it did not write the unsafe response behavior and therefore does not replace the smallest BIC. The direct security fix closes both layers by enforcing the view-properties policy on PATCH and by masking password-like fields during all target serialization. causal_chain.bug_semantics: In releases before 1.0.4, PickleScan extracted explicit GLOBAL, INST, and STACK_GLOBAL references and checked those names against a finite unsafe-global blocklist, but it did not interpret the callable/value flow produced by REDUCE. An attacker can therefore encode pkgutil.resolve_name as the only visible global, call it with a data string such as 'os:system' in a first REDUCE to obtain a blocked callable, and invoke that returned callable in a second REDUCE. Because pkgutil.resolve_name was not in the blocklist and the eventual os.system reference never appears as a pickle global, the malicious pickle had issues_count == 0 despite executing arbitrary code when unpickled. The gadget makes every blocklisted target reachable through the same indirection.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The flaw originates in the first scanner implementation, commit c1d5abdcc740e0d08a0d12d015d08e1e6f29a67e. That commit created src/picklescan/scanner.py with an explicit _suspicious_globals blocklist, _list_globals logic limited to GLOBAL and STACK_GLOBAL, and scan_pickle_bytes logic that increments issues_count only when the extracted module/name is present in that list. pkgutil.resolve_name was neither listed nor semantically followed through REDUCE. This is the smallest repository commit that created the vulnerable security decision; it is not a move, refactor, revert, release-only commit, or squash aggregate.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Stored XSS in the Rucio WebUI rule-approval flow: an authenticated low-privilege user can submit attacker-controlled HTML/JavaScript in POST /proxy/rules/ as the rule comment. The backend persists that value in the rule's comments field and list_rules returns it. approve_rules.js copied the entire server object into a DataTables data source and declared the comments property as a display column without a text renderer or output encoding, so DataTables inserted the stored value as HTML when an administrator reviewed waiting-approval rules. Script then executes in the WebUI origin, with the victim's session/API-token authority. The advisory also identifies a rule-detail viewing trigger; the directly demonstrated root sink in history is the unescaped approval-table comments column.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 010746bc16b72313d1e779fa9a15996c44b40a9f created lib/rucio/web/ui/static/approve_rules.js and, in one atomic feature commit, introduced the vulnerable chain: list_rules server data is pushed unchanged into filtered_data, passed to DataTable, and the raw {'data': 'comments'} property is displayed. The immediate parent already accepted and persisted rule comments through the REST/API/core path, but had no approve_rules.js sink, so this is the smallest first-writer rather than a later move, refactor, release commit, or squash.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The MCP-exposed ado installer accepted an attacker-controlled package/command string and interpolated it without validation into Stata source. A value such as `outreg2\nshell touch /tmp/stata_mcp_ado_poc\n//` therefore introduced a second Stata statement; Stata's `shell`/`!` escape executed that statement as an OS command with the server user's privileges. In the advisory-era implementation, the default CLI selected profile `all`, `_TOOL_REGISTRY` included `ado_package_install` in `all`, the wrapper forwarded `package`, `SSC_Install.install()` formed `f"ssc install {package}{self.REPLACE_MESSAGE}"`, and `StataController.run()` delivered it to the interpreter. The guard blacklist did not protect this separate install path.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The smallest true BIC is b61cd574b86bb6aa3a931ed637de0fb66ce82607, not the later installer-framework commit. Although titled as a directory-renaming refactor, b61cd574b86bb6aa3a931ed637de0fb66ce82607 independently added the complete `@mcp.tool(name="ssc_install")` entry point in `src/stata_mcp/__init__.py`: its unvalidated `command` argument was embedded into `write_dofile(f"ssc install {command}...")` and executed by `stata_do`. Commit 51e4bf3aff9e188de931ae77686bd42bc77524da merely moved that tool to `mcp_servers.py`; 0001cec1135824bc77dca6fe116ac6b06a2c8c4d later introduced the equivalently vulnerable `SSC_Install.install()` class; and 28e0757d5d0df5a9c6be257218e277dff332659e rewired/renamed the existing MCP tool to `ado_package_install`. Those later commits preserve or refactor an already exploitable flaw and are not the BIC.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: In the legacy (non-ZIP) PyTorch path, scan_pytorch validated the first pickle's magic value with get_magic_number(), which statically searched pickletools.genops() for an INT/LONG opcode. PyTorch instead unpickles that object. An attacker can make __reduce__ invoke eval to compute the correct MAGIC_NUMBER without an INT/LONG opcode, then place an RCE pickle later in the legacy stream. PyTorch accepts and executes the stream, while vulnerable scan_pytorch obtains None, raises InvalidMagicError before scanning the six-pickle stream, and reports no dangerous globals for the payload.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The original legacy-PyTorch support commit implemented semantic validation by statically extracting the first INT/LONG opcode rather than accounting for the fact that PyTorch unpickles the magic object; the same commit gated all subsequent pickle scanning on that incomplete result.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An unauthenticated POST to the WebUI /ui/login endpoint reaches userpass_auth(). For a nonexistent username, select_account_name() yields no ui_account and the handler immediately renders a response saying that no account is associated with that identity. For an existing username paired with a wrong password, execution instead attempts get_auth_token_user_pass() and renders a different cannot-get-auth-token response. Comparing those response bodies therefore reveals whether the supplied username exists (CWE-204); analogous distinct account/token failure responses were also present in the SAML paths.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A malicious pickle can encode STACK_GLOBAL/GLOBAL ("profile", "run") followed by REDUCE with attacker-controlled Python source. Unpickling resolves the module-level profile.run(), which passes that source to Profile.run() and ultimately exec(). PickleScan's exact module/name lookup did not flag profile at all in early releases; by v1.0.3 it looked up name "run" against {"Profile.run", "Profile.runctx"}, so the exact comparison still missed the executable global and returned issues_count == 0.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated or otherwise protocol-reachable Kyuubi client can supply a local-file URI in Spark path-bearing session/batch configuration. When kyuubi.session.local.dir.allow.list is nonempty, the server accepted the URI whenever the unnormalized uri.getPath string began with an allowed directory. An absolute path such as /allowed/../outside/secret therefore passes the textual startsWith check, but the downstream filesystem/Spark consumer resolves .. and uses a local file outside the allow list. This bypass exposes server-local files to frontend clients.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The vulnerable textual-prefix authorization check was first written in source commit 4f2faa6a22541ef850f5b049149e08ab6fd4c49b, the first member of PR #2991. Apache merged that ten-commit PR as squash b585fb4257995d5dd8905c0a25e62a13a1264b77. Later source commits moved/refactored the check, but did not create the missing-normalization flaw.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: ChaiScript's built-in async() launched a std::async worker executing a script closure that could continue using its Dispatch_Engine after the owning ChaiScript instance began destruction. If that worker raised eval_error while the main thread destroyed the engine, error formatting called Dispatch_Engine::get_type_name and Type_Info::bare_equal over entries in the concurrently freed type map, producing the reported heap-use-after-free. The dereference in bare_equal is the observed sink, not the lifecycle root cause; the missing ownership/join relationship for engine-spawned workers is the flaw.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 52d03a66b15358e8fd2caeb5b063044c8aa839d2 first registered the script-visible async function in include/chaiscript/chaiscript_stdlib.hpp as a direct std::async(std::launch::async, t_func) call and returned only its future, without registering the spawned work with Dispatch_Engine or making engine destruction join it.
