causal_chain.bug_semantics: A script-controlled integer right operand reaches Boxed_Number::go for assign_remainder. In the vulnerable implementation, the assign_remainder arm executes *t_lhs %= c_rhs without first calling check_divide_by_zero(c_rhs); a zero operand therefore invokes integer remainder by zero and terminates the process with SIGFPE. The public PoC reaches this path with ret %= i when i is initially zero, including from an async script task, making this an availability flaw.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit dd918c524d0bc9d081df723f42e18874874e4cf7 rewrote boxed-number dispatch to use if constexpr and inlined the assignment switch. During that rewrite it replaced the previously protected binary_int_go assign_remainder path with a newly written bare *t_lhs %= c_rhs, dropping the existing zero-divisor guard. Commit 9bbe7238278f96141b51ab4c6e5313ffc2879bea shortly afterward restored guards for ordinary remainder and quotient assignment but accidentally put the intended assign-remainder guard in the assign_bitwise_and arm, so this specific regression persisted through 4804fb6e036dc325f56eecde8e875717a357e187.

audit_record.ai_marker: No AI marker on the BIC. `git cat-file -p dd918c524d0bc9d081df723f42e18874874e4cf7` shows human author and committer Jason Turner <jason@emptycrate.com>, subject `Use if constexpr in boxed_number`, and no message body, Co-Authored-By/Generated-with trailer, or bot identity.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Upright exposed all-verbs Prometheus and Alertmanager proxy routes to session-authenticated browser users while both proxy controllers called skip_forgery_protection and forwarded the request method, path, and body to their upstream services. An unauthenticated attacker could induce a logged-in victim's browser to issue a cross-site request carrying the ambient session (including a Lax-cookie top-level GET) and reach enabled upstream write or management operations such as creating an Alertmanager silence or requesting Prometheus /-/reload; there was no Fetch-Metadata, Origin, or equivalent provenance gate.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The public repository does not contain the true implementation origin. dbf67daef2c624c1d5f01ef4233a8bccb3c927aa first adds both skip_forgery_protection proxy controllers to this repository in a 58-file, 2,918-insertion commit explicitly titled 'Move UI and Traceroute probe to engine', but its routes do not expose them. 29b423ea9e0cec753da97105afccf7a694a5b0e6 later adds the all-verbs proxy routes and completes the reachable vulnerable chain in a 98-file, 3,427-insertion/1,905-deletion commit explicitly titled 'Continue extraction of Upright core'. Both are import/extraction aggregates rather than the smallest commit that originally designed the vulnerable proxy, and the pre-extraction source history is absent from this clone.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The constant-integer for-loop optimizer bound the script loop variable to a native stack-local int through var(&i). ChaiScript's intentional := reference-assignment semantics could copy that reference into ret; after the optimized-loop lambda returned, ret (including a value returned through async/future) still pointed at the destroyed stack slot. Converting fut.get() during string interpolation then dereferenced the dangling numeric pointer in Boxed_Number::get_as<int>(), producing garbage or an ASan-invalid read/segmentation fault.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 683164650a462b6d5ea58bb899f4c2e668243a1d, 'Add ability to compile for loops', first added the specialized compiled-for-loop path in include/chaiscript/language/chaiscript_parser.hpp and created 'int i = for_loop_params.start; t_ss.add_object(for_loop_params.id, var(&i));'. Later commit ff2ab6bb8dfc72f89128382d73b7d36ebcb4630a merely moved that existing mechanism into chaiscript_optimizer.hpp, so it is not the BIC.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: ChaiScript accepted recursively re-entering user-defined script functions without any maximum call-depth check. The disclosed script defines string::`/=` so its body evaluates `${this/= 2}`, immediately dispatching the same operator again; eval_function and AST_Node_Impl::eval repeatedly enter Function_Push_Pop/new_function_call until the native thread stack is exhausted and the host aborts with stack-overflow/SIGSEGV. An attacker needs a local path to make the host evaluate supplied ChaiScript, and the resulting impact is denial of service.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: ChaiScript's script-visible async() launched a callable with std::async(std::launch::async, ...) but the ChaiScript/Dispatch_Engine did not own or join the resulting worker. A script could start asynchronous work and finish while that work was still resolving identifiers. Engine teardown on the main thread then freed shared Dispatch_Engine state, including map nodes in the symbol/object tables, while a worker still used that state. A subsequent heterogeneous std::map lookup read a freed std::string key through chaiscript::str_less::operator(), producing the reported heap-use-after-free. str_less is the observed ASan crash site, not the causal ownership defect. The issue #632 PoC launches two async functions that repeatedly access undefined re6 and then lets the script end without waiting for the futures, creating the teardown/read race.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The smallest true BIC is 52d03a66b15358e8fd2caeb5b063044c8aa839d2, which first added future support and registered script async() as a direct std::async(std::launch::async, t_func) call in include/chaiscript/chaiscript_stdlib.hpp without engine lifetime tracking or a teardown join. Its sole parent a32a180a063d9186ca38b2708a9c19d50da378db has no <future> include, future type, async registration, or std::async launch. Later commits 630c618ae7d87bd7bee7979997f31bad7fecd803, 5ff97979fd85db218112f0a69d21fe2f95ef9abc, 7ab6bce7faf0ba466b38a9ed31ccbdadbbd99ecd, 70cdbef69333a5fecd6e9e034d9e1428a544c8a5, and cff6a0acedbc1b8e53aeef118570929b50a711c9 only adjusted wrapping/module APIs or formatting around the already-vulnerable launch and are not introducers.

The HTML provider reads the stored ConfigBean attribute and concatenates it into generated markup without HTML/attribute encoding; the reported payload begins with a double quote and contains , breaking out of the generated value attribute and creating an executable element. JavaScript then runs in the Administration Console origin and can read information or issue requests with the victim administrator's session.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A remote unauthenticated attacker can submit an unlimited sequence of incorrect administrator credentials to either /j_security_check (j_password) or /management/domain (HTTP Authorization). Before the fix, each request is authenticated immediately and a failed attempt merely returns the login error/HTTP 401; no per-user/host attempt state, delay, concurrency cap, or temporary lockout makes online brute-force guessing progressively more expensive.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The smallest causal origin recoverable from public history is javaee/glassfish commit 0fee8143d3ad099bb7b4583785693957c838523a (SVN r29730), which added the REST wrapper and its security path for /management/domain. RestAdapter.authenticate invokes AdminAuthenticator for every request and, on false, immediately emits 401 plus WWW-Authenticate: BASIC without retaining failed-attempt state. Its parent exposed /management/domain directly and had no authenticated failed-login path. Commit c1f1b2942b2a657eb61e707069dd4ea9d3e3a730 later expanded the same omission to the Admin Console: AdminConsoleAuthModule accepted /j_security_check credentials and posted them to REST, forwarding failure to the error page without throttling. Eclipse commit 571714739b23e16c4c90d5229b806433920b3bcb is only the 2018 Initial Contribution snapshot; following the files in the public predecessor history decomposes that aggregate to 0fee8143d3ad099bb7b4583785693957c838523a rather than treating the import or later moves as the BIC.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Genkit's unauthenticated developer servers accepted requests on non-loopback interfaces without validating the HTTP Host header. A LAN peer, or a website using DNS rebinding, could invoke registered actions through the Tools/Dev UI runAction API with attacker-controlled input and context (including forged context.auth) and read the result; the telemetry trace SSE endpoint additionally widened CORS to '*', exposing action traces. CORS origin response headers were not an authorization gate.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The earliest public carrier is GitHub squash aggregate 91ed3de52e7db92943886526395ad8eac6faa77f ('Added runner, action reflection, and typed registry. (#3)'). It simultaneously makes `genkit start` start a Runner API, adds the unauthenticated runAction proxy, and adds a Reflection API whose `/api/runAction` executes registry actions while both Express servers call `listen(port)` without a host or Host check. Its message enumerates many squashed member changes, including 'Added basic Reflection API', 'Added starting of app code when starting Runner API', and 'Implemented passthrough endpoints in Runner API'. The member commit objects/parents needed to distinguish which smallest member first completed the vulnerable path are not in the public repository, so the aggregate is not recorded as the BIC.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Command_OPEN_POWERSHELL built a PowerShell -Command program by interpolating the directory of the edited file directly into a single-quoted Set-Location argument. Because an apostrophe in a Windows directory name was not escaped, a crafted path such as C:\safe'; Start-Process calc; #' terminates the string and appends attacker-chosen PowerShell. A victim need only open a file from that directory and invoke Open PowerShell or Open PowerShell as Administrator; the latter can execute after the UAC flow with elevated rights.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Atomic commit 3340e0d352a795ddfaf89214e66f7989371b21c7 changed the pre-existing PowerShell-command skeleton from a cmd.exe /k cd invocation to powershell.exe with `-NoExit -Command "Set-Location -Path '%s'"`, passing strFolder.c_str() without PowerShell single-quote escaping. That exact semantic conversion first created the injection; the immediately preceding skeleton commit still invoked cmd.exe and therefore did not contain this PowerShell parsing flaw.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: RustCrypto ml-dsa signature decoding used one non-strict monotonicity predicate for both hint cuts and per-polynomial hint indices. The cuts may repeat, but FIPS 204 HintBitUnpack requires the indices within each polynomial to be strictly increasing. Changing the index check from < to <= therefore lets an attacker duplicate a hint index in an otherwise valid signature and have the non-canonical byte string accepted, creating signature malleability across ML-DSA-44, ML-DSA-65, and ML-DSA-87. The assigned c2sp/wycheproof repository is reference/test-vector provenance, not the repository containing the vulnerable verifier: its repeated-hint cases are correctly marked invalid.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Before the fix, both PATCH /boards/{boardID}/blocks/{blockID} and the batch PATCH /boards/{boardID}/blocks endpoint treated a comment as an ordinary board block. An authenticated user with board-wide PermissionManageBoardCards (the editor capability) could name a comment created by another member and alter its title/fields: the handlers checked board access/association but did not compare block.CreatedBy with the session user or require the elevated PermissionDeleteOthersComments capability. The single endpoint then called PatchBlockAndNotify and the batch endpoint called PatchBlocksAndNotify, so the unauthorized patch reached persistent storage. The fix loads each target and, for TypeComment with CreatedBy != userID, rejects the request unless PermissionDeleteOthersComments is present; it also preserves the original creator/create time in the insert/history path.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The smallest reconstructable BIC is PR #877 member 7c1d63a9d9ee6a5f82655f780196d96f35cdd12e ('Adding support for patch blocks'), not the mainline squash c734cfb8d16b1a4a20e3fb03b3afdf052fa53fce. That member first registered a session-authenticated PATCH-by-block-ID route and implemented handlePatchBlock as getContainer -> decode arbitrary BlockPatch -> App.PatchBlock, without loading the target for a comment-owner authorization decision. Its parent already supported the 'comment' block type and rendered comments, but had no PATCH route or handlePatchBlock. Later 3450eb6d4ffda75d303f53795b3d7c38cecd2330 added the batch variant; aa540e73ce669a1acd491a5edd7d55199ef1b87c converted the guard to board-wide PermissionManageBoardCards while retaining the missing object-owner check; c1f2ae63165dfc5a162b6d364c3f1644e5114a1c only moved the handler to server/api/blocks.go. The October 2025 deletion fix 80c4012a52f3d59ef38ddde90f12cb761b33caa6 protected deletion of others' comments but left modification exposed.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: When STOMP auto-create is enabled, an authenticated principal holding only SEND or CONSUME permission can request an unsupported routing type in a SEND destination-type or SUBSCRIBE subscription-type header. The vulnerable STOMP path sees the existing address, copies its routing-type set, adds the requested type, and calls ActiveMQServer.updateAddressInfo directly, bypassing the ServerSession CREATE_ADDRESS security check. Because checkRoutingSemantics runs only after this mutation, it sees the newly added type and accepts the operation. The result is an unauthorized persistent augmentation of the address routing semantics.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit d773e8f66b5db2b0fcaa646384c24690d38aaa69 intentionally added support for STOMP clients to use the same address with different routing types. Its new existing-address branch performed the update through manager.getServer().updateAddressInfo rather than the authorization-enforcing ServerSession API, creating the root authorization bypass.

Because checkRoutingSemantics runs only after this mutation, it sees the newly added type and accepts the operation. The result is an unauthorized persistent augmentation of the address routing semantics.
evidence: The Apache oss-security announcement at https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/05/27/8 identifies ARTEMIS-5996/CVE-2026-40914, describes unauthorized routing-type augmentation by a STOMP user with only send or consume permission, declares 2.0.0-2.44.0 and 2.50.0-2.53.0 affected, and recommends 2.54.0.

`git show d773e8f66b5db2b0fcaa646384c24690d38aaa69 -- artemis-protocols/artemis-stomp-protocol/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/artemis/core/protocol/stomp/StompConnection.java` shows the first existing-address branch: when the requested type is absent and auto-create-addresses is enabled, it copies existing types, adds the requested type, and invokes `manager.getServer().updateAddressInfo(simpleQueue, routingTypes)`. The same commit's tests explicitly say a STOMP send should alter an existing address to support the second routing type.

At the BIC, `git grep -n -E 'autoCreateDestinationIfPossible|checkRoutingSemantics' d773e8f66b5db2b0fcaa646384c24690d38aaa69 -- .../StompConnection.java .../VersionedStompFrameHandler.java` shows mutation before validation on both paths: subscribe lines 692/694 and send lines 190/192 call autoCreateDestinationIfPossible before checkRoutingSemantics.

Direct parent verification: `git show e937c9903f9fa429c23fe50a3fd49e99ad2de0b9:artemis-protocols/artemis-stomp-protocol/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/artemis/core/protocol/stomp/StompConnection.java` shows autoCreateDestinationIfPossible acts only when getAddressInfo is null, creates through `session.createAddress`, and contains no existing-address routing-set update. Its subsequent checkRoutingSemantics rejects a requested type absent from an existing address.

Independent origin checks agree: `git log 53173375c4d5e4b57890e89d37ed8b666c974474^ -L '/public void autoCreateDestinationIfPossible/,/^   }/':artemis-protocols/artemis-stomp-protocol/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/artemis/core/protocol/stomp/StompConnection.java` traces the vulnerable branch to d773e8f66b5db2b0fcaa646384c24690d38aaa69; `git log --all --reverse -S'manager.getServer().updateAddressInfo(simpleQueue, routingTypes)' -- .../StompConnection.java` returns d773e8f66b5db2b0fcaa646384c24690d38aaa69 as the addition and ede2051960ddd6bf5657076fe5889f18a5699c6c only as a later refactor/removal of that spelling.

Release introduction: tag 2.5.0 resolves to 5f5b1dcf8f731b53d1b271fdde46dddacdd71bd7 and has no `updateAddressInfo(simpleQueue, routingTypes)` hit; tag 2.6.0 resolves to bcaa11c2eea681d5758398be0b8c2ff8ae2c2878 and contains it at StompConnection.java:297. `git tag --contains d773e8f66b5db2b0fcaa646384c24690d38aaa69` begins at 2.6.0 and includes every existing release tag through 2.44.0 and then 2.50.0 onward. Thus direct history narrows the exact mechanism's effective floor to 2.6.0, despite the advisory's conservative 2.0.0 floor; no 2.45.0-2.49.0 tags exist.

Closing fix: `git show 53173375c4d5e4b57890e89d37ed8b666c974474` deletes the duplicated direct update and changes both SEND and SUBSCRIBE to StompConnection.checkAutoCreate, which calls `getSession().getCoreSession().checkAutoCreate(QueueConfiguration...)`. In tag 2.54.0, ServerSessionImpl.checkAutoCreate updates an existing address by calling ServerSessionImpl.createAddress, whose line `securityCheck(art.getName(), CheckType.CREATE_ADDRESS, this)` enforces the missing permission.

Fix boundary: `git grep -n -E 'updateAddressInfo\(simpleDestination|checkAutoCreate\(destination' 2.53.0 -- .../StompConnection.java .../VersionedStompFrameHandler.java` finds the vulnerable direct update at StompConnection.java:197. The same command at 2.54.0 finds checkAutoCreate at StompConnection.java:491 and VersionedStompFrameHandler.java:196 and no direct update. `git tag --contains 53173375c4d5e4b57890e89d37ed8b666c974474` returns 2.54.0, 2.55.0, and 2.56.0, making 2.54.0 the first fixed release.

`git cat-file commit d773e8f66b5db2b0fcaa646384c24690d38aaa69` directly verifies the full parent e937c9903f9fa429c23fe50a3fd49e99ad2de0b9, human author/committer identities, 2018 timestamps, and complete absence of AI trailers or bot identity. The commit has one parent and is the narrow ARTEMIS-1794 implementation, not a merge, release/backport, revert, move, or squash aggregate.
audit_record.flaw_origin: Commit d773e8f66b5db2b0fcaa646384c24690d38aaa69 intentionally added support for STOMP clients to use the same address with different routing types. Its new existing-address branch performed the update through manager.getServer().updateAddressInfo rather than the authorization-enforcing ServerSession API, creating the root authorization bypass.
audit_record.reasoning: The vulnerability is caused by the newly added direct server update, not by later renames or refactors. The parent cannot mutate an existing address and instead rejects a mismatched requested routing type, while d773e8f66b5db2b0fcaa646384c24690d38aaa69 adds exactly the mutation that makes the later semantic check self-satisfying. The direct fix 53173375c4d5e4b57890e89d37ed8b666c974474 removes that bypass and delegates to a session path that checks CREATE_ADDRESS. Tag and source checks establish introduction in 2.6.0, persistence through 2.53.0, and closure in 2.54.0; the published lower bound of 2.0.0 is broader than the exact code history. AI attribution is judged solely from the BIC object. It contains only named human identities and no AI/bot marker, so reporter credit to bugbunny.ai and any properties of the 2026 fix are irrelevant and the correct verdict is NOT_AI.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: With address auto-creation disabled, an authenticated OpenWire client can request a non-durable JMS topic subscription for a nonexistent address. AMQConsumer creates a random, non-durable temporary queue on that address; the broker implicitly creates the temporary address after checking only queue-creation permission, not CREATE_ADDRESS. The unauthorized address persists until the OpenWire connection closes, when temporary resources are removed.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: 84e8a87325a976c9970b8e85d03fc33207623af3 introduced Artemis's independent CREATE_ADDRESS permission and explicit address model while retaining the OpenWire non-durable-topic path that creates a temporary queue and the server queue-creation path that implicitly materializes its missing address without a CREATE_ADDRESS check. Before this commit there was no independent CREATE_ADDRESS authorization boundary to bypass.

audit_record.ai_marker: No AI marker in the BIC commit object: `git cat-file -p 84e8a87325a976c9970b8e85d03fc33207623af3` shows human author `jbertram <jbertram@apache.org>`, human committer `Martyn Taylor <mtaylor@redhat.com>`, subject `ARTEMIS-876 Remove all reliances on JMS prefixing`, and no body or Co-Authored-By/Generated-with trailer; neither identity is a bot.
audit_record.bug_semantics: With address auto-creation disabled, an authenticated OpenWire client can request a non-durable JMS topic subscription for a nonexistent address. AMQConsumer creates a random, non-durable temporary queue on that address; the broker implicitly creates the temporary address after checking only queue-creation permission, not CREATE_ADDRESS. The unauthorized address persists until the OpenWire connection closes, when temporary resources are removed.
evidence: Apache's advisory at https://lists.apache.org/thread/4wlrp31ngq2yb54sf4kjb3bl41t4xgtp describes the exact OpenWire non-durable-topic attack, missing createAddress permission, disabled address auto-creation, temporary-address lifetime, affected org.apache.activemq versions 2.0.0-2.44.0 and org.apache.artemis versions 2.50.0-2.52.0, and fixed version 2.53.0.

At BIC 84e8a87325a976c9970b8e85d03fc33207623af3, `git show -- artemis-server/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/artemis/core/security/CheckType.java` adds CREATE_ADDRESS and `git show -- artemis-server/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/artemis/core/server/impl/ServerSessionImpl.java` adds the separately authorized createAddress method while createQueue still checks only CREATE_DURABLE_QUEUE/CREATE_NON_DURABLE_QUEUE before calling server.createQueue. The same commit's ActiveMQServerImpl diff implicitly adds a missing AddressInfo while creating a queue. `git log --reverse -S'CREATE_ADDRESS' -- artemis-server/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/artemis/core/security/CheckType.java` identifies this as the first CREATE_ADDRESS addition.

The pre-fix OpenWire path is reproducible with `git show a2bb690e468d7956a4c83f10efa65f09a6d66f45:artemis-protocols/artemis-openwire-protocol/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/artemis/core/protocol/openwire/amq/AMQSession.java`: createConsumer invokes checkAutoCreateQueue only inside `if (openWireDest.isQueue())`, so topics bypass it. In AMQConsumer.createTopicSubscription, the non-durable branch creates a UUID-named queue on the requested address with durable=false and temporary=true.

Direct parent verification: `git rev-parse 84e8a87325a976c9970b8e85d03fc33207623af3^` returns 0bcde8140fb1f0927de58fcf856f3b449a2cdf5d; `git grep -n 'CREATE_ADDRESS' 0bcde8140fb1f0927de58fcf856f3b449a2cdf5d -- artemis-server/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/artemis/core/security/CheckType.java artemis-server/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/artemis/core/server/impl/ServerSessionImpl.java` has no match. Thus the parent lacks the distinct authorization boundary whose omission makes the later behavior an incorrect-authorization flaw.

Fix 75f51f0198221355e694c4db31e74a268c963cd6 (`Check auto-create for OpenWire JMS topic sub`) moves destination checking outside the queue-only branch and calls checkAutoCreate for topics before AMQConsumer initialization. That reaches ServerSessionImpl.checkAutoCreate; when the temporary queue needs a missing address it calls createAddress, whose implementation unconditionally performs `securityCheck(..., CheckType.CREATE_ADDRESS, ...)`. The added JMSTopicSubscriberWithSecurityTest expects JMSException and verifies the address remains absent.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: When the image proxy is enabled, an authenticated forum user can embed an attacker-chosen non-HTTPS URL in an IMG BBCode tag. SMF rewrites that URL into its own proxy.php URL and computes the required HMAC/hash with the server-side image-proxy secret, so the hash check is not an authorization boundary against that user. The proxy then performs a server-side fetch. Before the fix, destination validation was absent or limited to literal IP addresses and the exact hostname localhost; a public-looking hostname that resolved to loopback, RFC1918, link-local/cloud-metadata, or another reserved address, and redirects to such an address, reached the fetchers. This permits SSRF into services visible to the SMF host.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The root flaw was introduced by the original image-proxy endpoint in dcbaefb0976cf3e9d9490455bb59504d5c807847: proxy.php accepted a signed request URL and passed it directly to curl_fetch_web_data::get_url_data without validating the resolved destination. Follow-up commits in the same feature series supplied enabled defaults (f7a3f2b5b0bcc538637fd48ff273f094bcbc85e4), automatically signed attacker-controlled BBCode image URLs (a892a53ba45330d69b8ad8b1ede82aebaa29537b), added avatar use (d12746587bbf9b4015854677ac2a2916937116e5), and exposed settings (cc52ef5f6fae05bb41a66817758971d7a2063681). Those commits completed and broadened the attack path, but dcbaefb0976cf3e9d9490455bb59504d5c807847 is the smallest commit that first wrote the unsafe server-side fetch rather than a later move or refactor.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The attachment-approval action accepts an authenticated request after a GET-session check, collects pending attachment IDs from either sa=all plus mid or a caller-supplied aid, obtains the boards on which the user has approve_posts, and then is supposed to retain only attachments whose message board is authorized. The condition uses assignment rather than comparison: in 2.1, `if ($allowed_boards = array(0) || in_array(...))`, and in 3.0, `if ($allowed_boards = [0] || \in_array(...))`. Because assignment has lower precedence than `||` and the non-empty `[0]`/`array(0)` operand is truthy, the right-hand boolean expression is always true, true is assigned to $allowed_boards, and every queried pending attachment passes. A low-privileged authenticated user with a valid session can consequently approve pending attachments without approve_posts, use reject to delete pending attachments, bypass moderation for the user's own uploads, and target or enumerate other users' pending attachment IDs across boards.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The vulnerable condition is already present in the repository's sole root commit, a18e888838460a816fdbc2703e7e05ce7f626c91 (2012-01-24, subject `10610`). That commit is a 1,045-path initial source snapshot with no parent, not the smallest causal change that changed a correct authorization comparison into the assignment. Later commits only moved, extracted, or mechanically restyled the already-vulnerable code. Therefore the true flaw origin lies before the available Git-history boundary and cannot be assigned a real BIC from this repository.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: On a WolfStack node still using the published built-in cluster secret, an unauthenticated remote client could send that constant in X-WolfStack-Secret. The pre-25.9.2 validate_inter_node_secret() accepted it without constraining the transport peer, and require_auth() returned the privileged synthetic identity cluster-node without a session, API key, or account. A caller reaching the management port could therefore enumerate Docker/LXC containers and invoke POST /api/containers/{runtime}/{id}/exec, whose handler passed attacker-controlled command text to sh -c inside the selected container. The 25.9.2 fix routes every presentation of the built-in default through a transport-peer gate and accepts it only from an address already recorded in nodes.json; custom per-installation secrets remain valid normally.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 2d2d371527bde1e9d72eadcd2ee3e7c0ee3adfbc (v5.9.4) is the smallest true first-writer of the hard-coded credential. It deliberately replaced the parent revision's per-node /etc/wolfstack/cluster.key loading and two-UUID random generation with the source-visible CLUSTER_SECRET constant and made load_cluster_secret() return that same value on every installation. The header gate itself came from the immediately preceding v5.9.3 commit and was not vulnerable there because its expected secret was independently generated per node. The constant was temporarily removed by the 11.26.3 hardening and restored by the 11.26.4 revert, but the revert is a later carrier/reintroduction, not the first BIC; subsequent rotation/migration work retained the built-in value as an accepted fallback on unmigrated nodes until 25.9.2.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: ERC7984 stores confidential total supply in an euint64. On overflow, its mint path selects a transferred amount of zero and leaves supply unchanged rather than reverting. ERC7984ERC20Wrapper's wrap path first transfers the caller's underlying ERC-20 into the wrapper, while its ERC-1363 callback runs after the underlying transfer; both paths then call _mint and ignore the returned actual amount. Once the confidential supply is full, the transaction therefore succeeds with the underlying tokens retained but zero confidential wrapped tokens minted, causing user fund loss.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The unsafe composition first appears in PR #11 member commit 58f350da0359bc8de8d6a0a97e9ea35b664b44be: it creates ConfidentialFungibleTokenERC20Wrapper and adds both the transfer-then-_mint wrap path and the onTransferReceived _mint path without consuming or checking _mint's return value. The parent already had the intentionally non-reverting encrypted overflow behavior in ConfidentialFungibleToken, but had no ERC-20 wrapper, so the loss-of-funds mechanism did not yet exist.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The unauthenticated GET /api/artifacts handler reads the attacker-controlled id query parameter, interpolates it into the path of a Cloudflare API URL, and calls fetch with the deployment's Cloudflare KV Bearer token. URL normalization resolves ../ segments before the request is sent, so a traversal such as ../../../../../../../user/tokens/verify escapes /accounts/{account}/storage/kv/namespaces/{namespace}/values/ and reaches another Cloudflare API path with the victim token; the handler then proxies the Cloudflare response to the attacker.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The flaw originated in the initial artifact-sharing feature commit 421bf33c0e033ae5ab51f08902d9aa420f5b3f65, which created app/api/artifact/route.ts and in the same commit added the user-controlled id, the direct URL interpolation, the privileged Authorization header, the outbound fetch, and response proxying. Later type, TTL, and artifact-to-artifacts rename commits preserved that mechanism and are not introducers.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: In a server-capable NextChat deployment, app/mcp/actions.ts has a file-level "use server" directive, so its exported async MCP-management functions are remotely invocable Next.js Server Actions. The first exploitable form exposed updateMcpConfig, which accepted and persisted a caller-controlled MCP command/args/env configuration, and restartAllClients, which reloaded that configuration and passed it to StdioClientTransport; an unauthenticated caller could invoke those client-bundled actions in sequence to spawn an arbitrary process. Commit 8aa9a500fdee762abe5fd8e0bba00065be1725f4 later consolidated the same unsafe trust boundary into the advisory-named addMcpServer action, making arbitrary command execution a single request. No authentication, authorization, effective ENABLE_MCP gate, command allowlist, or safe environment boundary protects that action path; static-export builds do not expose Server Actions.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The smallest real BIC is 7d51bfd42e0f60a328abed353ab1ef717b6f3ba8 ("feat: MCP market"), not the later addMcpServer refactor. It first changed MCP configuration from a repository-owned static JSON import to caller-writable state and simultaneously exported the updateMcpConfig and restartAllClients Server Actions that turn an untrusted ServerConfig into a spawned stdio process. The immediate parent could initialize only repository-shipped configurations and had neither of those attacker-controlled management actions. The later 8aa9a500fdee762abe5fd8e0bba00065be1725f4 optimization replaced the two-action route with addMcpServer but did not originate the unauthenticated command-execution trust failure.

GHSA-2jqp-6hx7-phh8 / CVE-2026-7644 reports versions through 2.16.1 affected and says the project had not responded.

In the validated clone, git log --all -S 'export async function updateMcpConfig' -- app/mcp/actions.ts and git log -L :updateMcpConfig:app/mcp/actions.ts 7d51bfd42e0f60a328abed353ab1ef717b6f3ba8 both identify 7d51bfd42e0f60a328abed353ab1ef717b6f3ba8 as the first writer. The BIC adds file-level Server Action updateMcpConfig(config), which writes JSON.stringify(config) to app/mcp/mcp_config.json, and restartAllClients(), which clears state and calls initializeMcpClients(); that initializer reads the now-writable file and calls createClient(serverConfig, clientId). git log -L :restartAllClients:app/mcp/actions.ts at the BIC likewise begins at this commit.

git show 7d51bfd42e0f60a328abed353ab1ef717b6f3ba8:app/components/mcp-market.tsx shows both updateMcpConfig and restartAllClients imported into the client component and saveConfig calling them sequentially, making their Server Action identifiers client-visible. app/mcp/client.ts already passes ServerConfig.command, args, and env to StdioClientTransport and connects it, which is the process-spawn sink.

Direct parent verification: git grep -n -e updateMcpConfig -e restartAllClients -e addMcpServer 0c14ce6417821d512d04dec5a5755bf35deed51d -- app returns no matches. git show 0c14ce6417821d512d04dec5a5755bf35deed51d:app/mcp/actions.ts instead imports repository-owned mcp_config.json and initializes only Object.entries(conf.mcpServers); it has no action accepting an attacker-supplied ServerConfig and no caller-triggerable restart after a config write. Thus the exploitable configuration-to-spawn path is absent from the immediate parent.

Lifecycle cross-check: git show 8aa9a500fdee762abe5fd8e0bba00065be1725f4 -- app/mcp/actions.ts app/mcp/client.ts shows the later large 'Optimize MCP configuration logic' commit replacing the exported write/restart route with exported addMcpServer(clientId, config), which persists config and immediately calls initializeSingleClient. git log -S 'addMcpServer' -- app/mcp/actions.ts begins there. Commit e440ff56c89d11b29cdbb303eb8a9a71cddc2553 later amplified secret exposure by merging process.env into the spawned transport environment. Commit bc71ae247bd1110658aef933eaf301b344181122 only added isMcpEnabled as a separate exported query and did not call it from addMcpServer.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An unauthenticated request to /api/<unrecognized-provider>/<path> reaches the dynamic provider route's default branch, which calls proxyHandler. proxyHandler constructs its fetch destination directly from the attacker-controlled x-base-url header plus attacker-controlled path/query data, performs the server-side fetch without an allowlist or private/loopback-address rejection, and streams the upstream response back. An attacker can therefore make the NextChat server request arbitrary external or internal resources, including loopback and cloud metadata endpoints.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit f652f7326070dfbffcc5f90a999e95df21f4c650 is the atomic first writer of the vulnerable mechanism: it adds app/api/proxy.ts with fetchUrl derived from req.headers.get("x-base-url") and fetch(fetchUrl, ...), and in the same commit changes app/api/[provider]/[...path]/route.ts so unknown providers default to that proxyHandler. The pre-existing route instead sent its default branch to the fixed OpenAI handler, and app/api/proxy.ts did not exist in the immediate parent.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: For non-export builds, NextChat's Next.js response-header rule grants Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * to the API surface. The current rule also grants every method and request header, so JavaScript from an attacker-controlled origin can pass preflight, send custom headers, and read API responses. In the reported high-impact chain, the permitted x-base-url header reaches the catch-all /api/[provider]/[...path] route; an unknown provider falls through to app/api/proxy.ts, which constructs a server-side fetch URL from x-base-url and injects the configured OpenAI key when that attacker-controlled string contains api.openai.com. The wildcard origin is the underlying CWE-346/CWE-942 flaw; wildcard methods/headers and the unauthenticated proxy amplify its consequences.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 50cd33dbb2992066dae8c51c2da6ef4781e4500a is the smallest true BIC: it first added nextConfig.headers for non-export builds, matched /:path* (therefore including API routes), and emitted Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * plus Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. Its parent e6b49a60c0eba9e591546a419eed5ed389c44b43 has no nextConfig.headers callback or CORS response headers. Commit 0fb775d71a0fac5ce4aa802bc3eb0b066c12ed7b one day later narrowed the rule to /api/:path* but amplified it by changing Allow-Methods and Allow-Headers to * and adding a 24-hour max age; it did not first create the untrusted-origin policy. Commit 6f83fbd21278c90cd978108abe54291c38ec10d7 merely moved the already-vulnerable header array into CorsHeaders and is rejected as a refactor BIC.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The affected SDK methods insert caller-influenced identifiers directly into URL path template literals while attaching the merchant's bearer token. Slash or dot-dot content can be normalized by the WHATWG URL parser into a different API path, and a question mark can become attacker-chosen query syntax, so an application that passes an untrusted identifier without its own ownership check can make credentialed requests outside the intended resource. The affected families are payment get/capture/cancel, paymentRefund create/total/list/get, advancedPayment get/capture/cancel/update/updateReleaseDate, and disbursementRefund create/createAll/listAll.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Stored cross-site scripting in Telegram message search results: an attacker who can post to a shared Telegram group can store markup such as as message content. The application persists that content and later passes item.content to highlightKeyword(), which returned the raw text with only matching substrings wrapped in a span; Vue's v-html then assigned that attacker-controlled string as innerHTML. Merely rendering the result in another user's browser executes the handler. The closing change HTML-escapes message text before adding the intended highlight markup and also HTML/regex-escapes the keyword.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: In policycoreutils/scripts/fixfiles, the default fixfiles restore path and the non-destructive fixfiles relabel path run find over attacker-writable /tmp (and later /var/tmp, /var/run, and /var/lib/debug) and pass each matching pathname to a separate chcon process. A local attacker can replace an intermediate directory component with a symlink after find checks the entry but before chcon resolves the pathname. chcon --no-dereference avoids following a symlink only at the final component; it still follows swapped intermediate components, so the privileged invocation can apply an attacker-chosen SELinux label to an arbitrary target such as /etc/shadow, undermining MAC integrity.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The vulnerable find-plus-chcon design predates the repository's Git history. The earliest relevant Git object, 13cd4c8960688af11ad23b4c946149015c80d549, is a root snapshot titled 'initial import from svn trunk revision 2950'; its policycoreutils VERSION is 2.0.54 and the imported file already contains both vulnerable /tmp and /var/tmp commands. Because that aggregate import has no parent or SVN member commits in the validated clone, it is a history boundary rather than the smallest real BIC.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: tcpliveplay accepts a user-supplied pcap, obtains each packet from libpcap, rewrites its headers, and recalculates checksums. fix_all_checksum_liveplay derives the TCP checksum length solely from the untrusted IPv4 total-length/header-length fields as ntohs(iphdr->ip_len) - (iphdr->ip_hl << 2), without bounding that result by the pcap record's caplen. do_checksum_liveplay passes this length to do_checksum_math_liveplay, whose 16-bit loop reads that many bytes from the TCP-header pointer. A crafted pcap can therefore make the loop read beyond libpcap's heap packet buffer, causing the reported heap-buffer-overflow and denial of service.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The vulnerable checksum-length trust and unbounded checksum loop entered tcpreplay together when the externally developed tcpliveplay source was first imported as a new file in commit 0b287ed9052f740ecb04df556dd07f03c4186e01. Later commits e5039a91fbf018b5c7d084224c884e2275529724 (function rename) and 8f3761d212d39d82a3f2cad39f9f92c1ebc3ca5c (cleanup/formatting) preserved the same flaw and are not introducers.

First-party issue https://github.com/appneta/tcpreplay/issues/925 gives the ASan reproduction on 4.5.1: rewrite -> fix_all_checksum_liveplay -> do_checksum_liveplay -> do_checksum_math_liveplay, a READ of size 2 exactly past a 2048-byte libpcap heap allocation. The reporter explicitly notes that `ntohs(iphdr->ip_len) - (iphdr->ip_hl << 2)` can be large. The issue is labeled `shelved` (`Will not be addressed in foreseeable future`); maintainer comments on 2025-07-12 say no more tcpliveplay updates and close it without a code fix.

At tag v4.5.1 (peeled commit 0ba7d17fcb9ddedf61168f99c249b30731310d4e), src/tcpliveplay.c calls `do_checksum_liveplay(..., ntohs(iphdr->ip_len) - (iphdr->ip_hl << 2))`, then calls `do_checksum_math_liveplay((u_int16_t *)tcp, len)`; the latter loops `while (len > 1) { sum += *data++; len -= 2; }`. src/common/utils.c:217-258 validates pcap record len/caplen relationships but does not validate IPv4 ip_len against caplen.

`git log v4.5.1 -L 1084,1086:src/tcpliveplay.c` traces the vulnerable length expression through formatting commit 8f3761d212d39d82a3f2cad39f9f92c1ebc3ca5c and rename commit e5039a91fbf018b5c7d084224c884e2275529724 to 0b287ed9052f740ecb04df556dd07f03c4186e01, where the file is added from /dev/null with the same expression (then calling do_checksum_newconn). `git log --all -S 'ntohs(iphdr->ip_len) - (iphdr->ip_hl << 2)' -- src/tcpliveplay.c` independently returns only 0b287ed9052f740ecb04df556dd07f03c4186e01.

`git rev-parse 0b287ed9052f740ecb04df556dd07f03c4186e01^` returns e7f6ea96f6531bb71b68b206140ef033ff16f5fa. `git ls-tree -r --name-only e7f6ea96f6531bb71b68b206140ef033ff16f5fa -- src/tcpliveplay.c` returns no entry, while commit 0b287ed9052f740ecb04df556dd07f03c4186e01 adds the entire 1303-line file; this directly verifies parent absence.

`git for-each-ref --contains=0b287ed9052f740ecb04df556dd07f03c4186e01 --sort=creatordate refs/tags` shows the first containing prerelease as v4.0.0beta1 (peeled commit 4adacbdd9abc690e081d97e602d4460098327e97) and first stable release as v4.0.0 (peeled commit 5be5a90cfe1746747e9052386f9d410e6915d606), continuing through v4.5.1 and v4.6.1.

No closing fix exists in the validated history. `git log --all -G 'ip_len|caplen' -- src/tcpliveplay.c` finds no commit that bounds the checksum length to caplen. Commit e516e93a176d9b9e170e19c96b01be4e5b29e9fe adds only minimum Ethernet/IP/TCP-header caplen checks for a different advisory and leaves the vulnerable ip_len-derived checksum call unchanged. At master c3f6049a1de91e7d3b81543d0ecb01e465b05214, src/tcpliveplay.c still contains the unbounded call and loop; `git log -1 -S 'ntohs(iphdr->ip_len) - (iphdr->ip_hl << 2)' v4.6.1 -- src/tcpliveplay.c` likewise traces the still-present expression back to the BIC. causal_chain.bug_semantics: HPE OneView exposes PUT /rest/id-pools/executeCommand without authentication. The request JSON is deserialized as an ExecutableCommand; PoolController.executeCommand passes its attacker-controlled cmd property to RuntimeExecutorService.execute, which invokes Java Runtime.exec. A remote unauthenticated caller can therefore execute an arbitrary command (Rapid7 demonstrated a reverse shell as the trm3 Trusted RM Container user). Endpoint availability limits practical exposure: Rapid7 found it enabled on OneView for VMs 6.x and likely all unpatched OneView for HPE Synergy versions, while some other VM editions return 404 because ID Pools is disabled. HPE's official affected-products statement nevertheless lists all HPE OneView versions through 10.20.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The vulnerable implementation is proprietary HPE OneView appliance code in guidserver.jar (com.hp.ci.mgmt.guidpools.controllers.PoolController plus RuntimeExecutorService), not code in rapid7/metasploit-framework. This repository contains a post-disclosure Metasploit exploit client and documentation only. The smallest true BIC would be the HPE source-history change that first combined unauthenticated reachability with execution of the request-controlled cmd value, but HPE's source repository and commit history are not public in the assigned evidence.

audit_record.ai_marker: Not assessable: the true HPE OneView BIC commit object is unavailable, so there is no BIC author/committer identity or trailer block to inspect. causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated course student (role 3) can bypass navigation/button hiding by directly loading /courses/{course-id}/settings#share or /courses/{course-id}/people?add=true. The settings route renders the restricted course configuration and share link; the people page instantiates an invitation dialog whose open state is controlled only by the user-supplied add=true query. In v0.1.13 that dialog loads organization tutors (including names/emails), exposes the student invite link and QR code, and presents add-member actions. This is an object-keyed course authorization failure: membership is accepted where an admin/tutor role check is required. The advisory demonstrates unauthorized interface/data access; successful persistence of every offered mutation was not independently established and its CVSS vector records integrity impact as none.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: getRecommendTitleFromMarkdownString applies /#{1,6} {1,}(.*\S.*)(?:\n|$)/g to renderer-supplied Markdown when the Electron main process handles save and save-as. For an unmatched heading-like line such as '#' followed by a long run of spaces and then a newline, the greedy space quantifier and the two overlapping .* quantifiers around the required non-space character explore many equivalent partitions before failing. causal_chain.bug_semantics: A crafted DLT_JUNIPER_ETHER pcap processed by tcprewrite can reach the Juniper decoder's embedded Ethernet subdecoder. The subdecoder owns an allocated decoded_extra buffer, but tcpedit_dlt_copy_decoder_state() shallow-copies that pointer into the outer context without transferring or sharing ownership. At tcpedit_close(), both contexts are cleaned: in the reported 4.5.1 stack, dlt_linuxsll2_cleanup() runs once for the outer context and again while dlt_jnpr_ether_cleanup() recursively cleans the subcontext, freeing the same allocation twice and aborting under ASan. This is a local, user-assisted denial-of-service/memory-corruption path through a supplied capture file.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The ownership error originated in src/tcpedit/plugins/dlt_utils.c:tcpedit_dlt_copy_decoder_state() together with the Juniper subdecoder lifecycle in src/tcpedit/plugins/dlt_jnpr_ether/jnpr_ether.c: commit 745a71184c9d739305d4319cf2e6bb3998cc27b6 introduced the nested DLT_EN10MB context, recursive cleanup, and the comment 'just need to copy the ptr' followed by ctx->decoded_extra = subctx->decoded_extra. The later linuxsll2 cleanup is the observed free site, not the first root-cause introduction.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The authenticated Engine UI proxy handler accepted the destination host and port directly from /engine-ui/<host>:<port>/... and constructed an outbound HTTP URL without restricting that destination. Any remote requester able to reach the handler could therefore make the Kyuubi server contact arbitrary network-reachable HTTP services, yielding SSRF/open-proxy behavior and possible confidentiality, integrity, or availability impact.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The smallest reconstructed first-writer is PR #4795 member 3b0152f33b2c03ddd2b86c6ec8541661e01b039a: it added EngineUIProxyServlet.scala, parsed host and port from the request path, formed http://<host>:<port>/..., registered the /engine-ui servlet, and attached it to KyuubiRestFrontendService without any destination policy. The main-branch squash 4cd00a8777043fca4348d2c2f3a2b0b6e358e028 is only the aggregate landing commit, not the smallest BIC.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The vulnerable product is the proprietary AIT CSV Import / Export WordPress plugin, not Metasploit. In plugin versions through 3.0.3, the directly web-reachable admin/upload-handler.php accepts an unauthenticated multipart file field without restricting the uploaded type. An attacker can submit a .php file; although the handler may report a CSV parse error, the file remains in wp-content/uploads and is web-executable, yielding unauthenticated remote code execution even when the plugin is installed but inactive. WPScan also reports possible deletion through the same handler.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: External proprietary AIT Themes plugin source at ait-csv-import-export/admin/upload-handler.php. The assigned rapid7/metasploit-framework repository contains only a downstream exploit module that demonstrates the flaw; it does not contain the vulnerable plugin implementation or its release history.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The email-verification trust boundary was client-controlled in two complementary ways. The verification feature added is_email_verified and verified_at to profile while the existing authenticated profile UPDATE policy restricted only rows, not columns, so an authenticated user could PATCH their own /rest/v1/profile row and set is_email_verified=true. It also put {profileId, orgSiteName} into unsigned Base64 and /api/verify decoded that attacker-malleable data and set the named profile verified without integrity, ownership, or expiry checks. A later member of the same squashed feature made that handler use the Supabase service-role client, bypassing RLS and making a forged profileId capable of targeting an arbitrary profile.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: ClassroomIO v0.1.13 exposed its Supabase/PostgREST public.course resource to low-privilege authenticated clients. A student could replace the application's scoped POST with GET /rest/v1/course and supply an arbitrary relational select. The effective course SELECT policy admitted every published course as well as courses whose group contained the caller, while group, groupmember, and profile rows were globally readable. PostgREST followed the course->group->groupmember->profile and course->lesson->profile foreign keys, so the response disclosed course metadata, membership records, other students, and tutor profiles without an authorization decision tied to the requested relation set or HTTP method.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The first public-history writer is a0997b0b6951948efd7a8e8c5516c3d549f69cab (#19: Implement supabase local setup), which imported the remote schema and in one ordinary commit added the course/group/groupmember/profile tables and foreign keys, GRANT ALL on those tables to anon and authenticated, a course SELECT USING (true) policy, and a profile SELECT USING (true) policy. The commit is a schema import of an already existing remote database, so the production database may have predated the repository representation, but no earlier public commit contains the causal schema. Later RLS work preserved rather than originated the read exposure: 20240717053936_rls.sql enabled RLS yet created SELECT USING (true) policies for group and groupmember, and 20250808030821_rls_secure_courses.sql only narrowed course rows to is_published OR course-group/admin membership.

audit_record.ai_marker: Absent. `git cat-file -p a0997b0b6951948efd7a8e8c5516c3d549f69cab` shows author and committer `Rotimi Best <best@classroomio.com>`, one parent, and only the message `#19: Implement supabase local setup`; there is no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, AI trailer, or other AI marker in the BIC commit object.
audit_record.bug_semantics: ClassroomIO v0.1.13 exposed its Supabase/PostgREST public.course resource to low-privilege authenticated clients. A student could replace the application's scoped POST with GET /rest/v1/course and supply an arbitrary relational select. The effective course SELECT policy admitted every published course as well as courses whose group contained the caller, while group, groupmember, and profile rows were globally readable. PostgREST followed the course->group->groupmember->profile and course->lesson->profile foreign keys, so the response disclosed course metadata, membership records, other students, and tutor profiles without an authorization decision tied to the requested relation set or HTTP method.
evidence: Advisory reproduction and scope: https://github.com/classroomio/classroomio/issues/642 identifies affected v0.1.13 and records a student changing POST to GET /rest/v1/course with a select expanding group(*,members:groupmember(*,profile(*))) and lesson teacher profiles; the returned data includes other student profiles, tutor information, group membership, and internal course metadata. GHSA-rx88-8j23-4qxx/CVE-2025-67259 gives the same mechanism and CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N.

Affected-tag schema: `git grep -n -E 'create policy|CREATE POLICY' v0.1.13 -- supabase/migrations/20231115082347_remote_schema.sql supabase/migrations/20240717053936_rls.sql supabase/migrations/20250808030821_rls_secure_courses.sql` finds the original course `FOR SELECT USING (true)` and profile `FOR SELECT USING (true)` policies, the later group/groupmember/profile read policies, and the final course policy. `git show v0.1.13:supabase/migrations/20250808030821_rls_secure_courses.sql` shows the effective course predicate `using ((is_published OR is_user_in_course_group_or_admin(group_id)))`.

Relational exposure at the first writer: `git grep -n -E 'CREATE TABLE.*(course|group|groupmember|profile|lesson)' a0997b0b6951948efd7a8e8c5516c3d549f69cab -- supabase/migrations/20231115082347_remote_schema.sql` locates all five tables. In the same file, constraints at lines 865, 880, 883, 901, and 910 connect course to group, group to groupmember, groupmember to profile, lesson to course, and lesson teacher_id to profile. Grants at lines 1062-1064, 1078-1080, 1090-1092, 1094-1096, and 1166-1168 grant ALL on those resources to anon/authenticated/service_role. Those foreign keys are what allow PostgREST relational expansion.

Effective v0.1.13 RLS still permits the attack: `git show v0.1.13:supabase/migrations/20240717053936_rls.sql | sed -n '550,720p'` shows group and groupmember `for select to public using (true)`. Its profile section around lines 1075-1081 has `for select to authenticated, anon using (true)`. `git grep -n -E 'alter table "public"."(course|group|groupmember)" enable row level security' v0.1.13 -- supabase/migrations/20240717053936_rls.sql` confirms RLS is enabled, so these permissive predicates, rather than absent enforcement by accident, are the effective authorization rules.

BIC search: `git log --all --reverse -S'GRANT ALL ON TABLE "public"."groupmember" TO "authenticated"' -- '**/*.sql'` first reports a0997b0b6951948efd7a8e8c5516c3d549f69cab. `git log -L 938,954:supabase/migrations/20231115082347_remote_schema.sql v0.1.13` initially stops at 50e89f90c9f264ac93cc6882743e21ed70a9f011 because that commit reverted a temporary migration squash. Repeating `git log -L 938,954:supabase/migrations/20231115082347_remote_schema.sql d010531ef7932dc3093621f1771abb90c0b14368^` bypasses the delete/revert artifact and traces the course/profile permissive policies to a0997b0b6951948efd7a8e8c5516c3d549f69cab. Thus neither d010531ef7932dc3093621f1771abb90c0b14368 nor its revert is treated as an introducer.

Direct parent absence: `git cat-file -p a0997b0b6951948efd7a8e8c5516c3d549f69cab` names sole parent 78732f95f3372f3d2b0a1aca2e9be6af1a98a1cc. `git diff --name-status 78732f95f3372f3d2b0a1aca2e9be6af1a98a1cc a0997b0b6951948efd7a8e8c5516c3d549f69cab -- supabase/migrations/20231115082347_remote_schema.sql` reports `A`; `git ls-tree -r --name-only 78732f95f3372f3d2b0a1aca2e9be6af1a98a1cc -- supabase` contains config/functions/seed only and no schema migration or equivalent course/group grants/policies.

Version boundary: `git tag --contains a0997b0b6951948efd7a8e8c5516c3d549f69cab --sort=version:refname` includes every repository release tag from v0.1.0 through 0.2.11 and later; v0.1.13 resolves to commit 876a785b3c467b809804f56e0981bff448fcfdb5 and contains the vulnerable migrations. The advisory only claims/testing-proves v0.1.13, so the tag-containment result establishes code presence, not independent runtime testing of every tag.

Rejected apparent fix: one-parent landing commit 1e9a82e912736d87092715fae13329b76254d052 (`feat: complete rewrite of course (#622)`) removed the Supabase migration tree on main and is first contained by v0.3.0. Its tree 3a25148b9e8ce8f6d36e0b207dd7edbe9f3692e3 exactly equals PR-head f742cb1242b3f0f2012e44c20907863d1229a296, proving it is a squash landing. PR member f5c67b021c7f7496ffa85d76c470df97f9940857 deletes the Supabase files, but this is transport replacement, not a closing access-control fix.

Why no fix SHA is claimed: PR member 35dbde0378bd95b400c1763e49ba8191e1515ee7 added the replacement public unauthenticated GET /course/slug/:slug handler, and `git log --all -S'getCourse(undefined, slug)' -- apps/api/src/routes/course/course.ts` traces it to that member and the 1e9a82e912736d87092715fae13329b76254d052 squash. At current HEAD f08f6c6838259ca440299a82f5d100d44d5349cd, apps/api/src/routes/course/course.ts lines 112-125 still label the route public, apply no auth/member middleware, call getCourse(undefined, slug), and serialize the result. packages/db/src/queries/course/course.ts lines 333-475 defines that result as the entire course plus group members, profile id/fullname/username/avatar/email, attendance, contentItems, and organization settings; the slug query checks only slug and status ACTIVE, not isPublished or membership. Therefore the rewrite retires /rest/v1/course but preserves the advisory's root semantic disclosure through a first-party endpoint, and no later public commit/tag is a real closing fix.

BIC-only AI check: `git cat-file -p a0997b0b6951948efd7a8e8c5516c3d549f69cab` is the complete commit object used for attribution. AI-related trailers on the much later 1e9a82e912736d87092715fae13329b76254d052 rewrite/fix candidate are deliberately ignored under the protocol because they are not evidence on the BIC.

audit_record.reasoning: The security boundary was always supposed to be enforced by the server-side database/API layer, because a student controls the HTTP method and PostgREST select expression. The initial checked-in Supabase schema made course, group, groupmember, lesson, and profile data directly queryable and relationally expandable. Subsequent RLS migrations did not cure that causal error: course visibility remained public-or-member and the nested membership/profile relations remained globally readable. Git -S and line history, after explicitly bypassing the later squash/revert artifact, converge on a0997b0b6951948efd7a8e8c5516c3d549f69cab; its direct parent lacks the migration and causal rules. The BIC commit object is plainly human-authored and has no AI marker, so NOT_AI is supported independently of later history. No fix SHA is assigned: the March 2026 rewrite removed Supabase/PostgREST but its landed replacement exposes essentially the same sensitive relation graph from an unauthenticated slug route, and that code remains at current main. An endpoint rename/architectural refactor is not a root-cause remediation. This is therefore a closed attribution verdict for an explicitly unpatched vulnerability lifecycle, not an EVIDENCE_GAP about AI provenance.
audit_record.remaining_gap: Unpatched in public history as of current main f08f6c6838259ca440299a82f5d100d44d5349cd: no commit or release can be named as a true fix because the v0.3.0 rewrite removed the reported /rest/v1/course transport while retaining unauthenticated disclosure of course, group-member/profile email, attendance, content, and organization data at GET /course/slug/:slug. Deployment-specific confirmation of which commit was running when issue #642 was closed is not public, but that does not supply a source-level closing fix.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A local attacker who can make tcprewrite process a crafted truncated pcap with `--fixlen pad` can reach `untrunc_packet()`. That function reallocates the packet buffer when the pcap header's wire length exceeds its captured length. If realloc moves the allocation, the pre-realloc base pointer and the IPv4/IPv6 header pointers derived from it in `tcpedit_packet()` become dangling. Processing nevertheless continues through DLT layer-3 merging; the Ethernet L2-length path calls `get_l2len()` and then `get_l2len_protocol()`, which reads protocol data through the freed allocation. The issue #973 ASan trace reports that exact read-after-free and abort path. The defect is the realloc in a control flow that retains aliases into the old allocation, not a bounds error authored in `get_l2len_protocol()` itself.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14 is the smallest true BIC. To repair an overwrite reported as issue #80, it changed `untrunc_packet()` to accept `u_char **pktdata`, copied `*pktdata` into local `packet`, and added `packet = safe_realloc(packet, pkthdr->len)` before padding, but it did not make all caller-held aliases safe after a move (and at that point did not even assign the new pointer back to `*pktdata`). Its immediate parent 16abc7fe749bd3c130204d0b2707caf7cab5894e has neither realloc nor safe_realloc in `src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c`, so it cannot free the packet on this path. Commit b58b23a52ffd23c3b1a2e2fe8b868aff0239560d later added `*pktdata = packet`, but did not refresh `tcpedit_packet()`'s local `packet`, `ip_hdr`, or `ip6_hdr` aliases, so the same realloc-caused UAF lifecycle continued rather than being newly introduced there. Commit 64132c54c4000046b30f1fc3fe612db9b2f26860 only enlarged the realloc request with `PACKET_HEADROOM`; it is not the BIC.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: ICTBroadcast's unauthenticated /login.php session startup accepts the attacker-controlled session ID from the site cookie (normally BROADCAST) and passes it to the custom Session::read handler. The vulnerable handler logs `Session read requested with id: $id` before rejecting malformed IDs. The logging path invokes a shell command equivalent to `sh -c echo "[...] Session read requested with id: `id` " >> /usr/ictbroadcast/logs/gui.log`; therefore shell metacharacters/backticks embedded in the cookie are evaluated as command substitution. An attacker first GETs /login.php to obtain the configured cookie, then returns a value such as `` `echo${IFS}<base64>|base64${IFS}-d|sh` ``. No authentication is needed, and the injected command executes during session handling. The later-looking valid_sid check in the publicly downloadable 7.1.12 package is too late for the logged read path because fileLog is called on the raw ID first.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The flaw is in ICT Innovations' separately distributed ICTBroadcast product, not in rapid7/metasploit-framework. Rapid7's repository contains only the post-discovery exploit module and its documentation. Public vendor RPMs expose snapshots but not the ICTBroadcast Git history: build 6.0.26 (short build ID 67c41c6c) has an older procedural session_read with the logging calls commented out, while build 7.1.12 (short build ID e966e3ef) has the class-based Session::read and the unsafe pre-validation fileLog call. Those eight-hex build IDs are not full public commit objects, the package has no .git metadata, the bootstrap/logger implementation is ionCube-protected, and the vendor organization has no public ICTBroadcast product repository. Consequently the smallest commit that first wrote the unsafe logging flow, its direct parent, and any direct fixing commit are outside public history.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: tcpprep accepts include/exclude selector strings that are expected to contain a one-byte mode, a separator, and a payload. A malformed one-byte selector is heap-duplicated by the --load-opts doOptInclude path and passed to parse_xX_str. That function examines str[0] but, without checking the string length, advances the pointer by two bytes. For CIDR modes B, D, E, or S it then passes this one-past-allocation pointer to parse_cidr; mask_cidr6 immediately evaluates **cidrin and therefore reads beyond the two-byte allocation (the selector plus NUL), producing the reported heap-buffer-overflow/out-of-bounds read and crash. The closing fix rejects any nonempty one-byte selector before the switch and pointer advance.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The unsafe parsing rule originated in 3941c24fbcdf2a9822df5d2a84ac0c3f5612e408, which introduced -x/-X parsing in tcpreplay.c and, for P/S/D/B/E, unconditionally executed str = str + 2 before parsing the payload. Its parent had no -x/-X parser. Commit 90c47b79caa0b7685e6d0d737e01b786ac4ac475 later copied/moved that parser into xX.c and is therefore not the origin; a9a5ec78124ea11c0ab9e1a8a0d74ce6616c4790 then exposed the shared parser through tcpprep. Commit f7d2fb9b5b8696bcc9a7a7b8bc0b5bb8b48273d5 later added mask_cidr6 and the exact reported dereference sink, but the invalid one-past pointer already reached strtok in parse_cidr at the origin, so the IPv6 change is not the root BIC.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: In packet-rate mode, tcpreplay parses --pps as a double, rejects only an exactly zero double, then computes (COUNTER)(n * 60.0 * 60.0). A nonzero fractional rate whose magnitude is below 1/3600, including the published -0.000001, therefore passes the check but truncates to a zero packets-per-hour COUNTER. calc_sleep_time later uses that value as pph in integer division, raising SIGFPE and terminating a local replay.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 175f7ed06c6ad6488020220f9917ca213c568251 changed --pps from AutoOpts integer input to an unrestricted string parsed with atof and introduced the float-to-COUNTER packets-per-hour conversion without validating the converted value. That is the smallest commit enabling the advisory's nonzero fractional-input-to-zero-divisor path; later commit ebed7dde22ef3b77ceb64eefa2c873b92b435dda rejected only n == 0 and left the truncation path intact.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: During ZIP extraction, a local attacker able to mutate the extraction directory can replace an already-validated parent directory with a symlink before OpenClaw opens the destination pathname. The later pathname-based write follows the rebound parent and can create or truncate a file outside the extraction root with the OpenClaw process's privileges; leaf-only O_NOFOLLOW protection does not bind mutable parent traversal to the checked directory identity.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Original feature implementation. Commit 3a6ee5ee00176c88aee32bb8bfd543780014c079 first added the production ZIP extractor in src/infra/archive.ts with a lexical path.resolve/string-prefix containment check followed by separate mkdir, asynchronous ZIP decoding, and fs.writeFile(outPath, data). That check/use separation created the parent-symlink TOCTOU window at inception; later streaming and partial symlink-hardening changes retained the same mutable-parent pathname resolution and are not origins.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A tenant able to create or update Fission Function or Environment CRDs could request SYS_TIME in securityContext.capabilities.add on a tenant-controlled container or init container. The v1.24.0 admission validator and executor merge sanitizer used a fixed denylist containing only SYS_ADMIN, NET_ADMIN, SYS_PTRACE, SYS_MODULE, DAC_READ_SEARCH, and DAC_OVERRIDE, so SYS_TIME passed both layers and reached the resulting pod. Without restrictive Pod Security Admission on the function-pod namespace, CAP_SYS_TIME permits clock_settime(CLOCK_REALTIME) against the node-wide, non-time-namespaced real-time clock, corrupting wall-clock-dependent state for co-tenants. The separate OCI-default-capability concern was not fully addressed by this advisory's fix.

The mainline commit e484df8460bb4e8026e24210120602aa7f181f64 is the squash aggregate of the four-member PR chain and is therefore not substituted for the smallest real BIC. causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated user able to create and run workflows could supply the Git node with a staged working repository whose configured push remote was another attacker-controlled local repository. For push and pushTags, vulnerable releases left Git's file transport enabled, causing local git-receive-pack to run receive-side hooks in the target repository as the n8n process. Setting core.hooksPath=/dev/null on the initiating repository did not suppress hooks in that local receive target. The fix validates configured remotes and removes file from GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL for write operations when hooks are disabled.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The original Git node accepted a workflow-selected baseDirectory, constructed simple-git for that repository, and exposed git.push() without restricting repository-controlled local remote targets or Git's file transport. That original trust-boundary crossing, rather than a later move, import, refactor, or aggregate landing, is the flaw origin.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: With allow_unsafe_options at its safe default, a caller can put an unsafe Git option such as --upload-pack=<attacker command> in the value of a single-character kwarg such as n. The guard examines only the kwarg name, which is n in the original implementation and -n after candidate reconstruction, but transform_kwarg emits the value as a separate argv token. The check therefore misses the attacker-controlled option that Git executes. The defect first affected fetch, pull, and push, was later copied to clone/clone_from, and was later centralized and extended to ls_remote, revision traversal/iter_commits, blame, and archive.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: e6108c7997f5c8f7361b982959518e982b973230 is the smallest real BIC: it introduced default unsafe-option guards for Remote.fetch, Remote.pull, and Remote.push and fed check_unsafe_options only list(kwargs.keys()), while the existing single-character kwarg transformation emitted an option-like value as a second argv token. 5c59e0d63da6180db8a0b349f0ad36fef42aceed later propagated the same mistake to clone/clone_from. 701ce32fe5ba8cb622c0e0342a376a6beb47d738 later replaced the existing key-list checks with the still-key-only _option_candidates helper and added more guarded APIs; it expanded/refactored the already-present mechanism rather than introducing it.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: CredentialsPermissionChecker authorizes only credential IDs whose credential-type keys appear in a set inferred statically from unresolved node parameters. An authenticated member with edit access to a shared workflow can place another user's known credential ID on an HTTP Request node and make genericAuthType or nodeCredentialType an expression. The pre-execution checker sees the expression text rather than its runtime-resolved credential type, omits the credential ID from the ownership query, and execution later resolves and loads the unauthorized credential, allowing use or exfiltration.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The smallest causal source change is PR #25599 member 7d6023fe3478df86d88f3602f1ea5b53819a050b. It changed mapCredIdsToNodes from checking every referenced credential to skipping credential keys absent from getActiveCredentialTypes, whose static inference did not fail closed for expressions. Public squash 608e3bf214328e679c03da3e4a6e9c22ceaac9ca carried the flaw but is not the smallest BIC. Later bundle 2d9a2ec76e180b54e8091e31b1e0638c909abd99 added the unresolved genericAuthType value to the set, fixing literal generic types but preserving the advisory's expression mismatch and therefore not originating the flaw.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: TemplateContext.LimitToString bounded one ObjectToString conversion rather than cumulative rendered output. Each rendered expression entered a fresh top-level ObjectToString call, which reset _currentToStringLength, and StringBuilderOutput appended every resulting chunk without a render-wide cap. A template could therefore emit a near-1 MiB string in each of 1,000 loop iterations, pass the per-call check each time, and accumulate roughly 1 GiB until the host exhausted memory.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95 is the smallest real BIC: it directly added LimitToString, _currentToStringLength, and the top-level reset that made the safety counter restart for every ObjectToString conversion. Its two-file focused patch is neither a merge, aggregate, import, nor move, and its immediate parent lacks both LimitToString and _currentToStringLength. The older unconditional StringBuilderOutput append was a necessary sink but did not create the advisory-specific limit-bypass invariant; b5ac4bf30459fdc76964e3f751e16f7e96079ea7 later enabled the already-flawed limit by default. Commit 98563216488161a9edeba6c37c7cf82c98319c9b directly fixed the flaw by adding cumulative output accounting across write chunks.

`git cat-file commit 98563216488161a9edeba6c37c7cf82c98319c9b` shows a single parent and subject `Enforce cumulative output size limits`; `git grep` at that commit finds _currentOutputLength, WriteOutputChunk, GetAllowedOutputCount, and ResetOutputLimitTracking throughout the synchronous output path, establishing it as the direct causal source fix rather than a release aggregate.

`git rev-parse 6.6.0^{} 7.0.0^{}` resolves the release tags to b5ac4bf30459fdc76964e3f751e16f7e96079ea7 and 25d148a104dd4d679a1a1932442616599e003c2f. `git tag --contains 98563216488161a9edeba6c37c7cf82c98319c9b --sort=version:refname` starts at 7.0.0 and contains no 6.x release, matching the advisory's last-affected/first-patched boundary.

The assigned marker_state disagreement was primary `ai_marker` prose saying `absent: ...` versus reviewer `ai_marker: null`. Re-running `git cat-file commit b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95` shows human author and committer Alexandre Mutel <alexandre_mutel@live.com>, one parent, the plain subject `Add TemplateContext.LimitToString`, an empty body, and no Co-authored-by, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI-attribution trailer. There is therefore no actual marker to store, so the reviewer's null marker state is canonical; the primary's text correctly described absence but was evidence, not an AI marker.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The default object.to_json builtin recursively serialized IList/array elements and accessible object members through a static local WriteValue function without a recursion-depth limit, execution-stack guard, or circular-reference check. A template-controlled ScriptObject can refer to itself and be passed to object.to_json, causing WriteValue to revisit the same object until a fatal StackOverflowException terminates the hosting .NET process; sufficiently deep acyclic input reaches the same uncontrolled-recursion path.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: PR #533 member commit a65c891245e2c8550fb28fcd6e9d296c99ad6a2f is the smallest commit that first added ToJson, WriteValue, and both unchecked recursive calls in src/Scriban/Functions/ObjectFunctions.cs. Its immediate parent lacks the entire implementation. The later one-parent squash f2f3cf41cde1ba7226760fd9b456f3d5d7aa1ca1 is an aggregate rather than the BIC: the retained PR chain is reconstructable, the final member and squash have identical trees, and the vulnerable file blob written by a65c891245e2c8550fb28fcd6e9d296c99ad6a2f landed unchanged.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Rendering a ScriptObject recursively stringifies each stored member value without object-identity cycle detection. A member that points back to its containing ScriptObject therefore repeatedly re-enters object rendering; because ObjectRecursionLimit defaulted to 0 (unlimited), the guard was disabled and recursion continued until an uncatchable StackOverflowException terminated the host process.

The later a9affb64614358838aba16f28acb198f914e586d guard retained ObjectRecursionLimit=0 as the default and therefore preserved, rather than introduced, the already-existing vulnerable path.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: POST /api/provider-nodes/validate accepts a caller-controlled baseUrl and apiKey, constructs provider URLs from baseUrl, performs server-side fetches, and forwards apiKey in Authorization headers. The later assertPublicUrl mitigation remains bypassable because it compares hostname strings without resolving DNS or revalidating redirect destinations, and its IPv4-mapped IPv6 regex expects a dotted quad even though WHATWG URL parsing canonicalizes mapped literals to hextets first. Mapped loopback/link-local literals, DNS names resolving internally, and redirects can therefore reach internal services. The custom-embedding branch also returns up to 200 bytes of most non-2xx response bodies, while other validation branches expose status/timing signals. A dashboard session is required by default, but not when requireLogin is disabled.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The smallest real BIC is 0a28f9f924d2dc53027a910679ee3cff3e63a59c. It created src/app/api/provider-nodes/validate/route.js and in the same new-file patch first parsed caller-controlled baseUrl/apiKey, built `${baseUrl.replace(/\/$/, "")}/models`, fetched it without a destination policy, and forwarded `Bearer ${apiKey}`. Its direct parent has no such route. Commit 0b8bed5793c7a7c9beb7a5db7368720907f61ebc later added the custom-embedding fetch and 200-byte response reflection; 090886ced9a3481837f5687ec66da7d9f33eea08 later connected the hostname-only guard; 8ac631d6158c0f04976a0d0f7ca9ec2b981efeb5 later added the unreachable dotted-quad mapped-IPv6 check. causal_chain.bug_semantics: A page served from an attacker-controlled DNS name can retain its browser origin while DNS rebinding moves the connection to a victim's loopback Paperclip server. Paperclip's missing Host-header gate in default private local_trusted mode allowed that request to receive the implicit instance-admin board actor, create/configure a process-adapter agent with attacker-controlled command and arguments, and invoke its heartbeat/wakeup path, which passed the stored configuration to child_process.spawn as the Paperclip OS user.
