Its immediate parent 8c830eae70a14723749828f0ce5d9ae435270e9c lacks both server/src/middleware/auth.ts and server/src/services/heartbeat.ts, so the API-to-process-execution chain is absent there.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The runner registration-token API exposed token creation through GET routes. The token-scope middleware derives Read versus Write from the HTTP method and classifies GET as Read, but shared.GetRegistrationToken creates a runner token when no active token exists and returns it. A leaked read-scoped user, organization, repository, or admin token could therefore obtain a runner registration credential and register a malicious Actions runner able to receive workflow jobs with access to repository source and secrets.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: PR #27144 was squash-landed as baf0d402d9cb47849394202fcfc7c2e23b0faac3, but that mainline aggregate is not the smallest BIC. The reconstructable PR member eec5ed07521ffc767c0dd1bdccdece8a7f54fe3f first added the shared GET handler whose missing/inactive-token branch calls NewRunnerToken and added reachable organization and admin GET registration-token routes. Its immediate parent already classified GET as Read and contained neither the route nor the helper. The later member bba250f3e99bef12bbd9a1d9d790ab8155c999d5 extended the same mechanism to user and repository routes rather than originating it.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A scoped access token carrying only profile:read is accepted by PUT /user because that mutating route is guarded by RequireScopes(ScopeProfileRead). UpdateUser uses the token viewer's administrator identity and permits a supplied password to replace that administrator's password. The attacker can then log in with the replacement password; login issues a session JWT, and RequireScopes deliberately bypasses scope checks for session tokens, yielding unrestricted administrator access.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: PR #195 introduced route-level scoped-token authorization. Its member b47fa1c75d890cd080e3f6699bbfca8cd8d4b939 first wrote the causal mismatch in internal/router/user.go by binding PUT /user to ScopeProfileRead. GitHub later landed the PR as squash commit 3f8fb150158723aca31df2ae937a1aa7b31ac254; that mainline aggregate carries the flaw but is not the smallest BIC.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An administrator or authenticated caller with connect-write authority can persist an attacker-chosen ConnectURL. The public GET /api/connects/info path, and later authenticated peer-health paths, append /api/connect and make an unrestricted server-side HTTP request to that stored URL. Because the request path lacks scheme, host, resolved-address, redirect, loopback, private-network, and link-local/cloud-metadata validation, the caller can cause Ech0 to reach internal services or metadata endpoints and return or infer their responses.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: fabee479ccf98c081bb065926c726b461a42fdf3 is the smallest real origin. Its parent-to-child patch directly adds publicRoutes.GET("/connects/info", controllers.GetConnectsInfo), a GetConnectsInfo loop over stored ConnectURL values, and pkg.SendRequest backed by an unconstrained http.Client.Do. The relevant diff contains direct modifications rather than a rename, import, move, or aggregate; later rewrites, relocations, health checks, and the fetchPeerConnectInfo extraction preserve the already-vulnerable operation.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Ech0's scoped access tokens promised least privilege but privileged authorization was split among JWT authentication, opt-in RequireScopes route middleware, and service-level checks of the underlying account's IsAdmin bit. A deliberately narrow admin access token, such as echo:read, therefore authenticated to privileged routes that omitted RequireScopes, including /api/inbox and panel-comment routes. The public /api/backup/export path additionally reparsed a query JWT and rebuilt viewer state from only claims.Userid, discarding token type, scopes, audience, and JTI, so the backup service saw an unrestricted admin identity and returned the database/log ZIP.

It modified the existing scoped-token model and creation service to accept, validate, persist, and sign caller-selected Scopes and Audience while the same tree's authentication middleware still attached only viewer.NewUserViewer(mc.Userid), inbox had no scope guard, and backup export remained on PublicRouterGroup. Its direct parent 387667192911c86db1e1bcb3f544ce12d340ffdb could mint only legacy unscoped access JWTs and had neither scope/audience input nor CreateAccessClaimsWithExpiry, so the bypassable least-privilege contract was absent. causal_chain.bug_semantics: Budibase intended datasource credentials to be write-only by passing datasource responses through removeSecrets, but that redactor masked only schema fields typed PASSWORD or SENSITIVE_LONGFORM. MongoDB connectionString and Firebase privateKey held live credentials while declared STRING, so they survived redaction. The single-datasource GET route was authorized at TABLE/READ and, once its route parameter matched the controller lookup, allowed an authenticated application user with a datasource ID to receive those stored credentials in plaintext.

It changes GET /api/datasources/:id to /api/datasources/:datasourceId while the TABLE/READ controller already dereferences ctx.params.datasourceId and returns the stored datasource. Its direct parent therefore has a nonfunctional parameter mismatch. The older 29b51bc6c2fc8874ab7aa7a0c849ff5f205aec5a is a 116-file merge-resolution aggregate and, contrary to the reviewer claim, its new route is also :id while its controller reads datasourceId; it did not make that single-read path functional. causal_chain.bug_semantics: Ech0 globally installed its i18n middleware and passed unauthenticated request-controlled locale values, including the raw Accept-Language header after only TrimSpace, to go-i18n and golang.org/x/text/language.ParseAcceptLanguage without a size or shape bound. The x/text CVE-2022-32149 mitigation counted '-' separators but the parser also aliases '_' to '-', so a near-1 MiB malformed underscore-separated value bypassed the guard and exercised quadratic parsing, allowing unauthenticated CPU denial of service on every route. X-Locale and the lang query parameter also reached the same unbounded parser through ResolveLocale.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit b55edabd228d3de41e781bd3100f2e1ee0835516 first created Ech0's complete remotely reachable vulnerable path: it added internal/i18n/i18n.go, forwarded unbounded locale values to ParseAcceptLanguage and goi18n.NewLocalizer, read Accept-Language from the request, and registered the middleware globally. The parser weakness pre-existed in x/text, but the immediate parent did not contain Ech0's i18n parser path or global exposure.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: File Browser authorized only the requested source root and, for copy or rename, the destination root, then recursively removed, renamed, or copied the whole source tree without checking rules on every descendant. An authenticated restricted user could therefore operate on an allowed parent containing a denied child, exposing or relocating the child at an allowed destination or deleting it with the parent.

Its immediate parent had no resource delete handler or equivalent user-filesystem recursive deletion. causal_chain.bug_semantics: Access-rule authorization compared raw virtual paths as case-sensitive, slash-separated strings, while the host filesystem resolved equivalent names using its own case and separator semantics. On case-insensitive filesystems, a case variant of a denied path therefore missed the rule but reached the same file; on Windows, backslashes and traversal components likewise missed slash-based rules but were normalized by the filesystem. An authenticated user could consequently read or, subject to ordinary permissions, mutate an administrator-denied file while remaining inside the user's filesystem scope.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 9c36dea485ddd16a90f0a615e20baddaee6b9cde is the smallest real origin in the lineage that became File Browser v2. It added User.Allowed with the raw literal comparison strings.HasPrefix(url, rule.Path) and added HTTP handlers that passed request-derived paths to Allowed before filesystem access. Its sole parent 780f1bc16e4e5270fed2a6b7da442a47084d8c4b has no Rule type, User.Allowed function, or vulnerable comparison. The earlier 20baeeb41a9555cefc3b31b495e24e907736c443 was a 10,626-line bulk import explicitly described as based on caddy-filemanager and was removed during the rewrite, so it is rejected as an import rather than selected as the BIC. Later commits moved or extracted the same mechanism, and public master received it in squash aggregate 12b2c215221696de58431093e01eeff7a5414471.

GET /ticket/update/{id} exposed another tenant's ticket content and, once attachment support existed, its attachments; POST /ticket/save loaded another tenant's Ticket and then reassigned company_id and saved it; GET /ticket/delete/{id} deleted an arbitrary Ticket while its generic Request type also bypassed TicketDeleteRequest authorization.

Commit 946a0c5e43a1178534e5b013ea2608d565686220 later expanded the same object-ownership flaw to deletion, and 626b0228c248637086ce91bb17b2ec1b1c21961b later expanded read impact to attachments. Commit 65f6b9f961efe533b4d3f20f1eddad132fe8ef1d merely moved the already-vulnerable save lookup into TicketRepository and is not an introducer.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The conversion-history details endpoint reads a ConversionHistory row by caller-supplied history_id and serializes retained input_text, old_output_text, and new_output_text. Once ordinary conversion deletion became a soft delete, the parent conversion and its history remained in the database. The later normal parent lookup hid inactive conversions and returned None, while the authorization guard denied only when the parent was truthy and invisible; a deleted parent therefore skipped denial and its history payload was returned. The endpoint was anonymous immediately after the soft-delete change and remained exploitable by authenticated requesters after the later login hardening.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit bf868699adf960e7f812d30ccc3f1fa28131ba34 is the smallest causal BIC. It changed delete_convert from db.session.delete(convert) to is_active=False plus deleted_at without updating the already-existing direct history-details reader, so normal deletion first began retaining sensitive history that the reader disclosed by id. Its direct parent hard-deleted the conversion and deleted its histories through the ORM delete-orphan relationship and database ON DELETE CASCADE. Commit 37d7ba64638ad78f4604725f81bafac497ca235a was later partial hardening: it added login and visibility checks, but preserved the already-live deleted-parent disclosure with a truthiness-guarded check; it did not originate the vulnerability.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The POST routes /fetch_misp_event and /misp_search_events accepted a caller-controlled HTTPS MISP base URL and made server-side requests whose response data was returned to the caller. _validate_misp_url rejected unsafe IP literals but accepted every ordinary hostname without resolving it, so an attacker could use a hostname resolving to a private, loopback, link-local, or reserved address to reach and read an internal HTTPS service. The routes were also callable anonymously, increasing exposure, while the unresolved-hostname allow decision was the SSRF root cause.

The same direct feature commit added the unauthenticated request sinks; it was not an import, move, refactor, revert, release commit, or decomposed squash member.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The authenticated GET /download-export endpoint concatenated the attacker-controlled filename query parameter directly onto export_path(), checked only file_exists(), and passed the resulting path to response()->download(). Traversal components could therefore escape the export directory and disclose any file readable by the application process; the demonstrated impact is arbitrary file read, not write or code execution.

Commit 5eda5fcf38a87a1ceb39762474df6c2211def9fb later made the flawed method reachable at /download-export inside the auth middleware group, but did not write the vulnerable path construction. The later import/export aggregate 9049917b3807924bb301f35635d17958b23888cd only added a separate template-download method and retained the vulnerable method unchanged, so neither later commit is the smallest BIC.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The Markdown and PDF evaluation-export routes checked only whether the requester could view the conversion, while build_evaluation_report() selected every non-deleted evaluation comment and serialized each comment's content and author's first name without applying the existing per-comment privacy rule. A requester allowed to view a conversion could therefore export private evaluation comments that should have been visible only to the conversion owner, the comment author, or an administrator.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit c5d258d59530292bb17ab602d3b799373540596f directly introduced both export routes and build_evaluation_report(). The new routes called the report builder after only conversion-level authorization, and the new builder unconditionally appended all evaluation comments. The immediate parent already had the ordinary comment-visibility policy but had neither the report builder nor the export routes, so this is a direct feature introduction rather than a later import, move, rename, refactor, or aggregate.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An MCP caller can select smart_user operation=get-user-info and supply an attacker-controlled username. SmartUser.run dispatches to getUserInfo, which passes options.username to getUserDetails; on Unix that method interpolated the username into `getent passwd "${username}" || grep "^${username}:" /etc/passwd` and executed the string with promisified child_process.exec. POSIX command substitution remains active inside double quotes, so `$(...)` or backticks in username execute commands with the MCP server process's privileges.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The vulnerable smart-user implementation first appears in this target repository in fc3582544f6df4a14dcd3015edc835780f746aff, but that 69,886-line, 160-file commit expressly says it integrated 367 TypeScript files from the pre-existing hypercontext-mcp project. It is an aggregate external-source import, not the commit that originally authored the vulnerable shell interpolation. The true smallest BIC is therefore behind the unavailable hypercontext source-history boundary rather than a target-repository commit.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: After an administrator authenticates to the GlassFish Administration Console, crafted alertSummary or alertDetail request parameters can enter the shared alertMsg.inc template. The template copies request values into attributes rendered through #{alertSummary} and #{alertDetail}; JSFTemplating then evaluates the expressions with an unrestricted Faces EL resolver chain. Static methods, constructors, getClass()/class traversal, and static fields permit an injected expression to reach java.lang.Runtime and execute operating-system commands as the GlassFish service user. HTML escaping does not prevent the preceding server-side EL evaluation.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The vulnerable request-to-EL template is already present in parentless GlassFish root import 571714739b23e16c4c90d5229b806433920b3bcb, and the unrestricted JSFTemplating implementation is already present in parentless component root import 18d9b835fa98caec01ef026aab5ed907567dec0d. These are repository imports, not the smallest commits that wrote the flaw: the GlassFish root imports 30,345 files and 3,141,323 lines, while the component root imports 300 files and 141,910 lines. causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated bot author can store a rich-text link with a javascript: URL. Typebot serializes that author-controlled link and presents it to a visitor as active HTML or, in later viewers, assigns the stored URL directly to an anchor href without validating its protocol. A victim click executes attacker JavaScript in the viewer or embedding host page origin; target="_blank" and rel="noopener noreferrer" do not neutralize a javascript: URL. The assigned advisory snapshot records @typebot.io/js versions below 0.10.1 as vulnerable and 0.10.1 as first patched, and the first-party advisory metadata identifies application versions through 3.15.2 as affected and 3.16.0 as patched.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An initialized XKB client can first grow xkb->map->num_types to 255 with a SetMap request carrying XkbSetMapResizeTypes, then send firstType=255 and nTypes=10. CheckKeyTypes() accepts firstType because it rejects only firstType > num_types, computes the client-controlled sum nMaps=265 without bounding it to the caller's 256-entry mapWidths stack array, and writes mapWidthRtrn[i + firstType] for the supplied types. The writes to indices 256 through 264 overflow nine bytes into adjacent stack state, allowing a server crash and potentially privilege escalation when the X server is privileged.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: All causal code is already present in ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1, but that commit is a 609-file, 262690-insertion import explicitly described as 'R6.6 is the Xorg base-line', not the smallest authoring commit. Its imported xkb/xkb.c begins with an Xorg CVS revision dated 2000 and a 1993 copyright, so the vulnerable source predates the 2003 Git import. The retained repository does not contain the external CVS/X Consortium commit that first combined the fixed 256-entry stack array, unchecked firstType+nTypes sum, and indexed write.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: When persistent proxy memory is enabled, the proxy used the client-controlled x-headroom-user-id header as the memory partition key without authenticating or binding that identifier to the caller. A reachable client could select another user's partition, disclose stored memory through search/context injection, and create, update, or delete records in that partition. The shipped compose deployment made the data plane network-reachable by binding 0.0.0.0 and publishing port 8787 without requiring a proxy token.

Its sole parent 8c22a72715a328f1f7c3d4ba4a44516910192e80 contains neither the header selector nor proxy memory handler. causal_chain.bug_semantics: With OAuth enabled behind a reverse proxy that terminates browser-facing HTTPS and forwards the callback to Temporal UI Server over HTTP, authentication cookies used c.Request().TLS != nil to choose Secure. That request describes only the proxy-to-server hop, so the server could emit user* access/ID-token cookies and, later, refresh-token cookies without Secure even though the browser authenticated over HTTPS. Exploitation additionally requires steering the UI hostname to attacker-served HTTP, preventing HTTPS, and receiving a later same-site plaintext request while the credential is live; malicious content alone or passive observation of the successful TLS session is insufficient.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: temporalio/ui-server PR #219 moved the OAuth session from server-side cookies that forced Secure=true into browser-resident user* cookies containing the access token and set Secure from c.Request().TLS. The PR's sole source commit 8bca548c78fcadc737626bea96ef1e16075792d6 is the smallest real BIC. GitHub squash commit 821cf598371353f1b579dfe1e87aeb3638b041d6 landed the identical parent/tree/patch, temporalio/ui commit c6f84170173eb9e9d82a98fd78faf4adc8af09ed later imported the existing server tree, and later refresh-token work reused the same faulty transport inference; the squash, import, and extensions are not the origin.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: LiquidJS accepted a lexically resolved template pathname as proof that the file opened was inside a configured root, partials, or layouts directory. Node then followed symlinks at the file operation, so a symlink placed under an allowed template directory could point to an arbitrary readable file outside that directory and include, render, or layout would parse and render the external target. The assigned advisory records liquidjs <= 10.25.2 as vulnerable and 10.25.3 as the first patched version.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 8fbbec089fa4e3db4bec47462b1c08dd65c36648 is the smallest real BIC. Although the commit also moved existing modules, its newly added index.js handleCache() resolved an include name with path.resolve(this.options.root, filepath) and passed that non-canonical pathname to fs.readFileSync(), while the newly added tags/include.js evaluated the include name and called handleCache(). The immediate parent had neither handleCache/renderFile nor tags/include.js, so the causal filesystem-template load path was absent; later loader extractions, path checks, and file moves merely preserved or re-expressed this same symlink-following flaw.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: LiquidJS strip_html returned attacker-controlled HTML tags containing CR or LF instead of tag-stripped text. A payload such as therefore reached an unescaped HTML response, where browsers treat the line terminators as attribute whitespace and execute the event handler. In the advisory-era implementation the immediate defect was the generic <.*?> alternative: JavaScript dot did not consume CR/LF, while the other multiline alternatives used [\s\S].
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 4595e2872e7800b93b0d6e487430431a0402f0b2 first added strip_html with /<\/?\s*\w+\s*\/?>/g. That filter already returned the advisory's executable newline-and-attribute payload unchanged; its immediate parent had no strip_html at all. Commit 8e9e10fdb4c7f00ffa3997d3e2c0a0bfa48ce887 later replaced the original expression with the Ruby-Liquid-style alternatives and first wrote the advisory-era <.*?> implementation, but it did not introduce the vulnerability: the same payload and XSS trust path were already present in its parent. It changed the mechanism from a regex that rejected all attributed tags to one that handled same-line attributed tags but still rejected multiline ones.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated backend user holding backend.manage_editor can store attacker-controlled LESS in Editor Settings -> Markup Styles (html_custom_styles). LESS escaped-string syntax can preserve a literal </style><script>...</script><style> sequence. causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated backend user holding any one granular Theme Editor permission could enter Cms\Controllers\Index because the controller authorization was an OR gate, while AJAX code trusted the request-supplied template type without consistently checking the permission mapped to that type. The user could therefore reach pages, partials, layouts, content, or assets outside the granted scope. AssetList was also registered without requiring cms.manage_assets, and its upload path omitted the active-theme validation applied to other mutating asset handlers.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Single-parent commit 71a5dd67ab9e0d0da7caabd3fb5aaa3d86bb45e5 first added modules/cms/controllers/Index.php and modules/cms/widgets/AssetList.php while registering distinct cms.manage_* permissions. causal_chain.bug_semantics: getFilenameFromUrl accepts a decoded request pathname when it merely starts with the configured publicPath pathname, rejects dot-dot only when UP_PATH_REGEXP sees `..` as a complete path segment, and then slices the accepted string at publicPathPathname.length before joining the suffix to outputPath. With a non-slash-terminated publicPath `/assets`, `/assets../.env` passes the prefix check and guard because `..` remains embedded in the `assets..` segment, but the fixed-offset slice yields `../.env`, so path.join resolves one directory above outputPath. Disclosure requires a physical or custom output filesystem, such as writeToDisk; the default memfs and default publicPath `auto`/`/` do not expose this path, and URL normalization limits this bypass to one parent directory.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: OliveTin registered local-auth SIDs in server-side SessionStorage for about one year and authenticated requests that replayed the olivetin-sid-local cookie. Its implemented Logout flow expired only the browser cookie and did not delete the corresponding SID, so a copied pre-logout cookie remained accepted after the user appeared to log out; the eventual fix also revoked OAuth2's separate server-side state.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 8686a5629e6a8fae3d99f2af0a3e8c3c0c37aae0 is the smallest real BIC because it first implemented the advisory's exact vulnerable behavior: its new UI called Logout, and its Logout RPC returned an expired olivetin-sid-local cookie without revoking the already-authenticated provider/SID. The reviewer's earlier a7e7bf869ecbf87aa176337aac191e69bbcd90f9 added cookie-to-session authentication, but Logout at that tree was still a nonfunctional return-nil stub and did not clear a browser cookie; it supplied a prerequisite, not the post-logout bypass described by the advisory.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: OliveTin authorizes execution and disclosure of action logs independently. A caller granted exec:true but logs:false could invoke StartActionAndWait or StartActionByGetAndWait; each synchronous handler waited for the action, obtained its InternalLogEntry, converted the complete entry to the public LogEntry, and returned the action output without the logs authorization enforced on other log-bearing paths. causal_chain.bug_semantics: Stored XSS in the authenticated WebUI RSE-management flow. A privileged attacker can persist attacker-controlled markup in city, country_name, or ISP through the RSE creation path. The RSE list passes those stored values to DataTables as renderable data, while the RSE detail page concatenates them into HTML passed to jQuery.append. Viewing either page therefore parses the stored value as markup and can execute script in the victim's WebUI origin.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A project-scoped owner member or lessee administrator who may PATCH a volume target but is not permitted by baremetal:volume:view_target_properties can change an unrelated allowed field and receive the complete updated target in the HTTP 200 response. PATCH authorizes baremetal:volume:update, loads and updates the existing target, and serializes new_target without applying the target-properties redaction used by GET/list, thereby disclosing pre-existing iSCSI connection data or credentials. POST had the same unredacted response shape, but its caller supplied the returned values; the advisory's confidentiality escalation is the PATCH disclosure of existing secrets.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The original volume-target REST API commit c380e05dbf84079b01fb3b0ea099ef9b293b9b3d created an admin-only PATCH response that returned the complete target, so it is the latent response-shape origin, not the security BIC. Commit 000bc72cc29b8637df496f2e6768281606a27058 later rewrote the representation to plain JSON without changing that behavior. The vulnerability first became real in e870bd34d0ccacbaef7f4e4def2535eb28f822b9: that commit expanded baremetal:volume:update from system-only access to system/project owner-member and lessee-admin access, introduced a stricter baremetal:volume:view_target_properties boundary, enforced the new boundary on GET/list, and left PATCH returning the full target without the new check. This is the smallest causal commit inside the advisory's affected version boundary.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The authenticated /v1/completions endpoint accepted an attacker-chosen outer list of text prompts or token-id prompt lists. The serving path preserved that outer cardinality, created one engine generator and request ID per element, merged all generators, and allocated streaming or non-streaming response state proportional to the number of prompts. Per-prompt token and sampling limits therefore did not bound aggregate CPU, memory, scheduler, asynchronous-task, or response-buffer work initiated by one HTTP request.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: PR #2529 deliberately enabled batch completions. Its first member commit d04fd49c2bc9540237d3d11b6d1de26bbc35d232 removed the immediate-parent rejection of len(prompts) > 1 and added the complete unbounded fan-out mechanism: a generators list, a loop over every prompt, one engine.generate call per element, merge_async_iterators(*generators), and response arrays sized by prompt count. The second member a3a405c6a2b2f259671c5034c9a14e28187e97ac only added type annotations. The main-branch commit 3a7dd7e367277c47472912e84375fa912df07328 is the squash aggregate, not the smallest BIC; later imports, moves, and refactors merely preserved the mechanism and are also rejected as origins.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated attacker can persist attacker-controlled HTML or JavaScript in a replication rule comment. The WebUI later treated the returned comment as HTML in two places: the rule-detail page concatenated every rule metadata value into a jQuery-created table-row fragment, and the approval page supplied the raw comments value to DataTables. Viewing the rule or reviewing it for approval therefore executes the stored payload in the WebUI origin.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The optimized constant-integer for-loop exposed its native stack-local counter to script code through var(&i). ChaiScript's intentional := reference assignment could copy that alias into a returned Boxed_Value, including one transported by async/future. When the optimized-loop lambda returned, the counter's lifetime ended, but the escaped value retained its raw pointer; later numeric conversion in Boxed_Number::get_as dereferenced the dangling storage, producing garbage, an invalid read, or a segmentation fault.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated Administration Console user can persist attacker-controlled text in a configuration attribute, demonstrated by an application's description. A later browser request for that configuration object through the management REST interface receives text/html. The HTML provider reads the stored ConfigBean attribute and inserts it into generated markup without contextual HTML encoding; the reported payload containing is consequently parsed as an element and executes in the Administration Console origin with the victim administrator's session.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Legacy GlassFish commit be6b1571814721625e5e70343a2b178076d61450 first added the REST management HTML provider and directly concatenated proxy.attribute(attribute) between h2 tags. That was already an executable stored-XSS sink for attacker-controlled persistent configuration values. Commit 881906985072f3326ed2a53d3aa2f07a2c0973f8 later changed the presentation context to an unencoded input value attribute but did not introduce the underlying browser-facing unencoded output. Later provider moves, renames, refactors, and the parentless Eclipse Initial Contribution aggregate preserved the flaw and are rejected as BICs.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Genkit's unauthenticated developer servers listened beyond a loopback-only trust boundary and did not validate the HTTP Host header. A LAN peer, or a website using DNS rebinding, could reach the Tools/Dev UI or reflection runAction handler, execute registered actions with attacker-controlled input and context, and read results. The telemetry trace SSE handler also set Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, exposing trace data. CORS was not an authorization gate because it did not prevent handler execution and DNS rebinding made the request same-origin to the attacker's page.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The earliest public carrier is squash aggregate 91ed3de52e7db92943886526395ad8eac6faa77f. Its parent 805600159f34ca96d95c26c10c7b2799cb5951ce had only the stub Runner server and no runAction or reflection execution path; the aggregate adds an unauthenticated Runner runAction proxy, a reflection /api/runAction executor, and listeners without host arguments or Host validation. The aggregate message enumerates 27 squashed member changes, including 'Added basic Reflection API', 'Added starting of app code when starting Runner API', and 'Implemented passthrough endpoints in Runner API'. Those unavailable member objects must be distinguished to identify the smallest commit that first completed the exploitable path, so the aggregate itself is not accepted as the BIC.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: RustCrypto ml-dsa signature decoding reused one monotonicity predicate for two encodings with different rules. Hint cut offsets may repeat because a polynomial may have no hints, but hint indices inside each polynomial must be strictly increasing. Changing the shared comparison from < to <= made repeated cuts valid while also accepting duplicate indices. Verification could therefore accept a non-canonical, byte-distinct signature carrying a repeated hint index, causing ML-DSA signature malleability across ML-DSA-44, ML-DSA-65, and ML-DSA-87.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: With address auto-creation disabled, an authenticated OpenWire client could request a non-durable JMS topic subscription on a nonexistent address while permitted to create and consume from the subscription queue but denied CREATE_ADDRESS. The topic path skipped the broker's address auto-creation preflight and directly created a temporary queue, which implicitly materialized the missing temporary address without enforcing CREATE_ADDRESS; the address remained until the OpenWire connection closed. The fix's regression fixture grants CREATE_NON_DURABLE_QUEUE, although the advisory prose calls the relevant permission createDurableQueue.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit 84e8a87325a976c9970b8e85d03fc33207623af3 introduced Artemis's independent CREATE_ADDRESS permission and explicit separately-authorized address-creation operation while leaving the OpenWire non-durable-topic path able to create a temporary queue directly and the server queue-creation path able to materialize its missing address after checking only queue-creation permission. The older OpenWire code was a precursor, but before this commit there was no separate create-address authorization invariant for it to bypass.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: When the image proxy is enabled, an authenticated forum user can embed an attacker-selected non-HTTPS URL in an IMG BBCode tag. SMF rewrites it to its own proxy.php URL and supplies the secret-derived hash, after which the server dereferences the selected URL. Before the fixes, that dereference did not reliably reject hostnames resolving to loopback, private, link-local, cloud-metadata, or other reserved addresses, and redirects could reach the same destinations. The hash therefore did not prevent an authenticated poster from causing SSRF into services visible to the SMF host.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The attachment-approval path obtains the boards on which the authenticated user has approve_posts permission, but its per-attachment authorization predicate uses assignment rather than comparison: in 2.1, `$allowed_boards = array(0) || in_array(...)`, and in 3.0, `$allowed_boards = [0] || \in_array(...)`. causal_chain.bug_semantics: In policycoreutils/scripts/fixfiles, the DEFAULT restore path used find to select entries with unlabeled or undefined SELinux contexts and then invoked a separate privileged chcon process on each pathname. The non-full-cleanup relabel path reached the same code. An attacker controlling a searched directory could replace an intermediate component with a symlink after find checked the entry but before chcon resolved the pathname, causing an arbitrary target such as /etc/shadow to receive the attacker's chosen SELinux label. chcon --no-dereference protected only the final component and did not make the find-to-chcon pathname handoff atomic.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The vulnerable find-then-chcon mechanism predates the validated Git history. It is therefore a history boundary, not the smallest real BIC. Later commits only changed label selection, broadened the searched directories, moved the existing block, or added final-component --no-dereference handling without originating the race. The pre-r2950 Subversion member revision that first wrote the mechanism is unavailable in the clone.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: ClassroomIO v0.1.13 exposed its browser-reachable Supabase/PostgREST course resource without a server-side authorization rule that limited an authenticated student to the relations and fields appropriate for that role. A student could issue GET /rest/v1/course with a relational select expanding course to group, groupmember, profile, lesson, and teacher profile data; the effective course policy admitted course members while group/groupmember/profile reads exposed other people and metadata. The browser's normal query and UI role checks were not a security boundary because the student controlled the HTTP method and select expression.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Neither disputed SHA is a valid smallest real BIC. Primary candidate 60f06d6ab1468dd276ba4b95fe9478d4f95ce3e7 is a 77-file 'Sync with Server' aggregate that first adds the release-line browser projection, but that projection merely exercises the server authorization boundary and does not create the ability to send an arbitrary PostgREST GET. Reviewer candidate a0997b0b6951948efd7a8e8c5516c3d549f69cab is the first public repository representation of the causal grants/policies, but it adds a 1,290-line file explicitly named 20231115082347_remote_schema.sql containing a dump of an already-existing remote database. Its parent proves only repository absence, not absence in the deployed database. Later RLS commits preserve the exposure rather than originate it. Because imports, synchronization aggregates, moves, squashes, and reverts cannot substitute for the original smallest writer, the true BIC and its parent are outside the available public history.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: During ZIP extraction, a local attacker able to mutate the extraction directory can replace an already-validated parent directory with a symlink before OpenClaw opens the destination pathname. The later pathname-based write follows the rebound parent and can create or truncate a file outside the extraction root with the OpenClaw process's privileges; leaf-only O_NOFOLLOW protection does not bind mutable parent traversal to the checked directory identity.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Original feature implementation. Commit 3a6ee5ee00176c88aee32bb8bfd543780014c079 first added the production ZIP extractor in src/infra/archive.ts with a lexical path.resolve/string-prefix containment check followed by separate mkdir, asynchronous ZIP decoding, and fs.writeFile(outPath, data). That check/use separation created the parent-symlink TOCTOU window at inception; later streaming and partial symlink-hardening changes retained the same mutable-parent pathname resolution and are not origins.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: TemplateContext.LimitToString bounded one ObjectToString conversion rather than cumulative rendered output. Each rendered expression entered a fresh top-level ObjectToString call, which reset _currentToStringLength, and StringBuilderOutput appended every resulting chunk without a render-wide cap. A template could therefore emit a near-1 MiB string in each of 1,000 loop iterations, pass the per-call check each time, and accumulate roughly 1 GiB until the host exhausted memory.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95 is the smallest real BIC: it directly added LimitToString, _currentToStringLength, and the top-level reset that made the safety counter restart for every ObjectToString conversion. Its two-file focused patch is neither a merge, aggregate, import, nor move, and its immediate parent lacks both LimitToString and _currentToStringLength. The older unconditional StringBuilderOutput append was a necessary sink but did not create the advisory-specific limit-bypass invariant; b5ac4bf30459fdc76964e3f751e16f7e96079ea7 later enabled the already-flawed limit by default. Commit 98563216488161a9edeba6c37c7cf82c98319c9b directly fixed the flaw by adding cumulative output accounting across write chunks.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Rendering a ScriptObject recursively stringifies each stored member value without object-identity cycle detection. A member that points back to its containing ScriptObject therefore repeatedly re-enters object rendering; because ObjectRecursionLimit defaulted to 0 (unlimited), the guard was disabled and recursion continued until an uncatchable StackOverflowException terminated the host process.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e is the smallest real introducer. It changed ScriptObject enumeration to expose each stored value and added the ScriptObject-specific formatter that recursively calls ToString on that value. Its immediate parent lacks both vulnerable operations. The later a9affb64614358838aba16f28acb198f914e586d guard retained ObjectRecursionLimit=0 as the default and therefore preserved, rather than introduced, the already-existing vulnerable path.

evidence: Repository and advisory checks: `git remote get-url origin` returned https://github.com/scriban/scriban. The repository advisory https://github.com/scriban/scriban/security/advisories/GHSA-grr9-747v-xvcp gives the self-referential ScriptObject PoC, states that default ObjectRecursionLimit=0 is unlimited and causes a fatal StackOverflowException, lists 6.5.8 as affected, and lists 6.6.0 as patched; the assigned syndicated GHSA-PPRH-WGQR-2MMX/CVE-2026-74794 bundle describes versions before 6.6.0 as affected.

Smallest-BIC and direct-parent checks: `git show --format=fuller --patch cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e -- src/Scriban/Runtime/ScriptValueConverter.cs src/Scriban/Runtime/ScriptObject.cs` shows the same commit changing GetEnumerator from item.Value to item.Value.Value and adding `result.Append(ToString(span, keyPair.Value));`. `git show 790f00752e7b7392f2849452f37345852f313634:src/Scriban/Runtime/ScriptValueConverter.cs` shows no ScriptObject-specific branch, and the BIC patch shows the parent did not expose the stored value. The advisory PoC's recursive edge is therefore absent in the direct parent.

Aggregate/import/move rejection: `git cat-file -p cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e` shows exactly one parent, 790f00752e7b7392f2849452f37345852f313634, while the patch contains the functional additions themselves rather than an import or move. `git log --all --format='%H %P %s' -S'result.Append(ToString(span, keyPair.Value))' -- src/Scriban/Runtime/ScriptValueConverter.cs src/Textamina.Scriban/Runtime/ScriptValueConverter.cs` finds cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e as the addition and 55a6d61fb656e87a49bbe49334236be558c5d3a1 only as the later removal during refactoring, so the later move is rejected as the BIC. No squash decomposition is needed.

Lifecycle and direct-fix checks: `git show a9affb64614358838aba16f28acb198f914e586d -- src/Scriban/TemplateContext.Helpers.cs src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs` shows a guard conditional on ObjectRecursionLimit != 0 together with the default assignment ObjectRecursionLimit=0 and documentation that zero means no limit. `git show --format=fuller --patch a6fe6074199e5c04f4d29dc8d8e652b24d33e3e4 -- src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs` directly changes that default from 0 to 20. `git cat-file -p` for the fix shows one parent, so despite its subject saying 'Merge commit from fork', it is not a merge aggregate and directly contains the closing change.

Version-boundary checks: `git rev-parse 6.5.8^{commit} 6.6.0^{commit}` resolved b640147b792c41aa3756b463673c741e46c44470 and b5ac4bf30459fdc76964e3f751e16f7e96079ea7. `git diff 6.5.8^{commit} 6.6.0^{commit} -- src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs` shows ObjectRecursionLimit changing from 0 to 20, and `git tag --contains a6fe6074199e5c04f4d29dc8d8e652b24d33e3e4` starts at 6.6.0 and excludes 6.5.8.

Marker-state disagreement resolution: the primary encoded `ai_marker` as prose beginning `absent:`, whereas the reviewer encoded it as null. Re-running `git cat-file -t cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e` returned `commit`, and `git cat-file -p cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e` showed one parent, author and committer Alexandre Mutel <alexandre_mutel@live.com>, and only the ordinary subject `Fix pretty print object ScriptObject and ScriptArray, dump objects with {...} and [...]`. The BIC commit object has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, AI trailer, or other AI signal. Therefore the canonical marker state is null: the reviewer's state wins, while the primary's underlying observation was correct but placed in the wrong field representation. No PR, branch, later commit, or fix-commit attribution was used.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The runner registration-token API exposed token creation through GET routes. The token-scope middleware derives Read versus Write from the HTTP method and classifies GET as Read, but shared.GetRegistrationToken creates a runner token when no active token exists and returns it. A leaked read-scoped user, organization, repository, or admin token could therefore obtain a runner registration credential and register a malicious Actions runner able to receive workflow jobs with access to repository source and secrets.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: PR #27144 was squash-landed as baf0d402d9cb47849394202fcfc7c2e23b0faac3, but that mainline aggregate is not the smallest BIC. The reconstructable PR member eec5ed07521ffc767c0dd1bdccdece8a7f54fe3f first added the shared GET handler whose missing/inactive-token branch calls NewRunnerToken and added reachable organization and admin GET registration-token routes. Its immediate parent already classified GET as Read and contained neither the route nor the helper. The later member bba250f3e99bef12bbd9a1d9d790ab8155c999d5 extended the same mechanism to user and repository routes rather than originating it.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An administrator or authenticated caller with connect-write authority can persist an attacker-chosen ConnectURL. causal_chain.bug_semantics: Ech0 globally installed its i18n middleware and passed unauthenticated request-controlled locale values, including the raw Accept-Language header after only TrimSpace, to go-i18n and golang.org/x/text/language.ParseAcceptLanguage without a size or shape bound. The x/text CVE-2022-32149 mitigation counted '-' separators but the parser also aliases '_' to '-', so a near-1 MiB malformed underscore-separated value bypassed the guard and exercised quadratic parsing, allowing unauthenticated CPU denial of service on every route. X-Locale and the lang query parameter also reached the same unbounded parser through ResolveLocale.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit b55edabd228d3de41e781bd3100f2e1ee0835516 first created Ech0's complete remotely reachable vulnerable path: it added internal/i18n/i18n.go, forwarded unbounded locale values to ParseAcceptLanguage and goi18n.NewLocalizer, read Accept-Language from the request, and registered the middleware globally. The parser weakness pre-existed in x/text, but the immediate parent did not contain Ech0's i18n parser path or global exposure.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The withdrawn report alleged that an attacker could begin an OAuth sign-in, reach an OTP challenge, alter the factor strategy in the attempt request, and complete authentication without the correct code. A browser can always alter its request, so the alleged bypass would require the Frontend API server to accept a factor that was not valid for the prepared sign-in state. The CNA subsequently rejected CVE-2025-63700 after determining that it was not a security issue.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: No verified flaw exists in clerk/javascript. At @clerk/clerk-js 5.88.0 the public SDK only sends the selected strategy and entered code to the Frontend API; the authentication decision and factor-to-state binding are server-side. The relevant client transport predates 5.88.0, and the authoritative rejection establishes no vulnerable server behavior or repository-local origin.

Commit 65f6b9f961efe533b4d3f20f1eddad132fe8ef1d merely moved the already-vulnerable save lookup into TicketRepository and is not an introducer.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The POST routes /fetch_misp_event and /misp_search_events accepted a caller-controlled HTTPS MISP base URL and made server-side requests whose response data was returned to the caller. _validate_misp_url rejected unsafe IP literals but accepted every ordinary hostname without resolving it, so an attacker could use a hostname resolving to a private, loopback, link-local, or reserved address to reach and read an internal HTTPS service. The routes were also callable anonymously, increasing exposure, while the unresolved-hostname allow decision was the SSRF root cause.

The same direct feature commit added the unauthenticated request sinks; it was not an import, move, refactor, revert, release commit, or decomposed squash member.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The authenticated GET /download-export endpoint concatenated the attacker-controlled filename query parameter directly onto export_path(), checked only file_exists(), and passed the resulting path to response()->download(). Traversal components could therefore escape the export directory and disclose any file readable by the application process; the demonstrated impact is arbitrary file read, not write or code execution.

Commit 5eda5fcf38a87a1ceb39762474df6c2211def9fb later made the flawed method reachable at /download-export inside the auth middleware group, but did not write the vulnerable path construction. The later import/export aggregate 9049917b3807924bb301f35635d17958b23888cd only added a separate template-download method and retained the vulnerable method unchanged, so neither later commit is the smallest BIC.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: A project-scoped owner member or lessee administrator who may PATCH a volume target but is not permitted by baremetal:volume:view_target_properties can change an unrelated allowed field and receive the complete updated target in the HTTP 200 response. PATCH authorizes baremetal:volume:update, loads and updates the existing target, and serializes new_target without applying the target-properties redaction used by GET/list, thereby disclosing pre-existing iSCSI connection data or credentials. POST had the same unredacted response shape, but its caller supplied the returned values; the advisory's confidentiality escalation is the PATCH disclosure of existing secrets.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The original volume-target REST API commit c380e05dbf84079b01fb3b0ea099ef9b293b9b3d created an admin-only PATCH response that returned the complete target, so it is the latent response-shape origin, not the security BIC. Commit 000bc72cc29b8637df496f2e6768281606a27058 later rewrote the representation to plain JSON without changing that behavior. The vulnerability first became real in e870bd34d0ccacbaef7f4e4def2535eb28f822b9: that commit expanded baremetal:volume:update from system-only access to system/project owner-member and lessee-admin access, introduced a stricter baremetal:volume:view_target_properties boundary, enforced the new boundary on GET/list, and left PATCH returning the full target without the new check. This is the smallest causal commit inside the advisory's affected version boundary.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: OpenClaw's ZIP extractor constructed an output path under the extraction directory, checked path and symlink state, and only afterward opened that pathname for truncating/writing. A local attacker able to mutate the extraction tree could replace a checked parent directory with a symlink during that gap, causing an entry such as slot/target.txt to resolve outside the extraction root and clobber the external target. O_NOFOLLOW protected only the final path component; it did not bind parent resolution to the object that had been checked.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Original feature implementation. Commit 3a6ee5ee00176c88aee32bb8bfd543780014c079 first added the production ZIP extractor in src/infra/archive.ts with lexical containment checking followed by mkdir and fs.writeFile(outPath, data). Subsequent streaming and symlink-hardening commits changed the sink but preserved the same check/use separation; in particular 4b226b74f5fd3b106a83a6347fd404172e2fd246 added parent checks and O_NOFOLLOW on the leaf without making parent traversal race-safe.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: TemplateContext.LimitToString bounded only one ObjectToString conversion, not the cumulative rendered template. TemplateContext.Write(SourceSpan, object) converts each rendered expression through a fresh top-level ObjectToString call; ObjectToString resets _currentToStringLength whenever _objectToStringLevel is zero; and StringBuilderOutput.Write appends every resulting chunk without a cumulative cap. A template can therefore make a 1,048,575-character string, render it in each of the default 1000 loop iterations, pass the 1,048,576-character per-call limit every time, and accumulate roughly 1 GB in the output StringBuilder until the host process runs out of memory.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95 (Add TemplateContext.LimitToString) introduced the vulnerable safety mechanism: it added _currentToStringLength and reset it to zero at every top-level ObjectToString call, while leaving the already-existing output sink cumulative-unbounded. The older unconditional StringBuilderOutput append is a precondition, but b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95 is the smallest commit that created the advisory's LimitToString-bypass combination; b5ac4bf30459fdc76964e3f751e16f7e96079ea7 later changed the default LimitToString from disabled to 1,048,576 and made the bypass present under default 6.6.0 settings rather than introducing the reset.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The default object.to_json builtin recursively serializes IList/array elements and object members through a static local WriteValue function without a recursion-depth limit, execution-stack guard, or circular-reference detection. A template can create a ScriptObject that points to itself and pass it to object.to_json; WriteValue then revisits the same object until .NET raises the fatal, effectively uncatchable StackOverflowException, terminating the host process. Deep acyclic input can exhaust the stack by the same path.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The vulnerable ToJson/WriteValue implementation was first written in PR #533 member commit a65c891245e2c8550fb28fcd6e9d296c99ad6a2f. GitHub landed PR #533 as the one-parent squash f2f3cf41cde1ba7226760fd9b456f3d5d7aa1ca1, but the retained eight-member PR chain and identical head/squash trees permit decomposition; the second member is the smallest commit that adds object.to_json and both unchecked recursive calls.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Scriban's object-to-string rendering recursively formats every ScriptObject member value without tracking object identity. With the default ObjectRecursionLimit of 0 (unlimited), a ScriptObject that directly or indirectly contains itself repeatedly re-enters ObjectToString until the CLR throws an uncatchable StackOverflowException, terminating the host process and enabling denial of service wherever an attacker can influence the rendered object graph.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e is the smallest real introducer: it added the ScriptObject-specific pretty-print branch to ScriptValueConverter.ToString and the recursive call result.Append(ToString(span, keyPair.Value)). Its parent only handled ScriptObject through the generic IEnumerable path and did not recursively extract a KeyValuePair's Value, so the advisory PoC's self-referential ScriptObject path was absent. Later commits moved/refactored the formatter; a9affb64614358838aba16f28acb198f914e586d added an opt-in recursion guard but explicitly initialized ObjectRecursionLimit to 0, preserving the vulnerable default rather than introducing the already-existing recursion.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The API scope middleware derives write versus read permission solely from the HTTP method and therefore treats every GET as read-only. The GET runner registration-token handlers are not read-only: shared.GetRegistrationToken calls NewRunnerToken when no active token exists and returns the usable token. A leaked read:user token (or the corresponding read-scoped owner/repository token) can consequently mint or obtain a runner registration credential, register an attacker-controlled Actions runner, and receive workflow work exposing source and repository secrets.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The vulnerable GET-plus-create design first appears in PR #27144 source member eec5ed07521ffc767c0dd1bdccdece8a7f54fe3f, which added the shared state-mutating handler and reachable organization/admin GET routes; member bba250f3e99bef12bbd9a1d9d790ab8155c999d5 then added the user and repository GET routes. GitHub squashed the 22-member PR into mainline aggregate baf0d402d9cb47849394202fcfc7c2e23b0faac3, so that aggregate is not the smallest BIC.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An authenticated user could persist an arbitrary ConnectURL through the JWT-protected add-Connect operation. The server-side GetConnectsInfo path then read every stored URL and called the unrestricted HTTP helper on TrimURL(conn.ConnectURL) + "/api/connect"; the route introduced with that behavior was public, and later peer-info/health paths reused the same unsafe fetch. With no scheme/host/IP validation and no DNS-safe dialer, a stored peer URL could drive server-originated requests to loopback, private networks, link-local cloud metadata, or internal DNS names.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Second-order Oracle SQL identifier injection in the post-CREATE/post-UPDATE row lookup. Oracle table names are read verbatim from user_tables.TABLE_NAME and carried into the external-table query metadata. When Oracle returns response.lastRowid, OracleIntegration.query constructs SELECT * FROM "<table name>" WHERE ROWID = '<driver-produced ROWID>' by direct interpolation. An embedded double quote in the table name terminates the quoted identifier and makes the remainder SQL syntax. A user able to write that external table can trigger the lookup; the injected SQL runs with the configured Oracle datasource user's privileges and can cross Budibase's table/row authorization boundary. response.lastRowid is not the attacker-controlled part.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: 115fc08aa4d08ca08c65c84e3805c6df0e1ea0b8 is the smallest real origin: it replaced the prior returning implementation with a post-write ROWID lookup and first wrote the raw quoted-identifier interpolation, initially using json.endpoint.entityId. At that revision ExternalRequest derives endpoint.entityId directly from tableName, while Oracle schema introspection stores row.TABLE_NAME verbatim, so the original line already has the same identifier-injection semantics. dbe9eedcbadc6d164447078039801a53a2dcfa65 later changed the expression from json.endpoint.entityId to json.table.name but preserved the unsafe double-quote interpolation; it is a source-name rewrite, not the BIC.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Ech0 installed internal/i18n.Middleware() on the global Gin router, so every unauthenticated request supplied its raw, trimmed Accept-Language header to NewLocalizer. NewLocalizer passed that unbounded value directly to go-i18n, whose tag parsing reaches golang.org/x/text/language.ParseAcceptLanguage. The x/text CVE-2022-32149 guard counts '-' separators but the scanner also aliases '_' to '-', so a near-1 MiB header made from malformed underscore-separated subtags bypasses the guard and exercises quadratic gobble/memmove behavior. The same unbounded parser was also reachable through X-Locale and the lang query parameter via ResolveLocale, with those explicit-locale paths potentially adding another parse. This is an unauthenticated CPU denial of service on public routes.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Application-boundary flaw first created by b55edabd228d3de41e781bd3100f2e1ee0835516: that single ordinary commit added the i18n implementation, directly forwarded acceptLanguage to goi18n.NewLocalizer, read Accept-Language from the request without a size/shape bound, and globally registered the middleware. The underlying parser behavior pre-existed in dependencies, but Ech0's remotely reachable unbounded data path did not exist in the immediate parent.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Authenticated users remain inside their configured filesystem scope but can bypass administrator path deny rules because authorization compares the uncanonicalized virtual path literally while the backing filesystem resolves an equivalent name differently. On case-insensitive filesystems, a case variant such as /secret.TXT names denied /Secret.txt without matching its case-sensitive rule. On Windows, a mixed-separator traversal such as /allow\..\Secret.txt likewise misses the slash-based rule while filepath/afero resolves it to the denied file. The affected operations include reads and, subject to the user's ordinary permissions, modification, deletion, copying, and sharing; internally generated OS-separated paths also caused nested recursive/archive checks to miss rules on Windows.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The recoverable pre-squash PR history is two-stage. Commit 3dcbdfc8776b25f58a9134ba9f4d893f62db2b7c first wrote the flawed path-rule primitive: User.IsAllowed uses raw, case-sensitive strings.HasPrefix(url, rule.Path), while User.BuildFs exposes the scope through afero.NewBasePathFs and therefore host filesystem path semantics. Commit 41828f18050c3e90fc54ea2468324246b45e7d85 then activated that primitive at the HTTP resource gate and directory-listing checks. The smallest source-level flaw origin is 3dcbdfc8776b25f58a9134ba9f4d893f62db2b7c; later moves through types/rule.go, lib/rule.go, rules/rules.go, and master squash 12b2c215221696de58431093e01eeff7a5414471 preserve rather than originate it.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The top-level GET /api/config route accepts requests without an authentication dependency. In v0.6.32 an unauthenticated request still receives instance identity/version, OAuth-provider names, and authentication/security feature flags including auth mode, trusted-header auth, LDAP, API-key, signup, login-form, WebSocket, and update-check settings. An optional bearer token or cookie only selects additional authenticated fields; absence of a token is not rejected. This is the information-disclosure/authentication-bypass behavior described by CVE-2025-63391/GHSA-hqhc-8hp4-hrwc.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Original implementation: single-parent commit 733e963c44d0ffd71bfc1acedb185c42592db66e directly added the unauthenticated top-level /api/config route and returned application configuration. Later commits expanded the public response. Commit cbadf39d7d73638214b8a2bea5946f46290c3749 added optional user detection and gated richer user-only configuration, but deliberately retained a public response and therefore did not close the advisory's stated unauthenticated configuration disclosure.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The withdrawn report alleged that, after beginning an OAuth sign-in and reaching an OTP challenge, an attacker could alter the attempt request's authentication strategy (for example, swap an email-code attempt to another factor) and have the server complete authentication without the correct code. The public clerk-js 5.88.0 UI does send the factor strategy and entered code to the Frontend API, but that client-controlled request is not an authentication trust boundary; the alleged bypass requires the server to accept a strategy that was not valid for the sign-in attempt. The CNA later rejected CVE-2025-63700 because further investigation established that this was not a security issue.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: No verified flaw exists in the audited repository. The allegation depended on improper state/factor validation by Clerk's non-public Frontend API backend, while clerk/javascript only constructs and sends the client request. The relevant client request behavior predates 5.88.0 and was unchanged by that release, and the authoritative CVE record plus Clerk's first-party vulnerability history state that the report was investigated, withdrawn, and never a real vulnerability.

audit_record.reasoning: The report's proposed attack crosses the browser/server boundary: changing a browser request is always possible, so a bypass exists only if the Frontend API fails to bind an OTP attempt to the prepared factor and sign-in state. The public SDK at 5.88.0 passes the UI-selected factor strategy and code to that API, but contains no server-side authentication decision. Git diff shows 5.88.0 did not introduce the relevant request path, and git log -L shows the generic path existed years earlier. There is no closing patch or first patched package version; 5.89.0's OTP work only changes the input UI. Most decisively, on 2025-12-23 the CNA withdrew the CVE after determining it was not a security issue, and Clerk's first-party history says it was never a real vulnerability. Selecting the 2022 request helper, the 5.88.0 release commit, or any later change as a BIC would therefore violate the protocol's requirement for the smallest commit that first wrote genuinely vulnerable lines. Since no true BIC exists, there is no parent-absence claim and no BIC commit object on which an AI marker may be judged. EVIDENCE_GAP is used rather than NOT_AI because a closed NOT_AI verdict requires a real BIC; it is used rather than BLOCKED because the repository and public lifecycle are accessible, but the reachable evidence does not establish any vulnerability to attribute.
audit_record.remaining_gap: A closed AI/non-AI attribution would require a reproducible authentication bypass plus the actual code and history of the server-side factor/state validation that caused and fixed it. No such reproducer, vulnerable backend line, fix commit, or patched version is present in the cited report or public repository, and the CNA/vendor instead affirmatively concluded that the report was not a security issue. Consequently there is no defensible BIC, parent-absence proof, fix SHA, or BIC-only AI marker to record.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Authenticated cross-tenant IDOR/BOLA in the web ticket CRUD: GET /ticket/update/{id} loaded Ticket::find($id) and exposed another tenant's ticket content and attachments; POST /ticket/save accepted an attacker-selected ticket id, loaded that record without company_id scoping, then overwrote company_id with the attacker's company and saved it; GET /ticket/delete/{id} loaded and deleted any numeric ticket id without tenant scoping, and its generic Request parameter bypassed the authorization implemented by TicketDeleteRequest.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The original ticket CRUD commit 2feef9f35593dba39525f6a8a07b4cd3f74f19bd directly introduced the first vulnerable read and save endpoints and their unscoped Ticket::find lookups. Commit 946a0c5e43a1178534e5b013ea2608d565686220 later expanded the same flaw class by adding the unscoped GET delete endpoint. Commit 65f6b9f961efe533b4d3f20f1eddad132fe8ef1d only moved the already-vulnerable save lookup into TicketRepository and is not a BIC. Commit c837c80a4f7de40348e142af7d15e60c39ebcaf1 later created TicketDeleteRequest but did not wire it into TicketDeleteController, so it was incomplete hardening rather than the origin.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The public POST routes /fetch_misp_event and /misp_search_events accepted a caller-controlled HTTPS MISP base URL and API key, then made server-side requests and returned the remote JSON response or selected event data. _validate_misp_url rejected unsafe IP literals but treated every syntactically ordinary hostname as safe without DNS resolution. A hostname resolving to a private, loopback, link-local, or reserved address therefore bypassed the guard, allowing an anonymous network caller to make cti-transmute reach an internal HTTPS service and disclose its response. The direct fix resolves domain names, requires every resulting address to be globally routable, and requires authentication on both routes.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The Markdown and PDF evaluation-export routes authorized only access to the conversion, then build_evaluation_report() selected every non-deleted evaluation comment without applying the already-established per-comment privacy rule. On a public conversion, any viewer, including an anonymous viewer, could therefore export a private evaluation comment belonging to another author and receive both its content and the author's first name; only the conversion owner, comment author, or an administrator should see such a comment.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Direct feature introduction in c5d258d59530292bb17ab602d3b799373540596f: the same one-parent commit created both export routes and build_evaluation_report(), whose comment loop appended every selected evaluation comment without a visibility check. Later conversion-model renames and refactors preserved that omission; blame immediately before the fix still traces the query, loop, author, and content lines to c5d258d59530292bb17ab602d3b799373540596f.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The volume-target PATCH handler authorized baremetal:volume:update, loaded the complete existing VolumeTarget, applied even an unrelated permitted patch such as one to extra, persisted it, and serialized the returned object with convert_with_links without either enforcing baremetal:volume:view_target_properties on the response or masking password-like values in properties. A project-scoped caller allowed to update a target but forbidden to view target properties could therefore use the 200 PATCH response to read pre-existing iSCSI credentials. POST also returned properties unredacted, but those values had just been supplied by that caller and are not the confidentiality escalation at the root of this CVE.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: The response-sanitization omission was introduced with the original volume-target REST API in c380e05dbf84079b01fb3b0ea099ef9b293b9b3d (released in 9.0.0). It became a privilege-boundary vulnerability when project-scoped volume target access was added in e870bd34d0ccacbaef7f4e4def2535eb28f822b9, which is contained in 17.0.0 but no 16.* tag. Later commit 000bc72cc29b8637df496f2e6768281606a27058 only converted the endpoint representation and preserved the same unsanitized PATCH response, so it is a refactor rather than the BIC.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: During ZIP extraction, a local attacker able to mutate the extraction directory can replace an already-validated parent directory with a symlink before OpenClaw opens the destination pathname. The later pathname-based write follows the rebound parent and can create or truncate a file outside the extraction root with the OpenClaw process's privileges; leaf-only O_NOFOLLOW protection does not bind mutable parent traversal to the checked directory identity.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Original feature implementation. Commit 3a6ee5ee00176c88aee32bb8bfd543780014c079 first added the production ZIP extractor in src/infra/archive.ts with a lexical path.resolve/string-prefix containment check followed by separate mkdir, asynchronous ZIP decoding, and fs.writeFile(outPath, data). That check/use separation created the parent-symlink TOCTOU window at inception; later streaming and partial symlink-hardening changes retained the same mutable-parent pathname resolution and are not origins.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: TemplateContext.LimitToString bounded one ObjectToString conversion rather than cumulative rendered output. Each rendered expression entered a fresh top-level ObjectToString call, which reset _currentToStringLength, and StringBuilderOutput appended every resulting chunk without a render-wide cap. A template could therefore emit a near-1 MiB string in each of 1,000 loop iterations, pass the per-call check each time, and accumulate roughly 1 GiB until the host exhausted memory.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95 is the smallest real BIC: it directly added LimitToString, _currentToStringLength, and the top-level reset that made the safety counter restart for every ObjectToString conversion. Its two-file focused patch is neither a merge, aggregate, import, nor move, and its immediate parent lacks both LimitToString and _currentToStringLength. The older unconditional StringBuilderOutput append was a necessary sink but did not create the advisory-specific limit-bypass invariant; b5ac4bf30459fdc76964e3f751e16f7e96079ea7 later enabled the already-flawed limit by default. Commit 98563216488161a9edeba6c37c7cf82c98319c9b directly fixed the flaw by adding cumulative output accounting across write chunks.

`git show --format= --find-renames b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95 -- src/Scriban/TemplateContext.Helpers.cs src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs` directly shows the addition of _currentToStringLength, the `_objectToStringLevel == 0` reset, per-conversion LimitToString checks, and the LimitToString property. `git show --format=fuller --stat --summary` shows a focused, single-parent, two-file modification with no rename, import, merge, or aggregate boundary.

`git log --all --reverse -S'_currentToStringLength' -- src/Scriban/TemplateContext.Helpers.cs src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs` returns only b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95, confirming the vulnerable counter's origin rather than a later move or refactor.

`git cat-file commit 98563216488161a9edeba6c37c7cf82c98319c9b` shows a single parent and subject `Enforce cumulative output size limits`; `git grep` at that commit finds _currentOutputLength, WriteOutputChunk, GetAllowedOutputCount, and ResetOutputLimitTracking throughout the synchronous output path, establishing it as the direct causal source fix rather than a release aggregate.

`git rev-parse 6.6.0^{} 7.0.0^{}` resolves the release tags to b5ac4bf30459fdc76964e3f751e16f7e96079ea7 and 25d148a104dd4d679a1a1932442616599e003c2f. `git tag --contains 98563216488161a9edeba6c37c7cf82c98319c9b --sort=version:refname` starts at 7.0.0 and contains no 6.x release, matching the advisory's last-affected/first-patched boundary.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: Rendering a ScriptObject recursively stringifies each stored member value without object-identity cycle detection. A member that points back to its containing ScriptObject therefore repeatedly re-enters object rendering; because ObjectRecursionLimit defaulted to 0 (unlimited), the guard was disabled and recursion continued until an uncatchable StackOverflowException terminated the host process.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e is the smallest real introducer. It changed ScriptObject enumeration to expose each stored value and added the ScriptObject-specific formatter that recursively calls ToString on that value. Its immediate parent lacks both vulnerable operations. The later a9affb64614358838aba16f28acb198f914e586d guard retained ObjectRecursionLimit=0 as the default and therefore preserved, rather than introduced, the already-existing vulnerable path.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: The runner registration-token API exposed token creation through GET routes. The token-scope middleware derives Read versus Write from the HTTP method and classifies GET as Read, but shared.GetRegistrationToken creates a runner token when no active token exists and returns it. A leaked read-scoped user, organization, repository, or admin token could therefore obtain a runner registration credential and register a malicious Actions runner able to receive workflow jobs with access to repository source and secrets.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: PR #27144 was squash-landed as baf0d402d9cb47849394202fcfc7c2e23b0faac3, but that mainline aggregate is not the smallest BIC. The reconstructable PR member eec5ed07521ffc767c0dd1bdccdece8a7f54fe3f first added the shared GET handler whose missing/inactive-token branch calls NewRunnerToken and added reachable organization and admin GET registration-token routes. Its immediate parent already classified GET as Read and contained neither the route nor the helper. The later member bba250f3e99bef12bbd9a1d9d790ab8155c999d5 extended the same mechanism to user and repository routes rather than originating it.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: An administrator or authenticated caller with connect-write authority can persist an attacker-chosen ConnectURL. The public GET /api/connects/info path, and later authenticated peer-health paths, append /api/connect and make an unrestricted server-side HTTP request to that stored URL. Because the request path lacks scheme, host, resolved-address, redirect, loopback, private-network, and link-local/cloud-metadata validation, the caller can cause Ech0 to reach internal services or metadata endpoints and return or infer their responses.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: fabee479ccf98c081bb065926c726b461a42fdf3 is the smallest real origin. Its parent-to-child patch directly adds publicRoutes.GET("/connects/info", controllers.GetConnectsInfo), a GetConnectsInfo loop over stored ConnectURL values, and pkg.SendRequest backed by an unconstrained http.Client.Do. The relevant diff contains direct modifications rather than a rename, import, move, or aggregate; later rewrites, relocations, health checks, and the fetchPeerConnectInfo extraction preserve the already-vulnerable operation.

causal_chain.bug_semantics: OracleIntegration's post-CREATE/post-UPDATE path performs a second SELECT by the driver-produced response.lastRowid. It directly interpolated the Oracle table name, obtained verbatim from user_tables.TABLE_NAME, between double quotes without doubling an embedded double quote. A crafted quoted table name can therefore terminate the identifier and inject SQL executed with the configured datasource user's privileges; response.lastRowid is not the injection vector.

Its direct parent has no lastRowid branch or ROWID SELECT. causal_chain.bug_semantics: Ech0 globally installed its i18n middleware and passed unauthenticated request-controlled locale values, including the raw Accept-Language header after only TrimSpace, to go-i18n and golang.org/x/text/language.ParseAcceptLanguage without a size or shape bound. The x/text CVE-2022-32149 mitigation counted '-' separators but the parser also aliases '_' to '-', so a near-1 MiB malformed underscore-separated value bypassed the guard and exercised quadratic parsing, allowing unauthenticated CPU denial of service on every route. X-Locale and the lang query parameter also reached the same unbounded parser through ResolveLocale.
causal_chain.flaw_origin: Commit b55edabd228d3de41e781bd3100f2e1ee0835516 first created Ech0's complete remotely reachable vulnerable path: it added internal/i18n/i18n.go, forwarded unbounded locale values to ParseAcceptLanguage and goi18n.NewLocalizer, read Accept-Language from the request, and registered the middleware globally. The parser weakness pre-existed in x/text, but the immediate parent did not contain Ech0's i18n parser path or global exposure.
